By pairing with CSS scroll-padding to account for floating on-screen keyboards and host top capsules, the mini-app provides flawless accessibility without jarring instantaneous viewport jumps.
key_takeaways: Scrolls ancestor containers to bring the target element into the visible viewport snapport
Accepts scrollIntoViewOptions controlling smooth animation and 2D block/inline alignment
Essential for form validation error targeting and accessibility focus management on mobile

title: Element.scrollTo() & CSS scroll-behavior: Deterministic Scroll Motion & Accessibility Overrides
standard_reference: W3C CSSOM View Module / Element scrollTo() & CSS scroll-behavior property
detail: [SPEC FACT] The scrollTo() method of Element and Window scrolls to a particular set of coordinates inside a given element. It accepts x/y coordinates or a ScrollToOptions dictionary containing left, top, and behavior ('auto', 'smooth', 'instant'). The CSS scroll-behavior property sets the default scrolling behavior for a scrolling box when navigation or CSSOM scrolling APIs are triggered. Crucially, the smooth scrolling animation MUST honor user preference media queries (@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)), falling back to 'instant'. [SUPERAPP IMPL] Super-app mini-apps implementing back-to-top buttons or deep-linked anchor navigation use scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'smooth' }). Super-app container baseline style rules automatically force 'scroll-behavior: auto !important' when the operating system indicates reduced-motion preference, shielding sensitive users from motion nausea while preserving fluid 60fps scrolling transitions for general audiences.
key_takeaways: Programmatically navigates scroll containers to explicit pixel coordinates via ScrollToOptions
CSS scroll-behavior defines default scrolling physics ('smooth' vs 'auto')
Must be conditionally overridden to 'instant' under prefers-reduced-motion to satisfy WCAG 2.2

title: W3C Web Audio API AudioWorklet & Off-Thread DSP Audio Processing Architecture
description: Standardizes off-thread low-latency audio synthesis, real-time filtering, and signal processing via AudioWorkletNode and AudioWorkletProcessor in Dedicated AudioWorkletGlobalScope without blocking main-thread UI rendering.
spec_anchor: W3C Web Audio API - Section 12 The AudioWorklet Interface
relevance: Super-app mini-apps incorporating interactive audio, casual gaming DSP, voice analysis, or synthesizer engines must process 128-sample audio quantum frames strictly within audio rendering threads to eliminate audible glitching and preserve sub-50ms INP responsiveness on the main thread.

normative: Mini-app containers must expose BaseAudioContext.audioWorklet returning an AudioWorklet instance that inherits from Worklet for off-thread script compilation.
Custom audio DSP modules must be loaded asynchronously via audioContext.audioWorklet.addModule(moduleURL) and execute strictly inside an AudioWorkletGlobalScope.
Audio processing units must subclass AudioWorkletProcessor, implement a process(inputs, outputs, parameters) method, and register via registerProcessor(name, processorCtor).
AudioWorkletProcessor.process() must return a boolean indicating whether the processor node should remain alive and continue receiving execution slices from the rendering engine.
AudioWorkletGlobalScope must strictly disallow access to synchronous DOM APIs, window, document, and blocking network operations to prevent high-priority audio underruns.
implementation_guidelines: Utilize audioWorklet.addModule() during mini-app initialization or splash screens to prevent audio pipeline latency during interactive execution.
Ensure AudioWorkletProcessor instances communicate with main-thread controllers exclusively via their paired MessagePort interface using structured cloning or Transferable ArrayBuffers.
Enforce a maximum quantum budget of 128 audio frames (approx 2.67ms at 48kHz) inside process() to guarantee glitch-free, real-time audio playback without buffer dropouts.
anti_patterns: Executing long-running synchronous loops or allocating memory repeatedly inside AudioWorkletProcessor.process(), triggering GC pauses and audible dropouts.
Attempting to capture user microphone streams directly in the main thread with legacy ScriptProcessorNode, which is deprecated, highly inefficient, and causes main-thread jank.

title: AudioWorkletNode & AudioWorkletProcessor Lifecycle and MessagePort IPC Arbitration
description: Establishes formal bidirectional IPC arbitration, parameter modulation, and resource lifecycle management between main-thread AudioWorkletNode and rendering-thread AudioWorkletProcessor.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - AudioWorkletNode API
relevance: Provides the essential control bridge for super-app host runtimes and mini-apps to orchestrate off-thread audio state machines, dynamic audio parameter ramping, and automated teardown upon navigation.

normative: AudioWorkletNode must be instantiated on the main thread with a reference to a registered processor name: new AudioWorkletNode(context, processorName, options).
AudioWorkletNode must expose a port property of type MessagePort to establish private bidirectional message communication with its paired processor instance.
AudioWorkletNode.parameters must expose an AudioParamMap containing all custom parameters declared statically in AudioWorkletProcessor.parameterDescriptors.
AudioWorkletNode must integrate seamlessly into the BaseAudioContext routing graph via standard connect() and disconnect() methods alongside native GainNode and PannerNode instances.
Closing the parent BaseAudioContext must immediately terminate all associated AudioWorkletProcessor instances and release underlying native audio threads.
implementation_guidelines: Declare custom AudioParam descriptors with explicit minValue, maxValue, and defaultValue to leverage native C++ audio parameter interpolation (k-rate and a-rate).
Use Transferable objects (ArrayBuffer) across AudioWorkletNode.port.postMessage() for bulk waveform or neural network audio weights to eliminate IPC copy overhead.
Explicitly call audioWorkletNode.disconnect() when disposing audio UI components to allow the host audio rendering engine to reclaim processor resources.
anti_patterns: Flooding the AudioWorkletNode.port with high-frequency control messages from requestAnimationFrame loops instead of utilizing AudioParam automation curves.
Failing to catch and handle promise rejections from audioWorklet.addModule(), leading to silent audio failures and broken mini-app initialization.

title: AudioWorkletGlobalScope Execution Boundary & Anti-Fingerprinting Sandboxing
description: Defines strict isolation boundaries, clock coarsening, and security constraints for AudioWorkletGlobalScope to prevent audio-based side-channel attacks and timing fingerprinting.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - AudioWorkletGlobalScope
relevance: Prevents malicious third-party mini-apps from exploiting high-precision audio rendering callbacks to measure CPU cache timing differences, exfiltrate sensitive data, or construct hardware fingerprints.

normative: AudioWorkletGlobalScope must operate in an isolated execution thread separate from both the DOM main thread and Dedicated Web Workers.
AudioWorkletGlobalScope.currentTime must report audio context timeline seconds coarsened in alignment with cross-origin isolation and timing attack mitigations.
AudioWorkletGlobalScope must expose currentFrame reflecting the continuous frame counter without exposing arbitrary high-resolution monotonic timestamps.
Mini-app containers must enforce strict script origin checks on modules loaded into AudioWorkletGlobalScope, disallowing untrusted third-party remote CDNs without manifest whitelisting.
Storage APIs (localStorage, IndexedDB) and network fetch primitives must be completely inaccessible within AudioWorkletGlobalScope.
implementation_guidelines: Host super-apps must package verified audio processor modules locally within signed mini-app archive packages (.zpk/.wgt) rather than dynamically fetching scripts at runtime.
Implement strict memory ceilings for AudioWorkletGlobalScope heaps (e.g., <= 16MB) to protect low-end mobile devices against memory exhaustion attacks.
Audit registered AudioWorkletProcessor implementations during automated store security scanning to detect crypto-mining or acoustic timing probing scripts.
anti_patterns: Allowing eval() or new Function() execution within AudioWorkletGlobalScope, violating store CSP wasm-unsafe-eval and script execution boundaries.
Permitting guest mini-apps to load arbitrary remote worklet scripts over insecure HTTP connections.

title: AudioParamMap & Native AudioParam Parameter Automation Governance
description: Standardizes high-precision hardware-accelerated parameter automation and parameter introspection for custom AudioWorkletNode instances.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - AudioParamMap
relevance: Enables mini-apps to modulate digital signal properties (volume sweeps, filter cutoff frequencies, pan positions) with sample-accurate scheduling without main-thread timer jitter.

normative: AudioWorkletNode.parameters must be an instance of AudioParamMap, providing a read-only Map-like interface (get, has, entries, keys, values).
Parameters declared in static parameterDescriptors must be reified as AudioParam objects with a-rate (sample-rate precision) or k-rate (quantum-rate precision) processing modes.
AudioParam automation methods (setValueAtTime, linearRampToValueAtTime, exponentialRampToValueAtTime, setTargetAtTime) must execute deterministically inside the audio thread.
Any parameter queried via audioWorkletNode.parameters.get(paramName) must throw TypeError if paramName does not exist in the registered processor specification.
Super-app host audio policies must cap the total number of simultaneous custom AudioParams per worklet to prevent scheduling complexity saturation.
implementation_guidelines: Specify automationRate: 'k-rate' for parameters that do not require per-sample fidelity (e.g., master volume, bypass toggles) to reduce DSP computation overhead by 128x.
Schedule audio parameter transitions using linearRampToValueAtTime() anchored to audioContext.currentTime rather than setting values inside JavaScript setInterval loops.
Sanitize custom parameter inputs to guarantee that infinite or NaN values are never passed to automation curves, which halts the audio engine.
anti_patterns: Attempting to manually write to AudioParamMap via standard Map.set(), which is read-only and will fail or throw errors in strict mode.
Scheduling thousands of simultaneous exponential ramps on low-end mobile hardware, saturating audio rendering threads.

title: Worklet.addModule() Lifecycle & Asynchronous Dependency Compilation
description: Governs the asynchronous fetching, compiling, and execution of worklet modules across Worklet execution scopes, including signal-based cancellation and CORS credentials.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Worklet.addModule()
relevance: Standardizes the compilation and registration pipeline for mini-app audio worklets, ensuring deterministic initialization, error resilience, and leak-free cancellation.

normative: Worklet.addModule(moduleURL, options) must return a Promise that resolves when the module script and its static dependencies have been fetched, compiled, and executed.
The options dictionary must support credentials ('same-origin', 'omit', 'include') to enforce strict access control on protected worklet resources.
Worklet.addModule must throw an AbortError DOMException if an AbortSignal passed via options.signal triggers cancellation before module compilation settles.
If script compilation or top-level execution within the WorkletGlobalScope fails, the returned Promise must reject with an informative Error object.
Modules must be imported as ECMAScript modules with strict MIME type enforcement ('text/javascript', 'application/javascript').
implementation_guidelines: Pass an AbortSignal tied to mini-app navigation lifecycle to cancel in-flight worklet downloads when users rapidly navigate away from audio-enabled pages.
Preload core worklet scripts using link rel='modulepreload' in the mini-app HTML shell to minimize cold-start delay before audio playback.
Ensure that worklet module URLs resolve to the mini-app local package origin to comply with strict super-app Content Security Policies.
anti_patterns: Calling Worklet.addModule() multiple times concurrently for the same script, generating redundant compilation threads and network fetches.
Attempting to catch worklet compilation errors inside the processor rather than handling the addModule() Promise rejection on the main thread.

title: W3C ReportingObserver API & In-Page Browser Diagnostic Telemetry
description: Standardizes in-page programmatic observation of browser platform violations, deprecations, intervention events, and crash reports via ReportingObserver.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - ReportingObserver
relevance: Allows super-app container runtimes and mini-app monitoring SDKs to capture client-side CSP violations, deprecation warnings, and browser interventions in real-time without relying solely on backend network reporting endpoints.

normative: ReportingObserver must be constructible via new ReportingObserver(callback, options) within window and worker contexts.
The observer callback must be invoked asynchronously with an array of Report objects and a reference to the observer instance.

The options dictionary must support 'types' (an array of report type strings such as 'deprecation', 'intervention', 'csp-violation') and 'buffered' (a boolean indicating whether past reports should be delivered).
Invoking observer.observe() must register the observer with the user agent's internal reporting buffer.
User agents must cap the in-memory reporting queue to prevent memory leaks from unbounded error accumulation.
implementation_guidelines: Instantiate a ReportingObserver early in mini-app bootstrap with { buffered: true } to capture critical boot-time deprecations and CSP violations.
Batch collected reports and flush them to super-app analytics backends during Page Visibility 'hidden' transitions via navigator.sendBeacon.
Filter benign browser deprecation warnings on the client to avoid polluting production error aggregation pipelines.
anti_patterns: Setting up multiple redundant ReportingObserver instances across individual UI components instead of using a single centralized observer.
Failing to disconnect the observer upon mini-app teardown, leaving active callbacks attached to discarded DOM documents.

title: ReportingObserver.observe() & Historical Buffered Telemetry Recovery
description: Governs the registration and buffered replay lifecycle of the ReportingObserver interface, enabling late-loaded monitoring agents to audit initial boot health.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - ReportingObserver.observe()
relevance: Ensures analytics SDKs loaded dynamically or lazily after initial page render can still inspect early startup CSP violations and deprecated API calls.

normative: ReportingObserver.prototype.observe() starts collecting reports according to the options configuration provided during instantiation.
When options.buffered is true, any matching reports generated before the observe() call was made must be queued and delivered in the first callback batch.
Calling observe() on an already observing instance must update or refresh the active observation state without clearing historical buffers unless explicitly specified.
The user agent must ensure buffered report delivery does not starve main-thread input handling or block frame rendering.
Store review automated validation tools must utilize buffered observation to detect deprecated API usage during headless automated test runs.
implementation_guidelines: Use buffered observation in automated staging environments to capture 100% of deprecation notices generated by third-party mini-app dependencies.
Correlate early boot reports with W3C Trace Context headers to trace initialization anomalies back to specific API gateway deployments.
Drain observer records promptly during splash screen transitions to avoid memory buildup on low-end mobile devices.
anti_patterns: Assuming unbuffered observation will capture early page-load CSP script rejections that occurred before SDK script execution.
Relying on synchronous exception handlers (window.onerror) to capture deprecation notices, which are exclusively emitted via ReportingObserver.

title: ReportingObserver.takeRecords() & Synchronous Queue Drainage Lifecycle
description: Standardizes synchronous extraction of queued diagnostic reports via takeRecords() and deterministic resource reclamation via disconnect().
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - ReportingObserver.takeRecords()
relevance: Enables super-app container runtimes to flush pending diagnostic reports immediately before container destruction, app suspension, or route transitions.

normative: ReportingObserver.prototype.takeRecords() must return a sequence of all pending Report objects in the queue and immediately empty the queue.
Reports returned by takeRecords() must not be delivered to the observer's callback, preventing duplicate report processing.
ReportingObserver.prototype.disconnect() must immediately stop the observer from receiving reports and detach it from the platform reporting service.
Calling takeRecords() on a disconnected observer must return any remaining buffered records accumulated prior to disconnection.
Host super-apps must invoke takeRecords() during pagehide / visibilitychange events to guarantee telemetry transmission before OS process eviction.
implementation_guidelines: Combine takeRecords() with fetch(..., { keepalive: true }) inside visibilitychange event handlers to reliably send pending reports without blocking navigation.
Always call observer.disconnect() when unmounting micro-frontends or guest mini-apps to prevent memory leaks in single-page super-app shells.
Check the length of takeRecords() output; if empty, avoid dispatching unnecessary network telemetry requests.
anti_patterns: Ignoring takeRecords() during app unmount, resulting in lost diagnostics for crashes or CSP failures occurring immediately before user exit.
Reusing a disconnected observer without re-invoking observe(), leading to complete loss of subsequent diagnostic telemetry.

title: W3C Report Interface & Diagnostic Payload Object Model
description: Defines the formal schema, properties, and JSON serialization format for platform diagnostic reports delivered to ReportingObserver.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Report Interface
relevance: Standardizes the data structure consumed by super-app telemetry ingestion pipelines, ensuring consistent schema normalization across heterogeneous webview engines.

normative: Each report delivered via the reporting service must implement the Report interface, exposing readonly attributes 'type', 'url', and 'body'.
Report.type must be a DOMString identifying the report variety (e.g., 'deprecation', 'intervention', 'csp-violation').
Report.url must be a DOMString reflecting the address of the document or worker where the reported event occurred.
Report.body must return an instance of ReportBody specific to the report type, providing structured details (e.g., sourceFile, lineNumber, id, message).
Report instances must implement toJSON() serialization to facilitate zero-overhead JSON serialization for network transit.
implementation_guidelines: Normalize Report objects into OpenTelemetry-compatible event spans before forwarding to central enterprise observability collectors.
Sanitize Report.url query parameters to eliminate sensitive authentication tokens, session cookies, or PII before network dispatch.
Index reports by Report.type in client-side log aggregation to route security violations immediately to security operations centers (SOC).
anti_patterns: Assuming Report.body is always a flat key-value string dictionary rather than a polymorphic ReportBody subclass.
Attempting to mutate Report attributes directly, which are read-only and will throw errors in strict mode.

title: ReportBody Polymorphic Schemas & CSP/Deprecation Violation Payloads
description: Governs the specialized payload properties exposed across distinct ReportBody subclasses (CSPViolationReportBody, DeprecationReportBody, InterventionReportBody).
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Report.body
relevance: Enables automated store review linters and runtime security agents to parse fine-grained violation details, such as blocked-uri, violatedDirective, and effectiveDirective.

normative: When Report.type is 'csp-violation', Report.body must expose CSPViolationReportBody attributes including blockedURL, disposition, documentURL, effectiveDirective, originalPolicy, and statusCode.
When Report.type is 'deprecation', Report.body must expose DeprecationReportBody attributes including id, anticipatedRemoval (Date or null), and message.
When Report.type is 'intervention', Report.body must expose InterventionReportBody detailing the user agent policy action taken (e.g., throttling heavy CPU timers, blocking autoplay).
Sensitive origin credentials in blockedURL and documentURL must be stripped or redacted in accordance with referrer policies.
Automated compliance review systems must fail store certification if high-severity CSP violation reports are generated during smoke testing.
implementation_guidelines: Map CSPViolationReportBody.effectiveDirective directly to security audit checklists during mini-app store validation.
Track DeprecationReportBody.anticipatedRemoval timestamps in CI pipelines to alert developers well in advance of upcoming browser engine breaking changes.
Log InterventionReportBody occurrences to detect user experience degradations caused by aggressive browser background battery throttling.
anti_patterns: Treating all report types with a single generic error handler, missing critical security distinctions between CSP attacks and benign deprecations.
Failing to capture lineNumber and columnNumber from ReportBody when debugging third-party mini-app script failures.

title: W3C VirtualKeyboard API & OverlaysContent Layout Decoupling
description: Standardizes programmatic control over on-screen virtual keyboard behavior via navigator.virtualKeyboard, allowing mini-apps to decouple viewport resizing from keyboard emergence.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - VirtualKeyboard API
relevance: Critical for conversational mini-apps, chat interfaces, checkout payment sheets, and POS terminals hosted in super-apps, preventing sudden destructive viewport resizing when soft keyboards pop up.

normative: The VirtualKeyboard interface must be accessible via navigator.virtualKeyboard within Secure Contexts on touch-enabled mobile devices.
Setting navigator.virtualKeyboard.overlaysContent = true must prevent the user agent from automatically resizing the document viewport when the virtual keyboard appears.
When overlaysContent is true, the virtual keyboard must render as an overlay above document content, allowing the mini-app to adjust layout using CSS env() variables.
The host container must expose CSS environment variables keyboard-inset-top, keyboard-inset-right, keyboard-inset-bottom, and keyboard-inset-left representing keyboard geometry.
User agents must disallow virtualKeyboard manipulation from insecure cross-origin iframes without explicit Permissions Policy delegation.
implementation_guidelines: Enable navigator.virtualKeyboard.overlaysContent = true in fixed-position chat and checkout bottom bars to eliminate jarring keyboard jump jank.
Use CSS padding-bottom: env(keyboard-inset-bottom, 0px) to smoothly anchor action buttons directly above the emergent keyboard.
Feature-detect 'virtualKeyboard' in navigator before invoking methods to maintain graceful degradation on desktop platforms.
anti_patterns: Relying on window.innerHeight resize polling loops to detect virtual keyboard emergence, which causes heavy main-thread layout thrashing.
Setting overlaysContent = true without handling keyboard-inset-bottom in CSS, resulting in form inputs being completely obscured behind the keyboard.

title: VirtualKeyboard.boundingRect & High-Precision Occlusion Geometry
description: Provides real-time DOMRect dimensions of the visible virtual keyboard, enabling precision coordinate calculation for floating action buttons and toolbars.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - VirtualKeyboard.boundingRect
relevance: Enables super-app security capsule controls and mini-app floating elements to accurately calculate occlusion boundaries and avoid overlapping interactive controls.

normative: navigator.virtualKeyboard.boundingRect must return a DOMRectReadOnly object representing the exact size and position of the virtual keyboard.
When the virtual keyboard is hidden or occluded, all attributes of boundingRect (x, y, width, height) must report 0.
The coordinates returned must be expressed in CSS pixels relative to the client visual viewport bounds.
Changes in keyboard geometry (e.g., switching input languages, opening voice dictation trays, floating keyboard mode) must update boundingRect immediately.
Host super-apps must verify that mini-app security prompts (e.g., PIN pad confirmation) remain fully unobscured by boundingRect coordinates.
implementation_guidelines: Query virtualKeyboard.boundingRect within geometrychange handlers to determine whether custom modal sheets require vertical offset translation.
Check boundingRect.height > 0 to reliably detect keyboard visibility state without guessing based on window focus events.
Integrate boundingRect calculations with Canvas 2D or WebGL rendering viewports to adjust active camera frustums during text input.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding assumed mobile keyboard heights (e.g., 250px or 300px), which fails across varying Android OEM devices and dynamic IME docks.
Caching boundingRect across sessions instead of querying the live DOMRect property upon geometrychange events.

title: VirtualKeyboard 'geometrychange' Event & Compositor Animation Sync
description: Governs the asynchronous dispatch of geometrychange events when the virtual keyboard emerges, dismisses, or dynamically shifts dimensions.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - VirtualKeyboard: geometrychange event
relevance: Synchronizes mini-app UI repositioning with native OS keyboard transitions, maintaining sub-16ms frame rendering and fluid visual continuity.

normative: The virtualKeyboard object must fire a 'geometrychange' event whenever the keyboard appears, disappears, or changes height/width.
The geometrychange event must inherit from Event, be untrusted, and must not bubble or be cancelable.
User agents must dispatch geometrychange promptly following OS window manager inset updates.
Event listeners added via navigator.virtualKeyboard.addEventListener('geometrychange', handler) must execute within normal event loop task cycles.
Containers must throttle or coalesce rapid keyboard height oscillations during continuous typing or suggestion bar mutations.
implementation_guidelines: Debounce heavy UI recalculations inside geometrychange event handlers or schedule updates via requestAnimationFrame.
Animate floating toolbars upward using CSS transforms (transform: translateY(...)) synchronized with keyboard height transitions.
Remove geometrychange listeners upon mini-app page unmount to prevent memory leaks.
anti_patterns: Performing synchronous DOM layout mutations inside geometrychange handlers without batching, triggering forced reflow bottlenecks.
Assuming geometrychange fires only when keyboard opens, ignoring dismissal events where height collapses back to zero.

title: VirtualKeyboard.show() & hide() Programmatic Focus Orchestration
description: Standardizes imperative programmatic display and dismissal of the virtual keyboard independent of immediate DOM element focus.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - VirtualKeyboard.show()
relevance: Allows mini-apps utilizing custom canvas-based editors, code editors, or specialized input widgets (e.g., rich text or custom calculators) to control OS keyboard visibility smoothly.

normative: navigator.virtualKeyboard.show() must imperatively display the virtual keyboard provided a focusable element has focus or transient user activation is present.
navigator.virtualKeyboard.hide() must dismiss the virtual keyboard regardless of whether an editable element currently retains focus.
Calling show() or hide() must not change the currently focused DOM element unless handled explicitly by application logic.
If the device has a physical hardware keyboard attached and soft keyboards are disabled by the OS, show() must be a graceful no-op.
Super-app security sandboxes must prevent background or hidden mini-apps from calling show(), which could disorient the user.
implementation_guidelines: Call virtualKeyboard.hide() upon successful form submission or message dispatch to immediately return screen real estate to the user.
Combine virtualKeyboard.show() with custom virtualized text input elements (EditContext API) to build high-performance canvas editors.
Provide visible dismiss buttons on custom input bars that invoke virtualKeyboard.hide().
anti_patterns: Calling virtualKeyboard.show() continuously in a loop when a user attempts to dismiss the keyboard, creating an inescapable keyboard trap.
Relying on blurring an input element (input.blur()) to dismiss the keyboard, which can disrupt accessibility focus hierarchies.

title: Super-App Container VirtualKeyboard Security & Permissions Sandboxing
description: Establishes container-level security boundaries, anti-spoofing policies, and store review criteria for the VirtualKeyboard API.
evidence_level: Platform Implementation Standard / Store Compliance Gate
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Navigator: virtualKeyboard property
relevance: Protects users against malicious overlay attacks, phishing sheets mimicking system dialogs, and deceptive layout shifts in multi-tenant super-app environments.

normative: Mini-app containers must sandbox virtual keyboard insets so that third-party guest apps cannot spoof native super-app payment authorization dialogues.
When overlaysContent is enabled, host super-apps must ensure that persistent security capsules (e.g., close app, permissions indicator) retain higher z-index dominance.
Automated store review gates must audit mini-app use of virtualKeyboard.show() to verify it is bound to valid interactive user workflows.
Embedded cross-origin third-party widgets must be blocked from modifying overlaysContent unless specifically granted via permissions policy.
Container runtimes must automatically invoke virtualKeyboard.hide() whenever a critical host dialog (e.g., biometric auth, transaction confirmation) is invoked.
implementation_guidelines: Audit mini-apps in staging webviews using automated headless scripts that verify host navigation buttons remain clickable when virtual keyboard is open.
Log instances of unexpected virtual keyboard geometry mutations in store diagnostics to catch layout regressions.
Include standard test cases for both split-screen tablet modes and portrait mobile orientations during store submission reviews.
anti_patterns: Permitting guest mini-apps to obscure super-app security capsule controls by abusing negative margins with keyboard-inset-bottom.
Failing to dismiss the virtual keyboard when navigating between completely different mini-apps within the super-app shell.

title: IETF RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics & Method Idempotency and Safety Governance
description: Standardizes HTTP method classification into safe (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE) and idempotent (GET, HEAD, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS, TRACE) operations, defining explicit state-mutation boundaries and caching semantics for super-app API gateways.
evidence_level: IETF Proposed Standard / Internet Standard RFC 9110
spec_anchor: RFC 9110 - Section 9.2 Safe Methods & Section 9.3 Idempotent Methods
relevance: Super-app mini-apps invoking microservices and financial transaction APIs must adhere strictly to safe and idempotent HTTP semantics, ensuring automated retries over unreliable cellular networks do not cause duplicate order creation or unauthorized debiting.

normative: Mini-app client containers and gateway proxies must treat GET, HEAD, and OPTIONS methods as strictly safe, ensuring request execution causes no server-side state mutation.

Safe methods and idempotent mutation methods (PUT, DELETE) must be automatically retryable by client-side networking libraries upon TCP reset, timeout, or network transition without prompting user intervention.
Non-idempotent operations (POST, PATCH) must NOT be replayed automatically upon network failures unless accompanied by an Idempotency-Key header or mutual transaction token.

Client-side caching layers in super-app runtimes must invalidate cached representations of an effective request URI whenever an unsafe request (POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) returns a successful (2xx/3xx) response.
Status codes returned to mini-apps must conform to standard classes: 1xx Informational, 2xx Successful, 3xx Redirection, 4xx Client Error, and 5xx Server Error.
implementation_guidelines: Enforce mandatory Idempotency-Key header injection on all financial checkout and order submission POST endpoints within the mini-app SDK networking bridge.
Reject requests where GET or HEAD payloads contain unexpected body payloads at the gateway layer to prevent HTTP request smuggling.
Configure client-side fetch adapters to treat 4xx status responses as non-retryable logical application errors and 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After headers as gracefully throttled.
anti_patterns: Using GET requests with query parameters to execute destructive state mutations (e.g. GET /api/v1/orders/cancel?id=123), breaking browser prefetching and web proxy safety.
Blindly re-transmitting failed POST payment requests upon network timeout, risking duplicate charges and ledger discrepancies.

title: RFC 9110 Conditional Requests, ETag Validators & Content Negotiation
description: Defines preconditions, entity tags (strong vs weak ETags), conditional headers (If-Match, If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since), and proactive content negotiation (Accept, Accept-Encoding) for efficient mini-app asset delivery.
evidence_level: IETF Proposed Standard / Internet Standard RFC 9110
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - An overview of HTTP & RFC 9110 Section 13 Conditional Requests
relevance: Enables super-app runtime package distribution systems and API gateways to validate local cache freshness with 304 Not Modified responses, drastically reducing bandwidth and launch latency on 3G/4G networks.

normative: Package manifests and static assets distributed by super-app CDNs must provide strong ETag validators or Last-Modified timestamps for fine-grained cache validation.
Client networking layers must automatically synthesize conditional request headers (If-None-Match with stored ETag, If-Modified-Since) when revalidating stale cached assets.
Gateways must respond with HTTP 304 Not Modified without a message body when conditional revalidation succeeds, instructing the client container to refresh local cache TTL.
Transactional modification endpoints must support optimistic concurrency control via If-Match headers, returning HTTP 412 Precondition Failed upon mid-air collision.
Proactive content negotiation must leverage standard Accept, Accept-Encoding (br, zstd, gzip), and Accept-Language headers conforming to BCP 47 language tags.
implementation_guidelines: Implement strong cryptographic hash-based ETags (SHA-256) on mini-app bundle chunks (.zpk) to enable instant byte-level verification.
Utilize If-Match: "<version-etag>" for concurrent resource editing in collaborative or multi-device mini-apps to eliminate silent overwrite race conditions.
Ensure client webviews preserve Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br, zstd headers to maximize network payload compression.
anti_patterns: Relying solely on crude Cache-Control: max-age without ETag validators, forcing full bundle re-downloads when caches expire.
Stripping ETag and Last-Modified headers at intermediary edge proxies, completely breaking conditional revalidation.

title: IETF RFC 9113 HTTP/2 Binary Framing, Stream Multiplexing & Flow Control
description: Standardizes the binary framing layer, independent bidirectional stream multiplexing over a single TCP connection, priority signaling, and credit-based flow control (WINDOW_UPDATE).
evidence_level: IETF Proposed Standard / Internet Standard RFC 9113
spec_anchor: RFC 9113 - Section 4 HTTP/2 Frames & Section 5 Streams and Multiplexing
relevance: Eliminates HTTP/1.1 head-of-line blocking for subresource fetching, enabling mini-apps to concurrently download split code bundles, WebAssembly modules, fonts, and API responses over a single shared connection.

normative: All super-app client runtimes and CDN edge gateways must negotiate HTTP/2 via TLS Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) using the protocol identifier 'h2'.
Connections must operate over a binary framing architecture supporting standard frame types: DATA, HEADERS, PRIORITY, RST_STREAM, SETTINGS, PUSH_PROMISE, PING, GOAWAY, and WINDOW_UPDATE.
Streams must be concurrently multiplexed over a single TCP connection without serialization delays, transitioning through states: idle, reserved, open, half-closed, and closed.
Endpoints must respect SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS to prevent resource starvation, defaulting to a minimum of 100 concurrent active streams.
Flow control must be enforced per stream and for the connection overall using WINDOW_UPDATE frames to prevent faster senders from overwhelming receiver buffers.
implementation_guidelines: Configure edge gateways to maintain persistent warm HTTP/2 connections per active mini-app to eliminate repeated TLS handshake latencies.
Use RST_STREAM with error code CANCEL (0x8) when user navigates away or cancels a pending image/data request, instantly halting in-flight byte transmission.
Tune stream buffer allocations on mobile clients to prevent out-of-memory crashes during heavy burst downloads.
anti_patterns: Domain sharding across multiple subdomains in HTTP/2 environments, which fragments TCP connections and degrades HPACK compression efficiency.
Disabling flow control or ignoring WINDOW_UPDATE frames, resulting in buffer overflows and abrupt socket termination.

title: RFC 7541 HPACK Header Compression & State Memory Sandboxing
description: Specifies HPACK header compression format for HTTP/2, combining a static table of 61 predefined entries, an evicting dynamic table, and canonical Huffman encoding while mitigating CRIME-style compression attacks.
spec_anchor: RFC 7541 - Section 2 Compression Process Overview & Section 7 Security Considerations
relevance: Reduces HTTP header transmission overhead from hundreds of bytes to single-digit bytes for repetitive mini-app API calls while safeguarding authorization tokens and session cookies against side-channel decompression attacks.

normative: HTTP/2 endpoints must maintain synchronized encoding and decoding contexts consisting of the static table (61 indices) and an eviction-managed dynamic table.
The dynamic table size must be bounded by SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE advertised in SETTINGS frames (default 4096 octets), strictly enforcing FIFO eviction upon overflow.
Header fields containing high-entropy secrets (Authorization bearer tokens, Set-Cookie, API keys) must be encoded as Literal Header Field Never Indexed to prevent dynamic table exfiltration.
Decompressors must validate integer and Huffman encodings, immediately terminating the connection with COMPRESSION_ERROR (0x9) upon parsing malformed bit sequences.
Dynamic table size updates must be acknowledged within the frame sequence and cannot exceed the maximum buffer ceiling negotiated during connection setup.
implementation_guidelines: Instruct mini-app networking SDKs to mark Authorization headers with the never-indexed flag (RFC 7541 index representation type 0001xxxx).
Leverage static table entries for recurring pseudo-headers (:method GET/POST, :scheme https, :path /) to achieve 1-byte header representations.
Monitor dynamic table memory utilization on embedded mobile containers to enforce strict per-webview memory quotas.
anti_patterns: Indexing sensitive bearer tokens or session credentials in the HPACK dynamic table where compression ratio side-channels could reveal token prefixes.
Allocating unbounded dynamic table sizes on backend proxies, exposing gateways to memory exhaustion Denial-of-Service attacks.

title: Super-App Gateway HTTP/2 Rapid Reset & Smuggling Defense Governance
description: Establishes gateway-level mitigation policies against HTTP/2 RST_STREAM rapid reset abuse (CVE-2023-44487), stream concurrency flooding, and HTTP request smuggling between super-app edge gateways and internal microservices.
evidence_level: IETF / Industry Security Standard & OWASP API Security
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - HTTP request methods & CVE-2023-44487 Security Mitigations
relevance: Protects the super-app platform infrastructure from distributed denial-of-service attacks orchestrated by rogue mini-apps or compromised third-party clients rapidly opening and resetting HTTP/2 streams.

normative: Super-app API gateways must implement strict rate-limiting and anomaly detection on incoming RST_STREAM frame frequencies per connection.

If a client connection exceeds the rapid reset threshold (e.g. > 100 resets per second with low data exchange), the gateway must issue a GOAWAY frame with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM (0xb) and terminate the TCP socket.

Gateways translating HTTP/2 requests to backend HTTP/1.1 connections must normalize header casing, forbid duplicate Content-Length headers, and strip conflicting Transfer-Encoding headers to prevent request smuggling.
Mini-app store submission pipelines must conduct static code analysis on third-party SDK networking dependencies to detect aggressive polling or stream reset loops.
Edge gateways must enforce maximum connection lifespans and graceful GOAWAY draining during container scale-down and rolling deployments.
implementation_guidelines: Configure edge reverse proxies (Envoy, NGINX, HAProxy) with http2_max_concurrent_streams = 128 and strict reset rate limiters.
Standardize error reporting for throttled mini-apps using RFC 9457 Problem Details with type 'urn:ietf:rfc:9113:enhance-your-calm'.
Conduct automated regression testing for HTTP/2 downgrade smuggling vulnerabilities on all external-facing super-app microgateway routes.
anti_patterns: Allowing unrestricted RST_STREAM processing without tracking stream lifecycle costs, permitting attackers to exhaust server CPU and file descriptors.
Blindly forwarding malformed pseudo-headers (:authority, :path) into internal backend microservices without strict sanitization.

title: W3C Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG 2) Runtime Integration & DOM Sandboxing
description: Standardizes declarative 2D vector graphics representation, DOM element hierarchy (<svg>, <path>, <g>, <defs>, <symbol>), CSS styling integration, and responsive viewBox scaling within super-app mini-app runtimes.
spec_anchor: W3C SVG 2 - Section 2 Concepts & Section 5 Document Structure
relevance: Mini-apps extensively utilize SVG for scalable vector icons, resolution-independent illustration assets, interactive maps, and micro-charts across diverse mobile device pixel densities (1x to 4x DPR).

normative: Mini-app webview containers must support native SVG 2 rendering including geometry elements (<path>, <rect>, <circle>, <polygon>), structural elements (<g>, <defs>, <symbol>), and gradient/pattern paints.
Responsive vector scaling must be declared via the viewBox attribute with preserveAspectRatio controls, ensuring assets scale proportionally without pixelation across varying screen aspect ratios.
CSS properties applied to SVG elements (fill, stroke, stroke-width, transform, opacity) must participate in standard CSS cascading, @layer styling, and CSS custom property (variables) inheritance.
Inline SVG elements embedded directly in HTML documents must integrate into the document DOM tree, exposing standard SVGElement DOM interfaces and event listeners.
Stand-alone SVG image assets loaded via HTML tags or CSS background-image must execute in static mode, strictly disabling DOM manipulation and external network resource loading.
implementation_guidelines: Adopt <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"> as the baseline convention for all mini-app navigation and UI action icons to standardize sizing.
Use CSS variables for themeable fills (e.g. fill: var(--superapp-brand-color, #1890ff)) to enable instant dark mode and theme switching.
Consolidate recurring icons into SVG sprite sheets using <defs> and <symbol> to minimize DOM element overhead and memory consumption.
anti_patterns: Hardcoding fixed pixel width and height on root <svg> elements without viewBox, causing clipped layouts and blurred scaling on high-DPI displays.
Using raster PNGs or massive uncompressed SVGs for simple geometric icons, inflating package bundle size and slowing initial render.

title: SVG Active Script Execution Boundaries & Vector XSS Defense
description: Defines strict execution boundaries and sanitization policies for SVG vector assets, eliminating active script execution vectors (<script>, inline event handlers, javascript: URIs) in super-app environments.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs & OWASP Security Standard
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics & Security Considerations
relevance: SVG documents can contain executable JavaScript and event listeners. If untrusted SVG files (e.g. user avatars, merchant logos, dynamically generated QR codes) are rendered inline, they can execute arbitrary scripts with full mini-app privileges.

normative: Super-app runtimes must enforce strict isolation on SVG assets: SVG files loaded as images (, CSS background) must never execute scripts or evaluate external stylesheet links.

User-generated or dynamically imported SVG content rendered inline must undergo deterministic sanitization stripping all <script> elements, inline event handler attributes (onload, onerror, onclick), and javascript: URIs.
Mini-app Content Security Policy (CSP) must enforce default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline' on any isolated SVG browsing contexts or iframes hosting standalone vector documents.
The container must block navigation triggered from SVG <a> elements that specify dangerous scheme protocols (javascript:, data:text/html, vbscript:).
XML parser configuration in backend ingestion gateways must disable Document Type Definitions (DTDs) and external entity resolution (XXE defense).
implementation_guidelines: Always render third-party or user-supplied SVG assets using HTML elements or CSS masks rather than inline innerHTML injection.
Integrate robust DOMPurify or W3C HTML Sanitizer policies configured to sanitize SVG namespaces before mounting into DOM trees.
Reject SVG uploads that contain XML entity declarations (&entity;) or external system identifiers during store packaging and API upload.
anti_patterns: Directly assigning unsanitized SVG strings received from remote APIs to element.innerHTML, exposing the mini-app to trivial Stored XSS.
Serving user-uploaded SVGs with Content-Type: image/svg+xml without Content-Disposition: attachment or restrictive sandbox headers.

title: W3C SVG 2 <foreignObject> Sandboxing & Nested HTML Injection Mitigation
description: Establishes container sandboxing rules for the SVG <foreignObject> element, mitigating nested HTML/XHTML injection, DOM clobbering, and CSS exfiltration attacks.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - <foreignObject> SVG Element & W3C SVG 2 Section 10 Embedded Content
relevance: The <foreignObject> element allows embedding arbitrary HTML content (such as <div>, <form>, <iframe>, <input>) inside an SVG document, creating complex parser-mutation vulnerabilities and clickjacking overlays if not strictly regulated.

normative: Super-app mini-app store linters must reject or flag SVG assets containing <foreignObject> elements intended for untrusted icon/illustration distribution.
When <foreignObject> is utilized in first-party mini-apps for complex rich text or chart annotations, all child HTML elements must conform strictly to the host mini-app CSP.
Container webview layout engines must isolate <foreignObject> rendering to prevent nested HTML from overflowing parent SVG viewports or obscuring native host UI controls.
Interactive form inputs (<input>, <textarea>, <button>) placed inside <foreignObject> must not intercept touch gestures reserved for container navigation or modal dismissal.
Dynamic HTML insertion into <foreignObject> must require Trusted Types (TrustedHTML) when CSP require-trusted-types-for 'script' is active.
implementation_guidelines: Prefer standard SVG <text>, <tspan>, and textPath elements over <foreignObject> for rendering vector typography and labels.
Strip <foreignObject> completely during client-side SVG sanitization pipelines for all non-privileged mini-app components.
Verify coordinate clamping on <foreignObject> (x, y, width, height) to prevent full-screen transparent clickjacking overlays.
anti_patterns: Using <foreignObject> to embed external <iframe> elements within an SVG, bypassing standard iframe sandboxing controls.
Allowing unvalidated markdown-to-HTML parsers to output raw SVG <foreignObject> constructs into user comment threads.

title: W3C SVG 2 <use> Element Shadow Tree & Cross-Origin Fragment Boundaries
description: Standardizes the instantiation of re-usable SVG graphics via the <use href="..."> element, governing closed Shadow Tree cloning, cross-origin fragment fetching, and resource exhaustion limits.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - <use> SVG Element & W3C SVG 2 Section 5.6 The use element
relevance: The <use> element enables high-performance vector symbol re-use across mini-app views, but nested or recursive <use> elements can trigger catastrophic CPU exhaustion (Billion Laughs / SVG quadratic blowup).

normative: The <use> element must clone target elements into an encapsulated, closed shadow tree associated with the use element instance.

References declared via href (or legacy xlink:href) must resolve to same-origin SVG documents or pre-loaded document fragments; cross-origin fetches must require valid CORS headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin).
Runtimes must enforce strict cycle detection and maximum recursion depth limits (e.g. max depth <= 16) on chained <use> references to prevent infinite loop crashes.
CSS cascading into the <use> shadow tree must respect property inheritance (color, fill, stroke) while preventing shadow tree styles from leaking into outer document scope.
Store packaging validation must verify that all <use href="#symbol-id"> targets resolve to valid declared symbols within the mini-app package.
implementation_guidelines: Reference local document fragments (<use href="#icon-check">) rather than external file paths to ensure instant rendering without network roundtrips.
Avoid deep nesting of <use> elements (e.g. <use> referencing another <g> containing <use>), keeping symbol structures flat.
Audit SVG sprites during build-time CI to purge unused <symbol> definitions, reducing bundle size.
anti_patterns: Creating circular references where symbol A uses symbol B which references symbol A, causing webview renderer thread hangs.
Loading cross-origin SVG fragments over unauthenticated HTTP connections, exposing the mini-app to Man-in-the-Middle asset tampering.

title: OWASP DOM-Based XSS Prevention & Vector Asset Store Gating
description: Establishes comprehensive store submission rules, runtime DOM sanitization requirements, and CI/CD security gating for SVG assets and vector rendering pipelines.
spec_anchor: OWASP Cheat Sheet Series - DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet
relevance: Provides the definitive security checklist and automated review criteria for super-app store operators to certify that mini-apps handling rich text and vector graphics are immune to DOM-based XSS attacks.

normative: Mini-app store submission verification must incorporate automated static security analysis (SAST) scanning all packaged .svg files and inline vector templates for dangerous tags and attributes.
Assets containing <script>, <style> with expression/behavior, <animate> with arbitrary attribute injection, or inline event handlers must trigger automated store submission rejection.
Mini-apps accepting dynamic user SVG input must demonstrate use of context-aware HTML/SVG sanitization libraries (e.g. DOMPurify with USE_PROFILES: {svg: true, svgFilters: false}).
Super-app developer frameworks must provide safe vector rendering components (e.g. <super-icon name="..." />) that abstract away raw innerHTML and vector parsing.
All vector assets hosted on super-app storage gateways must be delivered with Content-Type: image/svg+xml and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'.
implementation_guidelines: Incorporate svgo (SVG Optimizer) and DOMPurify into the standard mini-app CLI build pipeline to strip comments, metadata, and scripts automatically.
Log all client-side sanitization interventions via the super-app security telemetry bridge to detect active exploitation attempts.
Establish explicit store guidelines documenting permitted SVG subsets for mini-app publisher submissions.
anti_patterns: Relying on naive regular expression blacklists (e.g. stripping '<script>') to sanitize SVG, easily bypassed via uppercase variations, XML entities, or event attributes.
Allowing unvetted third-party mini-apps to load dynamic SVG strings directly from arbitrary untrusted external CDN URLs.

title: W3C Media Source Extensions (MSE) v2 & DedicatedWorker Pipeline Offloading
description: Standardizes the execution of MediaSource and SourceBuffer operations inside DedicatedWorker execution contexts, decoupling CPU-intensive segment fetching, container demuxing, and buffer appending from the main UI thread.
evidence_level: W3C Working Draft / Candidate Recommendation MSE v2
spec_anchor: W3C Media Source Extensions v2 - Section 2 MediaSource in Workers
relevance: High-throughput video streaming, live commerce broadcasting, and interactive audio in super-app mini-apps can cause severe main-thread UI jank and touch input latency (INP degradation) if segment parsing and buffer appending occur on the main thread.

normative: Mini-app container runtimes must support MediaSource instantiation and lifecycle management within DedicatedWorker contexts.
The static property MediaSource.canConstructInDedicatedWorker must be exposed and return true to enable feature detection before spawning worker pipelines.
SourceBuffer instances created in DedicatedWorker contexts must process appendBuffer() and remove() operations asynchronously without blocking the worker or main UI event loops.
The worker context must maintain full access to Fetch API, Streams API, and WebAssembly to allow custom demuxers (e.g. fMP4, CMAF, TS, WebM) to feed SourceBuffers directly off-thread.
Terminating the worker or revoking the media source must trigger deterministic teardown of all allocated native media decoding queues and hardware buffers.
implementation_guidelines: Offload adaptive bitrate (ABR) algorithm calculations and HTTP chunk fetching completely into the media DedicatedWorker.
Stream fetched ArrayBuffer chunks directly into SourceBuffer.appendBuffer() using BYOB (Bring-Your-Own-Buffer) readers to minimize garbage collection churn.
Gracefully fall back to main-thread MSE only when running on legacy container webview versions where canConstructInDedicatedWorker is false.
anti_patterns: Executing heavy WebAssembly video demuxers on the main JavaScript thread, locking the UI thread for 100-300ms during video segment boundaries.
Transferring multi-megabyte ArrayBuffers back and forth between worker and main thread via structured cloning instead of passing the MediaSourceHandle.

title: MediaSource.handle & HTMLMediaElement srcObject Off-Thread Binding
description: Establishes standard cross-context binding of worker-based MediaSource instances to main-thread <video> or <audio> elements via the opaque transferable MediaSourceHandle interface and HTMLMediaElement.srcObject.
evidence_level: W3C Working Draft / MDN Authoritative Standard
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - MediaSource.handle Property & W3C MSE v2
relevance: Provides the essential, zero-copy architectural bridge allowing background worker threads to produce and feed media streams directly into native platform video decoders rendered on the UI thread.

normative: MediaSource instances created in DedicatedWorker contexts must expose a handle property returning a unique, opaque MediaSourceHandle object.
MediaSourceHandle must implement the Transferable interface, permitting zero-copy delegation across postMessage boundaries to the main window thread.
Main-thread HTMLMediaElement (<video>, <audio>) must accept MediaSourceHandle assignment directly to the srcObject property.
Assigning a MediaSourceHandle to srcObject must establish an internal control pipe and transition the MediaSource.readyState to 'open', firing the 'sourceopen' event inside the worker thread.
Once transferred, the MediaSourceHandle cannot be re-transferred or reassigned to multiple media elements concurrently.
implementation_guidelines: Transfer the MediaSourceHandle immediately upon worker initialization in the second argument array of worker.postMessage({ handle }, [handle]).
Set videoElement.srcObject = message.data.handle and await playback readiness via standard HTMLMediaElement 'canplay' or 'loadedmetadata' events.
Nullify videoElement.srcObject when exiting the video viewing context to signal the worker pipeline to close SourceBuffers.
anti_patterns: Attempting to generate an object URL (URL.createObjectURL) from a worker-instantiated MediaSource, which is invalid, deprecated, and fails in modern webview engines.
Passing raw decoded PCM or video pixel arrays across postMessage for video playback instead of utilizing the native MediaSourceHandle pipe.

title: MediaSourceHandle Interface Lifecycle & Concurrency Arbitration
description: Standardizes the MediaSourceHandle interface specification, defining ownership transfer rules, detached state handling, and memory lifecycle constraints across execution boundaries.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - MediaSourceHandle Interface
relevance: Ensures predictable error handling, resource cleanup, and multi-tenant isolation when multiple mini-apps or embedded video feeds instantiate off-thread media pipelines concurrently.

normative: MediaSourceHandle must be exposed in window and DedicatedWorker execution scopes as an opaque handle object with no readable prototype properties.
Attempting to read or modify properties on MediaSourceHandle must throw a TypeError, preserving strict encapsulation of the underlying platform media pipeline.

If the worker context hosting the parent MediaSource terminates prematurely or encounters an unhandled exception, the bound HTMLMediaElement must fire an 'error' event with MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED.
A MediaSourceHandle that has been transferred becomes detached in the sender context and cannot be utilized for subsequent postMessage operations.
Host containers must track active MediaSourceHandle instances per mini-app instance to enforce hardware video decoder allocation limits (e.g. max 4 active decoders per container).
implementation_guidelines: Implement an explicit worker heartbeat and watchdog in the mini-app shell to detect and recover from media worker crashes without reloading the entire mini-app.
Catch InvalidStateError when assigning detached or already-bound handles to srcObject.
Release underlying media resources explicitly by calling mediaSource.endOfStream() or closing the MediaSource within the worker upon video completion.
anti_patterns: Re-using the same MediaSourceHandle across multiple video player elements, causing state machine corruption and decoder stalls.
Failing to terminate idle media worker threads when the user pauses or backgrounds the mini-app, leading to battery drain.

title: HTMLMediaElement.srcObject Multi-Source Integration & Precedence
description: Defines the specification and precedence rules for HTMLMediaElement.srcObject, governing binding behavior for MediaStream, Blob, and MediaSourceHandle instances in mobile webviews.
evidence_level: WHATWG HTML Living Standard & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - HTMLMediaElement.srcObject & WHATWG HTML Section 4.8.4 Media elements
relevance: Provides the universal playback attachment point for modern super-app multimedia pipelines, eliminating memory leaks associated with URL.createObjectURL strings and facilitating smooth source transitions.

normative: HTMLMediaElement.srcObject must take absolute precedence over the 'src' HTML attribute or property; if srcObject is non-null, the user agent must ignore 'src'.
User agents must support assignment of MediaStream (WebRTC/Camera), MediaSource (main-thread), and MediaSourceHandle (worker-thread) to srcObject.
Clearing media playback must be executed by setting mediaElement.srcObject = null, which immediately stops decoding and detaches the underlying media stream.
Mini-app containers must prevent untrusted script injection from hijacking or replacing srcObject with unauthenticated media feeds.
Video playback initiated via srcObject must respect container autoplay policies, requiring transient user activation or the 'muted' attribute.
implementation_guidelines: Always prefer element.srcObject = handle over legacy URL.createObjectURL(mediaSource) to avoid persistent internal URL map memory leaks.
Explicitly set mediaElement.srcObject = null and call mediaElement.load() when unmounting video player components to release mobile hardware decoders immediately.
Monitor 'srcobjectchange' or observe srcObject property mutations in automated store quality checks to verify clean component teardown.
anti_patterns: Simultaneously setting both element.src and element.srcObject, resulting in confusing browser fallback behavior and redundant network requests.
Leaving srcObject attached to offscreen or paused video elements, holding valuable hardware video decoders hostage on constrained mobile GPUs.

title: Super-App Streaming Media Store Standards & Quota Governance
description: Establishes store review criteria, performance SLAs, memory quotas, and background throttling policies for mini-apps implementing adaptive streaming via Media Source Extensions.
evidence_level: Platform Implementation Standard / Store Review Guidelines
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Media Source Extensions API & Super-App Media Governance
relevance: Provides automated store validation rules and platform runtime policies to guarantee that high-bandwidth streaming mini-apps maintain battery efficiency, avoid thermal throttling, and prevent ANR crashes on mobile devices.

normative: Mini-apps categorized under Live Commerce, Video On Demand, or Cloud Gaming must utilize DedicatedWorker MSE (or WebCodecs) for demuxing and buffering to meet store INP (< 50ms) certification.
SourceBuffer queues must enforce strict memory budgets: maximum buffer memory must not exceed 50MB for 1080p video and 20MB for 720p streams on mobile devices.
The mini-app must implement dynamic buffer eviction, continuously removing played media segments via SourceBuffer.remove(0, currentTime - 30) to prevent memory ballooning.
When the mini-app enters background or hidden state, video decoding must pause within 2 seconds unless explicit background-audio permissions are granted by the user.
Automated store submission scanners must verify that all streaming network endpoints use HTTPS/TLS 1.3 and conform to mini-app manifest network domain allowlists.
implementation_guidelines: Integrate SourceBuffer 'updateend' event listeners with strict timeout guards to prevent deadlock when appending corrupt media segments.
Utilize the W3C Compute Pressure API in the media worker to dynamically downgrade streaming bitrates when mobile CPU or thermal pressure reaches 'serious' or 'critical'.
Provide detailed video playback analytics (buffering ratio, dropped frames, decoder errors) to the super-app observability bridge via PerformanceObserver.
anti_patterns: Accumulating hours of historical video chunks in SourceBuffer without eviction, leading to low-memory terminations (LMT) by the mobile operating system.
Continuing high-resolution video decoding while the webview container is completely occluded or minimized, wasting battery and mobile data.

title: W3C CSS Nesting Module Level 1 Syntax Scoping & Runtime Parser Architecture
description: Standardizes native hierarchical style rule nesting, direct nesting syntax, and parent selector scoping (&) within super-app mini-app style sheets without preprocessor build dependencies.
evidence_level: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft / Web Standard
spec_anchor: W3C CSS Nesting Module Level 1 - Section 3 Nesting Style Rules
relevance: Mini-apps require modular component styling. Native CSS nesting eliminates transpilation drift from SASS/Less, simplifies CSS OM hydration in shadow roots, and enforces component encapsulation boundaries.

normative: Mini-app webview rendering engines must implement native CSS Nesting Module Level 1 parser specifications, supporting direct selector nesting and the explicit nesting selector (&).
Nested style rules must automatically inherit the parent selector's specificity and context, evaluating as if wrapped in :is() pseudo-classes.
Container runtime CSS parsers must correctly handle nested declarations following nested rules without requiring explicit CSS blocks or ambiguous lookahead parsing.

Mini-app build packagers must validate that nested selectors do not exceed maximum nesting depth limits (recommended ≤ 4 levels) to avoid selector specificity explosion and style recalculation latency.
Super-app theme injectors must support nested @media, @supports, and @layer blocks within component scopes, ensuring adaptive theme overrides remain strictly scoped to target mini-apps.
implementation_guidelines: Use native & parent references to style micro-component states (e.g., &:hover, &:active, &.is-selected) directly within component definitions.
Structure mini-app CSS stylesheets using native nesting to reduce code duplication and eliminate redundant class namespace prefixes.
Leverage native nesting combined with Declarative Shadow DOM to achieve isolated, self-contained web component style bundles.
anti_patterns: Nesting selectors deeper than 5 or 6 levels, causing catastrophic style recalculation overhead during mini-app DOM mutations and scrolling.
Using complex universal or tag-based descendant nested rules (e.g. & * or & div) that bypass container CSS encapsulation and invalidate caching.

title: CSS Native Nesting Selector Model & Multi-Tenant Style Isolation
description: Defines the evaluation semantics of the CSS nesting selector (&) and specificity resolution via :is() pseudo-class equivalence in super-app multi-tenant containers.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs Standard & W3C Technical Architecture
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - CSS Nesting & Selector Specificity Processing Model
relevance: When third-party mini-apps run within shared webview contexts or super-app shell overlays, uncontrolled CSS cascading can pollute host UI or break mini-app components. Native nesting provides clean containment semantics.

normative: Webview CSS engines must compute the specificity of nested rules using the :is() matching semantics defined in CSS Selectors Level 4, taking the specificity of the most specific argument in the selector list.
When prepending host container scope classes (e.g., .superapp-scope &), the runtime must maintain deterministic selector resolution without specificity inversion.
Dynamic CSS injection via mini-app style elements or constructable stylesheets must preserve CSS nesting structures without stripping nested braces.
Container style sanitizers must reject malformed nested rules that attempt to break out of component boundaries using invalid root selectors (:root, html, body) when running in embedded sub-contexts.
Store validation linters must inspect mini-app CSS bundles to ensure legacy vendor prefixes (-webkit-nested) are upgraded to standard CSS nesting syntax.
implementation_guidelines: Scope all third-party mini-app styling under a top-level host wrapper class using & to prevent global document style pollution.
Verify that CSS nesting transpilers (if used during build stages) produce standard W3C syntax targeting modern WebView versions (Chromium 120+, Safari 17.2+).
Combine CSS nesting with CSS custom properties (variables) to allow super-app hosts to safely inject global typography and spacing tokens.
anti_patterns: Relying on preprocessor-specific string concatenation hacks (e.g. &__element in BEM) with native CSS nesting, which fails in native parsers because & represents a complete selector.
Overriding host navigation bar or bottom sheet styles using un-scoped root nested declarations.

title: W3C Nesting Selector (&) Expansion & Compound Selector Semantics
description: Standardizes the exact behavior, selector expansion, and compound selector composition of the ampersand (&) nesting selector across mini-app DOM components.
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Nesting selector (&) Syntax and Usage
relevance: Ensures developers correctly author compound selectors, pseudo-classes, and pseudo-elements within mini-app UI trees without triggering silent parse failures.

normative: The nesting selector (&) must represent the elements matched by the parent style rule selector list.
In compound selectors, & must immediately concatenate with class, attribute, or pseudo-class selectors (e.g. &.active, &[disabled]) without whitespace to denote compound matching.
Whitespace between & and succeeding selectors must denote descendant combinators, matching descendant elements within the parent context.
The container CSS runtime must support multiple occurrences of & within a single nested selector (e.g. & + &, & > .child + &) to enable complex relational styling without duplicating selectors.
Store static analysis tools must scan CSS source files to flag misplaced & selectors that result in invalid CSS grammar in target mobile webview engines.
implementation_guidelines: Use & to declare adjacent sibling relationships within component lists (e.g. & + & { margin-top: 8px; }) to maintain consistent grid and flex item gutters.
Test component styling across both direct nesting (div { span { ... } }) and explicit ampersand nesting (div { & span { ... } }) to ensure uniform cross-engine rendering.
Document ampersand usage guidelines in the super-app developer portal to accelerate mini-app frontend onboarding.
anti_patterns: Assuming & can be used as a string prefix for class names (e.g. &--modifier), which produces invalid selectors in standard CSS nesting.
Nesting selectors without understanding specificity inheritance, leading to unexpected !important workarounds.

title: CSS Cascade Layers (@layer) & Multi-Tenant Priority Architecture
description: Standardizes cascade layer priority ordering (@layer framework, component, overrides) to resolve style precedence conflicts between super-app host shells and hosted mini-apps.
evidence_level: W3C Candidate Recommendation & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - @layer & W3C Cascading and Inheritance Level 5
relevance: Mini-apps load host design systems, UI component libraries, and merchant custom styles simultaneously. Cascade layers provide deterministic precedence resolution regardless of selector specificity.

normative: The super-app container must establish an explicit layer precedence order at initialization: @layer reset, superapp-base, miniapp-components, miniapp-overrides.
Host injected styles must reside in lower-precedence baseline layers, ensuring mini-app developer component styles reliably override base styles without requiring high-specificity selector hacking.
Unlayered styles must be treated by the CSS engine as having the highest normal cascade precedence, ensuring emergency host hotfixes can override third-party rules when necessary.
Mini-app build toolchains must support encapsulating third-party CSS bundles inside named layers (@layer vendor.library) to prevent unconstrained global overrides.
Automated store code reviews must check that mini-app stylesheets do not abuse !important declarations inside low-precedence layers to invert cascade order.
implementation_guidelines: Declare layer order once in the root super-app document head before loading any mini-app stylesheets: @layer reset, framework, app, theme.
Encourage mini-app developers to organize their stylesheets into structured layers: @layer theme, layout, components, utilities.
Utilize anonymous layers (@layer { ... }) for isolated, single-use style blocks to minimize global layer namespace collisions.
anti_patterns: Using unbounded global selectors with !important to overcome specificity mismatches between host frameworks and mini-app code.
Declaring conflicting layer ordering across multiple asynchronously loaded mini-app CSS chunks.

title: Native CSS Nesting Engine Performance & Style Recalculation SLAs
description: Defines runtime performance benchmarks, memory optimization strategies, and style recalculation SLAs for native CSS nesting in high-density mobile mini-apps.
evidence_level: Chrome Developers Architecture Guide & W3C WebPerf
spec_anchor: Chrome Developers - CSS Nesting Relaxed Parsing & Performance Guidelines
relevance: Deeply nested or unoptimized CSS rules significantly increase style invalidation and layout recalculation time during mini-app navigation, degrading Interaction to Next Paint (INP) and frame rates.

normative: Mini-app stylesheets leveraging CSS nesting must pass automated store linting ensuring total style recalculation duration does not exceed 16ms for 95% of interaction events on mid-tier mobile hardware.

Webview rendering runtimes must implement the relaxed CSS nesting parsing specification (discarding the legacy requirement that nested selectors must begin with & or symbols), ensuring modern syntax compatibility.
The container must monitor memory consumed by the CSS OM; stylesheets with excessive nested rule counts (> 2,000 rules) must trigger packaging warnings during store submission.
Mini-app engines must leverage constructable stylesheets (CSSStyleSheet()) to parse and share nested stylesheets across multiple web component instances without redundant parsing overhead.
Build tools must strip comments and unused nested branches during mini-app packaging to optimize transmission payloads.
implementation_guidelines: Keep nesting hierarchy shallow (2-3 levels maximum: block > element > state) to minimize style selector matching time.
Audit style recalculation performance using Chrome DevTools Performance panel or Web Vitals INP profiling tools during mini-app QA.
Preload core nested stylesheets using <link rel="preload" as="style"> with high fetch priority for critical rendering paths.
anti_patterns: Generating thousands of deeply nested selectors through automated CSS-in-JS abstractions that bloat memory and trigger repeated layout thrashing.
Mixing old transpiled SASS nested outputs with native CSS nesting in the same bundle without normalization.

title: W3C CSS Text Module Level 3 Processing Model & International Text Typography
description: Standardizes white space handling, line breaking, justification, word wrapping, and text alignment processing models for multi-lingual super-app mini-app interfaces.
evidence_level: W3C Candidate Recommendation Draft - CSS Text Module Level 3
spec_anchor: W3C CSS Text Module Level 3 - Section 5 Line Breaking and Word Boundaries
relevance: Super-apps operate across global and Southeast Asian multilingual markets (Vietnamese, Lao, Thai, Chinese, English). Proper text breaking and boundary rules prevent UI overflow and truncated text across varied mobile display widths.

normative: Mini-app webview typography engines must conform to W3C CSS Text Module Level 3 line breaking algorithms across complex and non-Latin scripts.
Runtimes must support CSS text-align: justify with text-justify: inter-character / inter-word according to document language semantics declared in the html lang attribute.
Text transformation properties (text-transform: uppercase, lowercase, capitalize) must execute locale-sensitive case mappings (e.g. Turkish dotted/dotless i, Greek diacritics).
Line breaking opportunities must respect Unicode line breaking properties (UAX #14), preventing un-hyphenated overflows outside parent container bounds.
Store UI compliance scanners must verify that text containers specify proper wrap behavior to prevent horizontal scrolling regressions on compact mobile viewports (≤ 360px).
implementation_guidelines: Always set explicit lang attributes on mini-app root elements and multilingual text spans to ensure the browser text engine activates script-appropriate hyphenation dictionaries.
Use white-space: normal or white-space: pre-wrap for user-generated content cards to ensure line breaks are preserved while long text wraps appropriately.
Test typography rendering across varied font sizes using dynamic type accessibility settings (e.g. 200% system font scaling).
anti_patterns: Using white-space: nowrap on unconstrained text blocks, causing elements to spill horizontally offscreen and break layout geometry.
Assuming character spacing and line breaking rules for Latin scripts apply identically to CJK or Southeast Asian Brahmic scripts.

title: CSS Text Typography Processing System & Font Metrics Alignment
description: Establishes standard CSS text styling primitives, text-indent, letter-spacing, word-spacing, and vertical text baseline alignment for super-app design system consistency.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs Standard & W3C CSS Text 3
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - CSS text Overview & Text Styling Primitives
relevance: Ensures mini-app UIs adhere to the host super-app design tokens for typography, preventing visual fragmentation and illegible text hierarchies in embedded mini-apps.

normative: Container typography design tokens must declare standardized letter-spacing and line-height ratios corresponding to viewport font-size tiers.
Mini-app text nodes must calculate baseline alignments deterministically across custom downloadable webfonts and system fallback fonts.
The container runtime must support text-decoration properties (text-decoration-line, text-decoration-color, text-decoration-thickness) conforming to CSS Text 3 specifications.
Store UI guidelines must mandate minimum contrast ratios (WCAG 2.2 AA 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text) across all text declarations.
Dynamic font sizing via CSS clamp() (e.g. clamp(14px, 2.5vw, 18px)) must be supported across all mini-app webview rendering contexts.
implementation_guidelines: Expose host typography tokens as CSS custom properties (e.g. var(--superapp-text-sm), var(--superapp-font-regular)) for seamless mini-app integration.
Apply letter-spacing: -0.01em on display headlines to improve legibility on high-resolution mobile retina screens.
Audit mini-app typography using accessibility evaluation tools during automated CI/CD store verification.
anti_patterns: Using fixed pixel line-heights smaller than the computed font-size, causing overlapping multi-line text when users increase font scaling.
Disabling text selection globally with user-select: none across content paragraphs, degrading user reading accessibility.
