title: CSS overflow-wrap (word-wrap) Layout Containment & Text Overflow Defense
description: Standardizes the application of overflow-wrap (anywhere, break-word, normal) to prevent unbreakable strings from overflowing layout boundaries in responsive mini-app containers.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs & W3C CSS Text Module Level 3
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - overflow-wrap & W3C CSS Text 3 Section 5.5
relevance: Mini-apps frequently display user-generated URLs, account identifiers, transaction hashes, and unspaced strings. Without overflow-wrap, these strings cause severe layout clipping and horizontal viewport scrolling.

normative: All mini-app text containers rendering dynamic or external string content (usernames, transaction IDs, addresses) must specify overflow-wrap: break-word or overflow-wrap: anywhere.

When overflow-wrap: anywhere is applied, the layout engine must consider arbitrary character breaking opportunities, preventing min-content intrinsic sizing from pushing container widths beyond viewport bounds.
Webview container CSS resets must default body, p, span, and card containers to overflow-wrap: break-word to ensure robust baseline layout containment.
Mini-app flex and grid children containing text must set min-width: 0 to allow overflow-wrap breaking algorithms to function properly within auto-sizing tracks.
Store automated rendering checks must capture layout screenshots on 320px viewports to verify that long uninterrupted test tokens do not induce horizontal overflow.
implementation_guidelines: Apply overflow-wrap: anywhere on elements containing alphanumeric strings like transaction hashes, cryptographic public keys, or full URL links.
Pair overflow-wrap with hyphens: auto in multi-column news or article reading mini-apps to achieve visually balanced text blocks.
Include min-width: 0 on all flexbox items displaying variable-length text to prevent flex-basis expansion bugs.
anti_patterns: Relying solely on overflow: hidden without overflow-wrap, which truncates text invisibly and renders critical account info unreadable.
Forgetting min-width: 0 on flex child containers, causing long strings to expand the flex item beyond parent boundaries despite overflow-wrap.

title: CSS word-break (break-all, keep-all) Multilingual Word Boundary Governance
description: Defines word breaking rules across Latin, CJK (Chinese, Japanese, Korean), and Southeast Asian text scripts using word-break: normal, break-all, and keep-all.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs & W3C CSS Text 3
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - word-break Property & Multilingual Typography Processing
relevance: Super-app mini-apps serving diverse international communities require script-aware word breaking. For example, CJK text requires keep-all for natural phrasing, while narrow table cells require break-all for compact data density.

normative: Mini-app layout engines must support word-break values: normal, break-all, and keep-all conforming to W3C CSS Text 3 specifications.
For CJK typography, mini-apps must support word-break: keep-all to prevent breaking between Korean Hangul syllables or Chinese phrase units unless necessary.
For dense financial tables and numeric data columns in mini-apps, word-break: break-all must be permitted to allow wrapping anywhere when table cell widths are constrained.
The container must ensure that word-break behavior interacts predictably with overflow-wrap without canceling hyphenation opportunities.
Store localization review checklists must evaluate mini-apps in their declared target languages to ensure text breaking conforms to local typographical conventions.
implementation_guidelines: Use word-break: normal; overflow-wrap: break-word as the default standard for mixed Latin and multilingual body text.
Use word-break: keep-all specifically for CJK and Korean text blocks to maintain semantic word clustering and professional visual presentation.
Set word-break: break-all for compact technical identifiers, serial numbers, and account reference tags.
anti_patterns: Applying word-break: break-all universally to Latin body paragraphs, resulting in awkward mid-word breaks (e.g. 'su- / perapp') that severely impair reading comprehension.
Failing to adapt word-break rules when localizing mini-apps between English and East/Southeast Asian language editions.

title: CSS hyphens (none, manual, auto) & Dictionary-Driven Text Layout
description: Standardizes hyphenation control, soft hyphens (­), and dictionary-driven automated hyphenation for high-quality mini-app editorial and card layout rendering.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs & W3C CSS Text Module Level 3
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - hyphens Property & W3C CSS Text 3 Section 5.4
relevance: Editorial, e-commerce, and news mini-apps require clean text justification. Automated hyphenation eliminates unsightly rivers of white space in justified text and prevents awkward ragged edges in narrow mobile columns.

normative: Mini-app webview containers must support the CSS hyphens property with values none, manual, and auto.
When hyphens: auto is declared, the browser engine must select hyphenation patterns matching the language specified by the element's lang attribute.
Soft hyphens (U+00AD or ­) must always be recognized and rendered as discretionary line-break and hyphenation opportunities regardless of whether auto hyphenation is active.
Webview container runtimes must include hyphenation dictionary bundles for the platform's core supported operating languages (English, Vietnamese, French, etc.).
Store validation tests must verify that mini-apps enabling hyphens: auto explicitly define valid BCP 47 language tags on parent elements to avoid silent hyphenation failure.
implementation_guidelines: Combine text-align: justify with hyphens: auto on multi-line text cards to produce magazine-quality layouts on mobile screens.
Insert soft hyphens (­) manually into very long compound technical terms or brand names where automatic dictionary coverage may be missing.
Disable hyphenation (hyphens: none) on buttons, navigation tabs, and badge labels where multi-line word breaks reduce instant recognition.
anti_patterns: Setting hyphens: auto on documents without specifying a lang attribute, resulting in no hyphenation or erroneous language dictionary application.
Allowing excessive consecutive hyphenated lines in editorial mini-apps, which degrades typographic readability.

title: HTML fetchpriority Attribute & Network Loading Prioritization Architecture
description: Standardizes declarative network scheduling hints via the fetchpriority attribute (high, low, auto) across ,
evidence_level: WHATWG HTML / Fetch Living Standard & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - fetchpriority HTML attribute & WICG Priority Hints
relevance: Mini-apps must boot in under 500ms on mobile devices. fetchpriority allows mini-apps to explicitly promote critical hero images and entry scripts ahead of low-priority tracking beacons or analytics bundles.

normative: Mini-app webview containers must support the HTML fetchpriority content attribute with enumerated values: high, low, and auto.
The container network dispatcher must map fetchpriority values directly into HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 stream priority frames (weight/dependency trees) when fetching assets over multiplexed connections.
The primary mini-app hero banner or LCP candidate image must declare fetchpriority="high" to accelerate resource discovery and decoding over lower-priority below-the-fold media.
Non-critical third-party analytics, diagnostic scripts, and preloaded offscreen assets must declare fetchpriority="low" to avoid bandwidth contention on constrained cellular networks.
Store automated performance scanners must verify that no mini-app marks more than 2 concurrent images as fetchpriority="high" to prevent priority dilution and network congestion.
implementation_guidelines: Pair <link rel="preload" as="image" fetchpriority="high"> with the LCP image element to trigger instant parallel fetch during initial HTML streaming.
Set fetchpriority="low" on social share widgets, tracking pixels, and non-blocking decorative background images.
Audit priority distribution using the Chrome DevTools Network panel (inspecting Priority column: VeryHigh, High, Low, VeryLow).
anti_patterns: Setting fetchpriority="high" indiscriminately on all page images and scripts, destroying network scheduling effectiveness.
Using fetchpriority="high" on large non-critical video previews or heavy below-the-fold carousel images that delay above-the-fold rendering.

title: HTMLImageElement fetchPriority DOM Property & Dynamic Media Scheduling
description: Defines programmatic priority control via HTMLImageElement.fetchPriority and its role in responsive image loading and mobile viewport hydration.
evidence_level: WHATWG HTML Living Standard & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - HTMLImageElement: fetchPriority property
relevance: Allows dynamic mini-app client frameworks (e.g. React, Vue, Svelte, or native Web Components) to programmatically prioritize images based on viewport intersection before DOM attachment.

normative: The HTMLImageElement interface in mini-app webviews must expose the fetchPriority IDL attribute reflecting the content attribute.
Setting img.fetchPriority = 'high' programmatically prior to assigning img.src must immediately update the underlying network request priority.
Dynamic image loaders and carousel components must downgrade fetchPriority to 'low' for slide images located beyond the immediate viewport boundaries.
When combining loading="lazy" with fetchPriority="high", the container must evaluate intersection rules first, applying high priority once the lazy loading threshold is crossed.
Store submission benchmarking must measure LCP improvement from fetchPriority optimization, flagging apps where LCP exceeds 2.5 seconds on 4G emulation.
implementation_guidelines: Set img.fetchPriority = 'high' for the active item in hero product carousels, and 'low' for adjacent slide buffers.
Integrate fetchPriority configuration into mini-app image optimization components (e.g. <MiniImage hero={true} />).
Ensure server-side rendered or pre-rendered mini-app shells serialize fetchpriority directly into the initial HTML payload.
anti_patterns: Assigning img.fetchPriority = 'high' after setting img.src, which may arrive after the network dispatcher has already scheduled the request at default priority.
Setting fetchPriority="high" on all lazy-loaded product thumbnails in endless scrolling catalogs.

title: HTMLScriptElement fetchPriority & Main Thread Execution Governance
description: Standardizes priority hints on <script> tags to balance parser-blocking execution, module graph resolution, and deferred background logic.
evidence_level: WHATWG HTML Living Standard & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - HTMLScriptElement: fetchPriority property
relevance: Mini-app architectures rely heavily on JavaScript module bundles. Setting appropriate fetchPriority on module entrypoints accelerates Time to Interactive (TTI) and First Contentful Paint (FCP).

normative: Webview script loading pipelines must honor fetchPriority on both classic and module (<script type="module">) scripts.
The core mini-app runtime bootstrap bundle must be loaded with fetchpriority="high" (or preloaded) to expedite DOM hydration.
Auxiliary scripts (e.g., chat SDKs, payment gateways loaded conditionally, non-immediate feature bundles) must specify fetchpriority="low".
Async scripts without fetchPriority default to low priority; developers must be permitted to explicitly elevate them via fetchpriority="high" when early asynchronous execution is required.
Automated store packaging validators must check that vendor script bundles do not inject high-priority scripts into the main document without host platform approval.
implementation_guidelines: Load essential UI component definitions with <script type="module" src="app.js" fetchpriority="high"></script>.
Assign fetchpriority="low" to deferred feature modules imported dynamically via script injection.
Measure Total Blocking Time (TBT) to ensure high-priority script execution does not monopolize the main thread during initial user interactions.
anti_patterns: Marking multiple large monolithic script bundles with fetchpriority="high", causing network queue saturation and starvation of CSS stylesheets.
Elevating third-party ad or tracker scripts to high priority, severely degrading mini-app startup metrics.

title: Fetch API RequestInit priority Property & API Call Prioritization
description: Standardizes programmatic network request prioritization via the priority property in the RequestInit dictionary of window.fetch().
evidence_level: WHATWG Fetch Living Standard & MDN Web Docs
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - RequestInit: priority property & WHATWG Fetch Request Priority
relevance: Mini-apps execute numerous API calls simultaneously (user data, catalog listings, analytics logs, prefetch queries). The priority option allows developers to prevent background traffic from delaying critical user transactions.

normative: The mini-app JavaScript runtime must support RequestInit.priority with permitted values: 'high', 'low', and 'auto'.
Critical transactional API requests (e.g. checkout submissions, authentication handshakes, payment confirmations) must be dispatched with priority: 'high'.
Background telemetry, audit logging, and speculative prefetching requests must be dispatched with priority: 'low'.
When priority is omitted or set to 'auto', the container must assign default fetch priority (typically high for API fetches) according to standard Fetch specification heuristics.
Super-app API proxy gateways and Service Workers must inspect request priority metadata and preserve stream prioritization across upstream microservice hops.
implementation_guidelines: Wrap the global fetch client with a centralized API gateway module that automatically attaches priority based on endpoint classification (mutation vs telemetry).
Use priority: 'low' for all prefetch calls triggered on link hover or list scrolling.
Verify network waterfall sequences in integration tests to ensure checkout calls bypass background sync queues.
anti_patterns: Sending high-frequency analytics and sensor telemetry pings with priority: 'high', starving critical business API responses on high-latency mobile networks.
Hardcoding priority: 'high' across all internal RPC endpoints without differentiation.

title: End-to-End Resource Prioritization & Network Scheduling SLA Governance
description: Establishes holistic resource loading patterns, priority budgeting, and network SLA governance combining HTML attributes, preload links, and Fetch API priority controls.
evidence_level: MDN Web Docs & Web Performance Working Group Guidelines
spec_anchor: MDN Web Docs - Using Fetch: Prioritizing Requests and Network Governance
relevance: Provides a comprehensive architectural standard for mini-app developers and store operators to achieve predictable sub-second loading performance across fluctuating 3G/4G/5G mobile environments.

normative: Mini-app packages must enforce a strict network priority budget: at most 1 high-priority image, 1 high-priority stylesheet, and 1 high-priority bootstrap script on initial load.
Preload links (<link rel="preload">) must declare consistent fetchpriority attributes matching the element tag priority in the DOM to avoid double-download anomalies.

When network conditions degrade to slow 3G / 2G (detected via NetworkInformation API), the runtime must automatically downgrade all 'auto' priority requests to 'low' except explicit 'high' transactions.
The container network layer must support HTTP/2 PRIORITY / RFC 9218 Extensible Prioritization Schemes (urgency=u, incremental=i) mapping high/low priorities to wire headers.
Store submission pipelines must run automated network throttling tests (4G 1.6Mbps / 150ms RTT) and verify that initial visual render occurs within 1,200ms.
implementation_guidelines: Document standard resource prioritization patterns in the super-app developer documentation and SDK starter kits.
Implement automated lint rules in mini-app CLI tools to detect and warn against conflicting preload and fetchpriority settings.
Monitor real-user network timing metrics (DNS, TCP, TTFB, download duration) segmented by request priority tier.
anti_patterns: Preloading non-critical fonts or secondary images with fetchpriority="high", blocking the download of primary layout stylesheets.
Ignoring mobile network state changes and pushing heavy background data synchronization while the user is actively interacting with foreground UI.

title: WHATWG HTML <dialog> Element & Browser Top Layer Modal Isolation
description: Establishes normative standards for modal dialog rendering and view isolation using the HTML <dialog> element and the browser Top Layer rendering stack. Requiring mini app modal dialogs (payment confirmations, sensitive scope prompts, terms agreements) to use HTMLDialogElement.showModal() places the dialog in the browser Top Layer, automatically rendering above all z-index hierarchies in the DOM, preventing UI redressing, z-index hijacking, and clickjacking attacks. Furthermore, showModal() automatically applies focus trapping within the dialog boundary and provides built-in ESC key cancel event dispatching, guaranteeing accessible modal containment.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 4.11.1 The dialog element
detail.modal_lifecycle: HTMLDialogElement.showModal() activates top-layer rendering, sets inert on document ancestors, and traps tab focus; show() displays non-modal dialog; close(returnValue) sets returnValue and emits close event.
detail.top_layer_isolation: Top Layer stack renders independent of z-index and overflow clipping of host elements, eliminating stacking context escape vulnerabilities.
detail.security_mitigations: Prevents malicious third-party mini app scripts from overlaying fake host UI over system dialogs; ensures strict containment of user confirmation prompts.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps rendering full-screen modal prompts MUST utilize <dialog> with showModal() or host container sheet APIs; custom z-index: 999999 overlay hacks are flagged during automated store linting.

title: WHATWG HTML inert Global Attribute & Document Subtree Interaction Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the inert boolean global attribute to programmatically deactivate DOM subtrees during modal operations, drawer animations, and background workflow processing in super app containers. When an element is marked inert, the browser ignores all user input events (clicks, keypresses, touches), removes all contained elements from the accessibility tree, and excludes them from sequential keyboard focus navigation. This provides a declarative, performance-optimized mechanism for multi-view mini apps to prevent rogue touch events and focus leakage into inactive views without manual DOM removal or complex event listener detaching.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 6.5.3 The inert attribute
detail.runtime_behavior: Browser suppresses pointer events, keyboard focus, and accessibility node generation for the entire subtree of an inert node.
detail.performance_advantage: Eliminates CPU overhead of manually iterating DOM nodes to set tabindex='-1' and aria-hidden='true', delegating layout engine tree pruning to C++ engine core.
detail.superapp_container_use: When the super app capsule displays a native payment bottom sheet or security verification prompt, it marks the entire mini app container root as inert, preventing background interaction.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps managing multi-stage wizards or slide-over navigation drawers MUST apply inert to inactive panels to maintain WCAG 2.2 keyboard navigation compliance.

title: HTMLDialogElement.showModal() Built-In Focus Trapping & Accessible Interaction Architecture
description: Specifies programmatic lifecycle requirements for HTMLDialogElement.showModal(), detailing user agent standard mechanisms for initial focus assignment, cyclical keyboard navigation trapping, and cancellation event propagation. When showModal() executes, user agents determine the autofocus candidate or default to the first focusable element within the dialog, while blocking tab traversal beyond dialog boundaries. Listening for the 'cancel' event allows mini apps to validate mandatory user decisions before dismissal, while user agent ESC key handling guarantees an escape hatch against predatory dialog traps.

detail.focus_trapping_semantics: User agent constrains focus loop strictly between dialog first and last focusable elements; prevents keyboard focus leaks into host capsule controls.
detail.cancellation_governance: cancel event fires when user triggers platform dismiss (ESC key or hardware back gesture); preventDefault() can temporarily block closing if unsaved transaction data exists.
detail.return_value_contract: dialog.close(result) sets HTMLDialogElement.returnValue, returning structured status codes to invoking UI components.
detail.store_review_rule: Automated review gates verify that dialog cancellation cannot be indefinitely hijacked; canceling must resolve within 2 user dismissal gestures.

title: Browser Top Layer Stacking Architecture & UI Redressing Elimination
description: Defines the architectural properties of the browser Top Layer, a discrete rendering plane situated above the root stacking context and unaffected by parent overflow, transform, filter, or z-index CSS properties. In multi-tenant super app environments, third-party mini app components frequently suffer from CSS z-index escalation wars or clipping by overflow: hidden wrappers. By promoting elements to the Top Layer (via <dialog showModal>, Popover API, or Fullscreen API), elements are guaranteed unclipped viewport presentation and strict last-in-first-out (LIFO) visual stacking, completely eliminating z-index hijacking vulnerabilities.

detail.rendering_stack: Top Layer lives outside document root stacking context; render order is determined by insertion order into the top layer stack.
detail.clipping_immunity: Immune to ancestor overflow: hidden, clip-path, transform, or perspective styling that normally clips fixed-position elements.
detail.security_boundaries: Guarantees that host security notices and critical mini app alerts cannot be obscured by rogue floating elements with extreme z-index values.
detail.capsule_coordination: Super app native shell maintains a dedicated Top Layer tier above webview Top Layer, ensuring native close capsules and system alerts always supersede webview dialogs.

title: CSS ::backdrop Pseudo-Element Stacking & Modal Dimming Governance
description: Standardizes the styling and presentation layer for modal backdrops using the CSS ::backdrop pseudo-element generated for Top Layer elements. ::backdrop renders immediately below the Top Layer element and above all other page content, providing a standard, hardware-accelerated surface for background dimming, gaussian blur (backdrop-filter: blur()), and click-to-dismiss gesture handling. Super app design systems enforce unified ::backdrop visual tokens (e.g. rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45) with blur(4px)) to ensure cohesive UI ergonomics and prevent malicious transparent overlay clickjacking.

detail.rendering_position: Placed immediately behind the top-layer element in the stacking order, covering the entire viewport.
detail.styling_capabilities: Supports background-color, opacity, backdrop-filter, animation, and transitions for smooth modal entry/exit.
detail.clickjacking_defense: Enforces full viewport coverage to intercept unintended clicks to background mini app elements while modal is active.
detail.store_design_guideline: Mini apps must adopt platform-standard ::backdrop opacity tokens and avoid opaque backdrops that visually mask host capsule navigation controls.

title: ECMA-402 ECMAScript Internationalization API Standard & Engine Runtime Architecture
description: Establishes normative standards for client-side multilingual localization and locale data resolution within super app container runtimes based on ECMA-402. Mini apps operating across diverse global markets require high-performance, memory-efficient string comparison, number/currency formatting, date-time representation, and text segmentation without bundling massive third-party localization libraries (such as Moment.js or raw CLDR tables). Conformance to ECMA-402 ensures deterministic locale matching (lookup vs best fit), BCP 47 language tag parsing, and delegation to underlying operating system ICU data, reducing mini app bundle sizes by hundreds of kilobytes.

detail.specification: ECMA-402 ECMAScript 2026 Internationalization API Specification
detail.runtime_architecture: Exposes the global Intl namespace providing standardized locale-sensitive constructors optimized by host V8/JavaScriptCore C++ engines.
detail.bundle_optimization: Direct use of native Intl eliminates bloated JavaScript localization libraries, saving 150KB-400KB in mini app package payload.
detail.locale_resolution: Defines deterministic locale negotiation supporting BCP 47 tags with Unicode extension keys (e.g. ja-JP-u-ca-japanese, ar-SA-u-nu-arab).
detail.store_review_rule: Store static analyzers inspect mini app bundles and flag redundant third-party i18n runtimes, recommending native Intl adoption to improve startup latency.

title: Intl.Segmenter Locale-Sensitive Text Boundary Analysis & Word Segmentation
description: Standardizes locale-aware grapheme, word, and sentence boundary segmentation using Intl.Segmenter. In Asian languages (such as Chinese, Japanese, and Thai) that do not employ spaces between words, naive JavaScript split('') or regex operations break character clusters, corrupt emoji modifiers, or split words incorrectly, causing layout distortion and defective text wrapping. Intl.Segmenter provides high-performance, dictionary-driven segmentation matching native OS text layout engines, essential for mini app search tokenization, rich text editors, and responsive typography layouts.

detail.segment_iterator: segment(inputString) returns an iterable of SegmentData objects containing segment string, index offset, and isWordLike boolean.
detail.script_support: Accurately segments complex non-delimited scripts (CJK, Thai, Lao, Khmer) using underlying ICU break iterators.
detail.emoji_cluster_handling: Prevents corruption of zero-width joiner (ZWJ) emoji sequences and skin tone modifiers during text truncation.
detail.store_quality_standard: Mini apps providing text editing, chat widgets, or custom search parsing MUST use Intl.Segmenter to guarantee text rendering fidelity across CJK and SEA markets.

title: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat Localized Time Elapsed & Humanized Chronology Governance
description: Specifies native client-side relative time and elapsed duration formatting via Intl.RelativeTimeFormat. E-commerce transaction status updates, ride-hailing arrival estimates, and social feed timestamps within mini apps require localized relative phrasing (e.g. 'in 3 minutes', 'yesterday', 'il y a 2 heures'). Intl.RelativeTimeFormat formats values into localized strings or formatted parts without network round-trips to backend localization services, supporting numeric styles ('always' vs 'auto') for natural linguistic expressions.

detail.methods: format(value, unit) returns human-readable string; formatToParts(value, unit) returns tokenized array for granular styling.
detail.supported_units: year, quarter, month, week, day, hour, minute, second.
detail.memory_efficiency: Eliminates continuous string concatenation and localized template compiling on main thread during high-frequency feed rendering.
detail.store_benchmark: Super app catalog audit verifies that mini app transaction feeds utilize Intl.RelativeTimeFormat to prevent mismatched server/client time display drift.

title: Intl.ListFormat Localized Item Enumeration & Grammatical Joining Standards
description: Standardizes locale-aware list formatting and item enumeration using Intl.ListFormat. Mini app checkout summaries, permission scope listings, and product attribute enumerations often combine multiple items into human-readable sentences. Relying on hardcoded commas and 'and' fails in multilingual super apps (e.g. Oxford comma rules in English, Chinese enumeration comma '、' and '和', French 'et', or Arabic 'و'). Intl.ListFormat formats arrays into grammatically correct localized strings supporting 'conjunction', 'disjunction', and 'unit' styles.

description: Establishes standards for client-side sorting, searching, and alphabetical indexing of data collections using Intl.Collator. title: ServiceWorkerRegistration Interface & Container Registration Scope Security
description: Establishes normative standards for mini app Service Worker registration, scope restriction, and background coordination via the ServiceWorkerRegistration interface. title: self.skipWaiting() & Immediate Service Worker Activation Pipeline
description: Standardizes the self.skipWaiting() execution protocol for seamless over-the-air (OTA) updates and immediate service worker activation. By default, a newly installed service worker remains in the 'waiting' state until all client tabs/documents controlled by the current active worker are closed. In mobile super app containers where users navigate between mini app pages without closing the super app, waiting workers would stall indefinitely. Calling self.skipWaiting() within the install event listener forces the new worker to bypass waiting and immediately transition to activating, ensuring security patches and breaking API fixes take effect without user restarts.

title: Clients.claim() First-Load Network Interception & Controller Synchronization
description: Specifies normative requirements for self.clients.claim() within the Service Worker activate event handler. Normally, when a user accesses a mini app for the very first time, the document is loaded over the network before the service worker finishes registration; subsequent requests from that initial page load are not controlled by the service worker until a manual reload. Calling clients.claim() immediately binds all in-scope document clients to the active service worker, enabling instant offline asset caching and fetch interception on the user's first visit without requiring a page refresh.

While browsers automatically check for service worker script updates during navigation if >24 hours have elapsed, super apps need proactive update orchestration. By executing registration.update() during visibilitychange (when resuming from background) or upon receiving a WebSocket/Push update signal from the super app platform, the mini app container immediately queries the server for script byte differences, bypassing 24-hour dormancy caps and guaranteeing swift rollout of critical updates.

title: W3C ResizeObserver API & Asynchronous Box Dimension Observation
description: Establishes normative standards for asynchronous DOM element dimension monitoring using the W3C ResizeObserver API. Traditional window 'resize' event handlers cause severe main-thread thrashing, layout reflow storms, and INP degradation when multiple widgets recalculate dimensions simultaneously. title: ResizeObserver Memory Management & unobserve()/disconnect() Teardown Contracts
description: Specifies deterministic resource cleanup and memory leak prevention protocols for ResizeObserver instances via unobserve() and disconnect(). description: Standardizes client runtime error handling and mitigation contracts for 'ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications' exceptions. The W3C ResizeObserver processing model defines depth-based delivery passes to prevent cyclic infinite loops (where a resize callback mutates DOM styles that immediately trigger another resize). description: Establishes normative standards for modular, micro-frontend component styling using W3C CSS Container Queries (@container). detail.three_parameter_contract: Accepts minimum value, preferred value, and maximum value; preferred value scales continuously until clamped by boundaries.
detail.fluid_type_governance: Eliminates jarring font size jumps at discrete media query breakpoints, creating a polished native-like visual presentation.
detail.accessibility_integration: Must incorporate relative rem/em units in min and max parameters to respect system-level user font scale preferences.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app audit suites test fluid typography for text overflow and clipping when host device displays are set to 200% system font magnification.

title: CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3 & Declarative Feature Sandboxing
description: Establishes normative standards for conditional CSS processing under W3C CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3. The specification formalizes @supports and @media at-rules, enabling mini app styling engines to query user agent feature support, display capabilities, and operating environment constraints before applying advanced styling rules. This guarantees progressive enhancement across diverse WebView versions without stylesheet parsing failures.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3 - Section 6 Feature Queries: the @supports rule
detail.condition_logic: Defines grammar for feature queries including conjunction (and), disjunction (or), and negation (not) operators.
detail.progressive_enhancement: Allows mini apps to adopt cutting-edge CSS features (e.g. subgrid, anchor positioning, view transitions) while maintaining rock-solid fallbacks for older devices.
detail.parser_resilience: Prevents catastrophic stylesheet dropping: un-supported properties inside an @supports block are ignored safely without affecting the rest of the stylesheet.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app submission suites require all CSS declarations using experimental or browser-prefixed features to be wrapped in @supports queries.

title: CSS @supports At-Rule & Progressive Enhancement Sandboxing
description: Specifies protocols for declarative CSS feature queries using the @supports rule. Mini app developers declare condition checks (e.g. @supports (backdrop-filter: blur(10px)) or @supports selector(:has(a))) to selectively activate visual effects, modern layout models, and glassmorphism styling only when natively supported by the host WebView engine. In super app stores, this eliminates visual bugs and broken layouts on legacy Android system WebViews.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3 - Section 6.1 The @supports at-rule
detail.syntax_capabilities: Supports property: value pairs, selector() queries, and complex logical expressions with parenthesized grouping.
detail.webview_fragmentation_defense: Protects against WebView version fragmentation across Android 8 to 15, ensuring consistent rendering regardless of the underlying Chromium engine version.
detail.rendering_efficiency: Eliminates runtime JavaScript browser-sniffing scripts, offloading capability testing to the native C++ style parser.
detail.store_review_rule: Static analysis checks verify that CSS files using backdrop-filter or CSS grid subgrid provide fallback declarations outside @supports blocks.

title: CSS.supports() Programmatic Interface & Dynamic Style Gating
description: Standardizes programmatic CSS feature querying via the CSS.supports() static method. Mini app JavaScript frameworks and super app SDK bridges execute CSS.supports(property, value) or CSS.supports(conditionString) to dynamically verify whether the active container WebView supports specific styling features (e.g. CSS.supports('container-type', 'inline-size')) before dynamically injecting components or toggling virtualized rendering algorithms.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Conditional Rules Module Level 3 - Section 7 The CSS.supports() method
detail.method_signatures: CSS.supports(property, value) tests specific declaration; CSS.supports(conditionText) parses and tests arbitrary condition strings.
detail.dynamic_runtime_adaptation: Enables UI component libraries to choose between native CSS container queries and JavaScript ResizeObserver polyfills at initialization.
detail.zero_reflow_querying: Provides instant boolean results without triggering costly layout recalculations or DOM node creation.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app UI frameworks must use CSS.supports() rather than fragile navigator.userAgent string parsing to detect CSS engine capabilities.

title: Window.matchMedia() API & Programmatic Media Query Synchronization
description: Establishes normative standards for querying CSS media queries programmatically via window.matchMedia(mediaQueryString). Returning a MediaQueryList object, matchMedia enables mini apps and super app host shells to inspect viewport dimensions, orientation states, and accessibility preferences (e.g. window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')) synchronously without mutating DOM elements or measuring layout geometry.

detail.specification: CSS Object Model (CSSOM) View Module - Section 11 The MediaQueryList Interface
detail.query_evaluation: Synchronously evaluates media query string against current window state, returning a live MediaQueryList instance with matches boolean.
detail.system_preference_bridging: Allows host super app containers to synchronize system dark mode, reduced motion, and high contrast settings into guest mini app JavaScript state.
detail.avoiding_layout_thrashing: Replaces element.offsetWidth and window.innerWidth polling loops with zero-cost CSSOM media queries.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps responding to viewport or orientation changes must use matchMedia rather than window.onresize geometry reading.

title: MediaQueryList Interface & Asynchronous Environmental Change Handling
description: Standardizes event-driven reactive state synchronization using the MediaQueryList interface and its 'change' event. Instead of constantly polling viewport sizes, mini apps register event listeners (mql.addEventListener('change', callback)) on MediaQueryList instances. When a foldable phone unfolds, a tablet rotates, or the host OS toggles dark mode, the event fires asynchronously with the updated MediaQueryListEvent, enabling seamless UI restructuring.

detail.specification: CSS Object Model (CSSOM) View Module - Section 11.1 Event handlers on MediaQueryList objects
detail.event_contract: Dispatches MediaQueryListEvent containing media (string) and matches (boolean) properties whenever the evaluation state transitions.
detail.lifecycle_and_teardown: Requires mini apps to invoke removeEventListener('change', handler) during component unmounting to prevent memory leaks in single-page apps.
detail.foldable_and_multiwindow_support: Critical for handling dynamic window splits, Samsung DeX transitions, and iPad Split View mode changes without app reload.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must clean up registered MediaQueryList event listeners upon route teardown; automated tests check for orphaned listener retainers.

title: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification & Motion Sensor Sandboxing
description: Establishes normative standards for accessing physical device orientation and motion data under the W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification. The standard defines the DeviceOrientationEvent and DeviceMotionEvent interfaces, exposing physical angular coordinate orientation (alpha, beta, gamma) and linear acceleration data. Super app containers deploy strict governance over these events, enforcing permission prompting, background event suppression, and sampling frequency limits to eliminate keystroke eavesdropping and battery drain.

detail.specification: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification - Section 4 Device Orientation and Motion
detail.sensor_model: Exposes Earth-fixed frame orientation and device-coordinate acceleration from built-in accelerometers and gyroscopes.
detail.side_channel_threats: High-frequency motion sensor access can be exploited by malicious scripts to reconstruct pin/password keystrokes and infer user physical activity.
detail.privacy_boundaries: Requires secure context (HTTPS) and explicit user gesture permission on iOS (DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission) and Android.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps requesting device motion or orientation must declare functional justification in app.json and demonstrate interactive game/compass UX.

title: DeviceOrientationEvent Interface & 3-Axis Angular Orientation Governance
description: Specifies protocols for consuming physical device orientation data via the DeviceOrientationEvent interface. Exposing alpha (0 to 360 deg z-axis yaw), beta (-180 to 180 deg x-axis pitch), gamma (-90 to 90 deg y-axis roll), and absolute (boolean) properties, the event drives AR navigation, 3D product inspection, and mobile gaming. Super app host runtimes enforce quantization on angular values (e.g. rounding to nearest 0.5 degrees) to prevent micro-movement behavioral device fingerprinting.

detail.specification: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification - Section 5.1 The DeviceOrientationEvent Interface
detail.coordinate_system: Right-handed Cartesian coordinate system: alpha is rotation around Z (heading), beta around X (front-to-back), gamma around Y (left-to-right).
detail.quantization_safeguards: Host container bridges quantize floating point angles to 1 decimal place to thwart side-channel biometric tracking across mini app sessions.
detail.lifecycle_suspension: Event dispatching is immediately halted when document.visibilityState transitions to 'hidden' to preserve CPU and battery life.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must not run continuous deviceorientation event listeners in background tabs or invisible iframes.

title: DeviceMotionEvent Interface & Real-Time Kinematic Acceleration Telemetry
description: Standardizes dynamic physical movement tracking via the DeviceMotionEvent interface. The interface provides real-time measurement of device acceleration (with and without gravity), rotation rate, and sampling interval. Mini apps utilize motion telemetry for shake gestures, step counting, and tilt controls. Super app security layers sandbox motion events, intercepting raw sensor streams to enforce maximum 60Hz sampling caps and zero-data dispatch when the host app loses focus.

detail.specification: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification - Section 5.2 The DeviceMotionEvent Interface
detail.property_taxonomy: acceleration, accelerationIncludingGravity, rotationRate (alpha, beta, gamma in deg/s), and interval (ms).
detail.permission_arbitration: On modern iOS/WebKit platforms, requires explicit user activation prompt via DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() resolving to 'granted'.
detail.battery_and_thermal_impact: High-rate accelerometer polling increases CPU wakeups; super app runtime limits polling to active interactive screens.
detail.store_review_rule: Store security scanners check that mini apps request motion permissions conditionally and gracefully handle 'denied' permission states.

title: DeviceMotionEvent.acceleration & Linear Force Vector Isolation
description: Establishes normative standards for processing linear acceleration vectors via DeviceMotionEvent.acceleration. Unlike accelerationIncludingGravity, this property isolates the user-applied acceleration vector (x, y, z in m/s^2) by filtering out the Earth's 9.81 m/s^2 gravitational constant using onboard sensor fusion algorithms. Super apps validate acceleration thresholds to implement standard shake-to-refresh or shake-to-feedback gestures while rejecting spurious noise.

detail.specification: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification - Section 5.2 Interface DeviceMotionEvent (acceleration)
detail.vector_components: Exposes x (left-right), y (bottom-top), and z (perpendicular towards user) in meters per second squared.
detail.sensor_fusion_dependency: Requires device hardware support for accelerometer + gyroscope fusion; returns null when gravity separation is unavailable.
detail.gesture_detection_thresholds: Standard super app shake gesture pattern requires combined magnitude sqrt(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) > 15 m/s^2 across 3 consecutive cycles.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps implementing shake gestures must provide accessible touch button alternatives for users with motor disabilities (WCAG 2.2 2.5.4).

title: DeviceMotionEvent.rotationRate & Angular Velocity Telemetry Sandboxing
description: Standardizes angular velocity measurement via the DeviceMotionEvent.rotationRate dictionary. Exposing rotation rates around the alpha (deg/s z-axis), beta (deg/s x-axis), and gamma (deg/s y-axis) planes, this property captures dynamic rotational speed from physical gyroscope sensors. Super app host architectures enforce strict origin scoping, ensuring rotation rate streams cannot be correlated with external advertising SDKs to track user handling patterns.

detail.specification: W3C DeviceOrientation Event Specification - Section 5.2 Interface DeviceMotionEvent (rotationRate)
detail.velocity_metrics: alpha: deg/s around screen normal; beta: deg/s around horizontal screen axis; gamma: deg/s around vertical screen axis.
detail.noise_filtering_and_clamping: Super app container bridge applies low-pass filter to eliminate sensor jitter and clamps maximum reportable velocity to 720 deg/s.
detail.security_cross_origin_isolation: Disallowed in third-party cross-origin iframes unless explicitly granted via Permissions Policy: accelerometer 'self' gyroscope 'self'.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps using gyroscope rotationRate for gaming must implement calibration wizards and provide fallback on-screen joysticks.

title: CSS @starting-style Rule & First-Style-Update Entry Animation Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the definition of initial style states for elements transitioning from display: none or appearing in the DOM for the first time via the CSS @starting-style at-rule. This mechanism establishes a baseline style before the initial style recalculation, enabling fluid entrance animations for dynamic dialogs, popovers, and mini app drawer widgets without brittle JavaScript requestAnimationFrame timing hacks.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transitions Level 2 - Section 3 The @starting-style Rule
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines property values applied during the element's first style update before normal computed styles apply. When coupled with transition-behavior: allow-discrete, triggers smooth transitions immediately upon element rendering.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Eliminates visual flashes and jerky popups when super app host shell overlays or mini app modal components render dynamically.
detail.performance_and_security: Executed entirely on the GPU compositor thread without forcing synchronous JavaScript reflows or DOM layout thrashing.
detail.store_review_rule: Store static analyzers inspect mini app component stylesheets to ensure @starting-style rules include fallback visibility declarations for legacy WebView runtimes.

title: CSS transition-behavior Property & Discrete Value Animation Governance
description: Establishes normative standards for enabling transitions on discrete CSS properties using transition-behavior: allow-discrete. Traditionally, discrete properties like display and content-visibility flip instantly at 0% or 100% of duration; this property permits smooth transitions between none and visible values, synchronizing DOM removal with visual fade-out transitions.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transitions Level 2 - Section 2.1 The transition-behavior Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts 'normal' or 'allow-discrete'. When 'allow-discrete' is set on transition properties (e.g., transition: display 0.3s allow-discrete, opacity 0.3s), the element remains display: block until opacity transitions complete.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to cleanly animate exit transitions without requiring JavaScript setTimeout delays before removing elements or applying hidden classes.
detail.performance_and_security: Prevents race conditions between JavaScript DOM destruction and compositor animations, reducing stranded ghost DOM nodes.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app review validates that exit animations specify bounded durations (<= 500ms) to ensure responsive container interaction and prevent UI freezing.

title: CSS overlay Property & Top Layer Exit Animation Synchronization
description: Standardizes the CSS overlay property to transition elements into and out of the browser Top Layer. When dismissing a modal <dialog> or [popover], the overlay property transitions from 'auto' to 'none', keeping the element physically positioned in the Top Layer above all other content until outbound transition animations have fully completed.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transitions Level 2 - Section 2.2 The overlay Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Exposes values 'none' and 'auto'. Transitioning overlay with 'transition: overlay 0.3s allow-discrete' defers removal from the top layer stacking context until transition duration elapses.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures mini app payment confirmation sheets, biometric authorization dialogs, and native popovers do not prematurely drop below normal content during exit animations.
detail.performance_and_security: Guarantees top-layer security boundaries remain intact during animation, preventing clickjacking or UI redressing while an element is fading out.
detail.store_review_rule: Host security scanners verify that mini apps transitioning top layer dialogs do not stack non-dismissible transparent overlays that block user interaction.

title: W3C CSS Transitions Level 2 Standard & Compositor Animation Architecture
description: Defines the core architectural framework of W3C CSS Transitions Level 2, expanding CSS transition capabilities to discrete properties, event lifecycle hooks, and initial rendering states. This standard bridges declarative stylesheet animations with modern web component lifecycles, ensuring deterministic rendering performance across diverse mobile hardware.

detail.specification: W3C Working Draft - CSS Transitions Level 2
detail.technical_mechanics: Extends CSS transitions with transition-property, transition-duration, transition-timing-function, transition-delay, and transition-behavior syntax, defining reversing transition curves and style resolution phases.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides baseline compatibility requirements for super app WebView rendering engines across Android Chromium, iOS WebKit, and desktop runtimes.
detail.performance_and_security: Enforces compositor-friendly animation paths, discouraging expensive geometry re-layouts in favor of opacity and transform transitions.
detail.store_review_rule: Automated linter checks enforce adherence to CSS Transitions Level 2 syntax, flagging deprecated vendor prefixes and unoptimized layout triggers.

title: CSS display Property Animation & Layout Tree Boundary Governance
description: Standardizes the transition of the CSS display property between 'none' and rendered box states (block, flex, grid) when coupled with allow-discrete transitions. This standard eliminates the historical restriction that display could not participate in CSS transitions, establishing deterministic layout tree attachment and detachment points.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Display Module / CSS Transitions Level 2
detail.technical_mechanics: During a transition to 'none', display computes to 'none' only after all other transitioning properties have reached 100% completion; transitioning from 'none' takes effect immediately at start.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini app SPA view switchers and tab bars to animate transitions without leaving hidden views attached to the active layout tree, saving mobile memory.
detail.performance_and_security: Reduces layout thrashing by ensuring elements with display: none consume zero GPU layers and zero layout computation resources when inactive.
detail.store_review_rule: Store validation verifies that mini apps toggling display transitions do not trigger layout thrashing loops or retain memory-heavy offscreen subtrees.

title: W3C Picture-in-Picture API & Floating Video Sandboxing Architecture
description: Establishes normative standards for initiating and managing floating, always-on-top video playback via the W3C Picture-in-Picture API. This standard decouples video playback from the document viewport, allowing users to consume video content across other mini apps or system navigation while preserving host application security controls.

detail.specification: W3C Picture-in-Picture API - Working Draft
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines HTMLVideoElement.requestPictureInPicture(), Document.exitPictureInPicture(), and associated events. Operates an isolated system floating window with playback controls.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables seamless multi-tasking in super apps (e.g. video conferencing, live streaming commerce, sports) while users navigate mini app stores or chat screens.
detail.security_and_user_activation: Requires transient user activation (user gesture) to enter PiP; sandboxed iframes require explicit 'picture-in-picture' allow attribute in Permissions Policy.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review scanners inspect mini apps for unauthorized automated PiP popups and verify that video streams properly release hardware decoders upon exit.

title: HTMLVideoElement.requestPictureInPicture() Method & User Gesture Sandboxing
description: Standardizes programmatic initiation of Picture-in-Picture mode via HTMLVideoElement.requestPictureInPicture(). The method returns a Promise resolving to a PictureInPictureWindow instance, validating video readiness, codec support, and host container permissions before allocating a system-level floating surface.

detail.specification: W3C Picture-in-Picture API - Section 4 HTMLVideoElement Extensions
detail.technical_mechanics: Promise-based async invocation. Rejects with NotAllowedError if invoked without user activation, or InvalidStateError if video metadata has not loaded (readyState < HAVE_METADATA).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a consistent video detachment mechanism across custom video players, preventing proprietary native bridge bloat.
detail.security_and_user_activation: Strictly enforces user gesture gating to eliminate spammy popup windows. Only one element per document may occupy PiP mode simultaneously.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app review enforces proper error handling for Promise rejections, ensuring UI fallback controls remain fully functional if PiP is disabled by the host.

title: PictureInPictureWindow Interface & Adaptive Geometry Governance
description: Standardizes the inspection and dynamic tracking of floating video window dimensions via the PictureInPictureWindow interface. Exposing width, height, and the resize event, this interface allows mini apps to adjust video bitrate, aspect ratio, and UI overlay overlays in response to user window resizing.

detail.specification: W3C Picture-in-Picture API - Section 5 PictureInPictureWindow Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Read-only attributes width and height, alongside the 'resize' event listener. Dispatches events asynchronously when the user resizes the floating window.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini app adaptive video players to downsample high-resolution 4K streams to 720p/480p when placed in small floating windows, saving cellular bandwidth and battery.
detail.security_and_user_activation: Provides geometry telemetry without exposing user screen coordinates or underlying operating system window handles, preserving user privacy.
detail.store_review_rule: Review guidelines require video streaming mini apps to hook the resize event and optimize stream rendition ladders dynamically.

title: Document.exitPictureInPicture() Method & Window Teardown Lifecycle
description: Establishes normative standards for programmatically closing Picture-in-Picture windows via Document.exitPictureInPicture(). The method returns a Promise that resolves once the floating window has been dismissed and video playback is seamlessly re-docked into the host document layout.

detail.specification: W3C Picture-in-Picture API - Section 6 Document Extensions
detail.technical_mechanics: Asynchronously closes the active PiP window. Rejects with InvalidStateError if no video element is currently in PiP mode.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures that when a user navigates to a new mini app or completes a checkout flow, the host container can cleanly terminate or re-dock background floating videos.
detail.security_and_user_activation: Does not require user activation to close PiP, allowing automated teardown upon navigation, session timeout, or container backgrounding.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must register teardown hooks calling exitPictureInPicture() when unmounting video components to prevent orphaned floating video surfaces.

title: Document.pictureInPictureElement & State Inspection Telemetry
description: Standardizes runtime detection of active Picture-in-Picture sessions via Document.pictureInPictureElement and host feature availability via Document.pictureInPictureEnabled. These properties allow mini apps to audit active video detachment state and dynamically adjust player UI controls.

detail.specification: W3C Picture-in-Picture API - Section 6 Document Extensions (pictureInPictureElement & pictureInPictureEnabled)
detail.technical_mechanics: pictureInPictureElement returns the Element currently presented in PiP, or null. pictureInPictureEnabled returns a boolean indicating whether the feature is permitted by container policies.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables super app container shells to audit whether embedded third-party mini apps are currently monopolizing floating video layers.
detail.security_and_user_activation: Cross-origin iframes return null for pictureInPictureElement unless the iframe tree has received the 'picture-in-picture' Permissions Policy delegation.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review checks ensure mini apps verify pictureInPictureEnabled before rendering custom PiP trigger buttons, preventing broken UI elements.

title: StorageManager.estimate() Method & Origin Quota Telemetry
description: Standardizes programmatic retrieval of origin-scoped disk storage consumption and quota allocations via StorageManager.estimate(). The method returns a Promise resolving to a StorageEstimate object containing 'usage' and 'quota' metrics in bytes, allowing mini apps to monitor their local footprint across IndexedDB, Cache API, and OPFS.

detail.specification: WHATWG Storage Living Standard - Section 3.2 The StorageManager Interface (estimate)
detail.technical_mechanics: Returns Promise<StorageEstimate> with usage (bytes consumed) and quota (maximum byte allowance for origin). In some browsers, usageDetails breaks down consumption by subsystem (indexedDB, caches, serviceWorkerRegistrations).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides the essential telemetry hook for super app runtime dashboards and mini app client caches, allowing graceful proactive cleanup before hard quota errors occur.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents catastrophic write failures by allowing mini apps to throttle offline downloads when usage exceeds 80% of available origin quota.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing heavy offline storage (> 50MB) must query StorageManager.estimate() during initialization and log usage telemetry to prevent storage quota exhaustion.

title: StorageManager.persist() Method & Eviction Defense Request
description: Establishes normative standards for requesting durable storage persistence via StorageManager.persist(). By default, browser storage is 'best-effort', meaning the host OS or browser runtime may purge origin storage during disk space pressure. Calling persist() transitions the origin to 'persistent' storage, exempting critical local data from automated LRU eviction.

detail.specification: WHATWG Storage Living Standard - Section 3.2 The StorageManager Interface (persist)
detail.technical_mechanics: Returns Promise<boolean> resolving to true if persistence is granted, false if rejected. Runtime heuristics evaluate site engagement, bookmarking, or host container policy.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Critical for mission-critical mini apps such as offline POS terminals, enterprise banking ledgers, and secure messaging mini apps that cannot tolerate silent cache purging.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Protects IndexedDB records, OPFS databases, and Cache API assets from being purged when the device reaches low disk storage thresholds.
detail.store_review_rule: Store governance requires mini apps calling persist() to provide clear justification in their manifest, restricting durable grants to apps with verifiable offline utility.

title: StorageManager.persisted() Method & Persistence State Audit
description: Standardizes programmatic verification of current storage durability status via StorageManager.persisted(). The method returns a Promise resolving to a boolean indicating whether the current origin has been granted durable persistence, allowing mini apps to adapt data retention and sync strategies accordingly.

detail.specification: WHATWG Storage Living Standard - Section 3.2 The StorageManager Interface (persisted)
detail.technical_mechanics: Non-intrusive query returning Promise<boolean>. Unlike persist(), this method does not trigger permission prompts or user alerts.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables super app diagnostic modules to verify that approved enterprise mini apps have successfully retained their persistent storage tier.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: If persisted() returns false, the mini app knows it is operating in best-effort mode and must synchronize dirty transactional state to the cloud more frequently.
detail.store_review_rule: Store compliance testing verifies that mini apps audit persisted() status and implement graceful cloud fallback synchronizations when operating under best-effort storage.

title: StorageManager Interface & Unified Storage Architecture
description: Defines the core architectural framework of the StorageManager interface under the WHATWG Storage Living Standard. StorageManager centralizes quota management, storage persistence requests, and filesystem entry points (getDirectory) under a unified origin-bound object accessible via navigator.storage.

detail.specification: WHATWG Storage Living Standard - Section 3 Storage Architecture
detail.technical_mechanics: Binds estimate(), persist(), persisted(), and getDirectory() (for OPFS). Operates strictly within Secure Contexts (HTTPS / localhost).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a clean, unified capability layer for super app containers to enforce per-app storage budgets and prevent runaway disk usage across third-party tenants.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Structures client data into storage shelves, coordinating eviction policies across IndexedDB, Cache, Service Workers, and file systems under a single quota ceiling.
detail.store_review_rule: Automated security linters verify that mini apps do not bypass StorageManager by attempting to allocate unbounded LocalStorage or SessionStorage blocks.

title: Navigator.storage Property & Secure Context Gating
description: Establishes normative standards for accessing the singleton StorageManager instance via the Navigator.storage read-only property. The property is strictly gated to Secure Contexts, ensuring third-party mini app storage operations cannot be intercepted, manipulated, or sniffed over insecure network channels.

detail.specification: WHATWG Storage Living Standard - Section 3.1 Accessing Storage (Navigator.storage)
detail.technical_mechanics: Read-only property returning the StorageManager instance. Returns undefined in insecure contexts (non-HTTPS).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Guarantees that all mini app storage management APIs operate under secure cryptographic origin boundaries enforced by the super app host WebView.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Enables deterministic feature detection: 'storage' in navigator allows mini apps to safely degrade to in-memory caching if running in legacy or constrained environments.
detail.store_review_rule: Store submission gates enforce mandatory HTTPS for all mini app production bundle origins, ensuring navigator.storage is universally available and tamper-resistant.

title: CSS scrollbar-gutter Property & Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) Elimination
description: Standardizes the reservation of dedicated space for scrollbars via the scrollbar-gutter CSS property. By declaring scrollbar-gutter: stable (optionally with both-edges), mini apps prevent abrupt layout shifts and visual jitter when dynamic content causes scrollbars to appear or disappear, directly stabilizing Core Web Vitals (CLS) across mobile and desktop WebViews.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Overflow Module Level 4 / CSS Scrollbars Module Level 1
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts 'auto' | 'stable' | 'stable both-edges'. In 'stable' mode, the browser reserves gutter space along the relevant edge even when overflow does not necessitate a scrollbar, ensuring layout dimensions remain constant.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Prevents disruptive UI reflows in super app card lists, chat windows, and infinite-scrolling catalogs when async data loads into the viewport.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates repetitive synchronous layout recalculations and DOM element re-measuring triggered by sudden scrollbar insertion.
detail.store_review_rule: Store accessibility and performance audits verify that dynamic content containers utilize scrollbar-gutter: stable to enforce CLS scores <= 0.1.

title: CSS scrollbar-width Property & Mobile Screen Real-Estate Optimization
description: Establishes normative standards for configuring the physical thickness of scrollbars via the scrollbar-width property. Supporting 'auto', 'thin', and 'none', this standard eliminates bulky desktop scrollbars on compact mobile screens without resorting to non-standard, deprecated WebKit pseudo-elements.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Scrollbars Module Level 1 - Section 3 The scrollbar-width Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Configures scrollbar track width declaratively: 'thin' provides a slim, unobtrusive handle, while 'none' completely hides the visual scrollbar while preserving touch, mouse wheel, and programmatic scrolling capabilities.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to maximize visible horizontal and vertical screen space inside tight super app drawer panels and split-screen views.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Reduces visual clutter and GPU compositing layers associated with complex decorative scrollbar skins.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review rules require that when scrollbar-width: none is declared, the underlying container must retain accessible keyboard scrolling and visible scroll indicators when focused.

title: CSS scrollbar-color Property & Dark Mode Container Harmony
description: Standardizes the custom styling of scrollbar thumb and track colors using the scrollbar-color property. By accepting a pair of color values (<thumb-color> <track-color>) or 'auto', mini apps seamlessly adapt scrollbar palettes to host dark/light theme tokens without injecting intrusive CSS overrides.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Scrollbars Module Level 1 - Section 2 The scrollbar-color Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes two colors specifying the thumb (draggable handle) and track (background bar) respectively. Browsers enforce adequate contrast against container backgrounds.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures embedded mini apps maintain visual consistency with the super app host theme, preventing glaring white scrollbars in dark mode interfaces.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates memory overhead and parsing delays caused by thousands of lines of vendor-prefixed ::-webkit-scrollbar styling hacks.
detail.store_review_rule: Theme conformance checks verify that mini apps declare scrollbar-color using CSS custom properties linked to the host container theme tokens.

title: CSS overflow-clip-margin Property & Visual Ink Boundary Expansion
description: Standardizes the expansion of clipping boundaries on containers with overflow: clip using the overflow-clip-margin property. This allows ink overflow, box-shadows, and accessibility focus rings to extend cleanly beyond container bounds without establishing an unwanted scroll container or capturing scroll events.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Overflow Module Level 3 - Section 3.2 The overflow-clip-margin Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts <length> and optional reference box (content-box, padding-box, border-box). Allows content to visually spill over by the designated margin while maintaining clip behavior.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini app interactive cards and buttons to render high-contrast focus rings and subtle drop shadows without being awkwardly truncated by container edges.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Avoids the creation of scroll contexts, preserving browser rendering optimizations and preventing accidental scroll traps in nested UI hierarchies.
detail.store_review_rule: Accessibility linters ensure that mini apps clipping sub-components specify sufficient overflow-clip-margin to prevent WCAG focus indicators from being clipped.

title: CSS overflow Shorthand & Two-Axis Scroll Confinement Architecture
description: Defines the core architectural framework of the CSS overflow shorthand property for managing content spillover across horizontal and vertical axes. Supporting 'visible', 'hidden', 'clip', 'scroll', and 'auto', it establishes scroll containers, clipping boundaries, and formatting context roots essential for robust multi-tenant UI sandboxing.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Overflow Module Level 3 - Section 3 The overflow Shorthand
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts one or two values configuring overflow-x and overflow-y independently. Setting values other than 'visible' or 'clip' establishes a scroll container with an independent scrollport.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Acts as the fundamental barrier preventing mini app DOM elements from spilling outside assigned host WebView viewports or overlaying super app navigation headers.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Proper overflow scoping allows browser compositing engines to optimize paint invalidation areas, confining repaints strictly to the overflow boundaries.
detail.store_review_rule: Automated bundle review verifies that mini app root containers declare overflow: hidden or overflow: auto to guarantee strict layout sandboxing within the super app shell.

title: MediaStreamTrack.contentHint Property & Real-Time Codec Optimization
description: Standardizes the MediaStreamTrack.contentHint property under W3C Media Capture and Streams, allowing mini apps to provide normative hints ('motion', 'detail', 'text', 'speech', 'music') to underlying media encoders. This allows adaptive hardware encoders to optimize frame rate vs. resolution trade-offs dynamically without requiring custom WebRTC negotiation.

detail.specification: W3C Media Capture and Streams / MediaStreamTrack Content Hints
detail.technical_mechanics: Read/write string attribute on MediaStreamTrack. For video: 'motion' prioritizes smooth frame rates (e.g. video calling, sports), while 'detail' prioritizes high-resolution sharpness and text readability (e.g. document scanning, eKYC). For audio: 'speech' vs 'music'.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables super app mini apps (e.g., identity verification, document scanners, telemedicine, live video streaming) to dynamically signal encoder preferences to the host platform.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents bandwidth waste and CPU throttling by allowing encoders to downsample frame rate when sharpness is needed or compress resolution when fluid motion is prioritized.
detail.store_review_rule: Store guidelines mandate that mini apps handling document capture or text OCR set contentHint = 'detail' to ensure readable scans, while live commerce mini apps set contentHint = 'motion'.

title: MediaStreamTrack.applyConstraints() Method & Dynamic Hardware Reconfiguration
description: Establishes normative standards for dynamically adjusting camera and microphone hardware parameters via MediaStreamTrack.applyConstraints(). The method returns a Promise, allowing mini apps to alter resolution, frame rate, exposure, focus, and torch modes at runtime without tearing down active media pipelines or requesting new user permissions.

detail.specification: W3C Media Capture and Streams - Section 4.3.3.7 applyConstraints()
detail.technical_mechanics: Asynchronously applies a MediaTrackConstraints dictionary to an active track. Rejects with OverconstrainedError if mandatory 'exact' constraints cannot be satisfied by underlying hardware.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows seamless transitions in mini apps, such as switching from a low-power preview resolution to high-resolution snapshot mode during biometric capture or barcode scanning.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Enables runtime downscaling of video resolution and frame rate when host system thermal throttling or battery saver states are detected.
detail.store_review_rule: Store compliance tests verify that mini apps gracefully handle OverconstrainedError rejections and provide fallback constraints to prevent black camera viewfinders.

title: MediaStreamTrack.getSettings() Method & Hardware State Telemetry
description: Standardizes the retrieval of currently active hardware and pipeline configuration settings via MediaStreamTrack.getSettings(). Returning a MediaTrackSettings dictionary containing real-time width, height, frameRate, facingMode, deviceId, and channelCount, this method allows mini apps to inspect exact capture parameters.

detail.specification: W3C Media Capture and Streams - Section 4.3.3.6 getSettings()
detail.technical_mechanics: Synchronously returns the current operational settings of the track. If a property is not supported or not configured, it is omitted from the returned object.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables super app diagnostic engines to audit whether a mini app's video stream complies with container resolution limits and aspect ratios.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Provides telemetry data to detect hardware down-clocking or frame dropping under mobile device thermal pressure.
detail.store_review_rule: Store verification checks ensure mini apps verify facingMode ('user' vs 'environment') via getSettings() rather than assuming hardcoded camera placements.

title: MediaStreamTrack.getCapabilities() Method & Device Envelope Introspection
description: Standardizes the inspection of supported hardware ranges and capability boundaries via MediaStreamTrack.getCapabilities(). Returning a MediaTrackCapabilities object detailing min/max ranges for width, height, frameRate, aspect ratio, and supported facingModes, it enables mini apps to perform proactive constraint validation.

detail.specification: W3C Media Capture and Streams - Section 4.3.3.5 getCapabilities()
detail.technical_mechanics: Synchronously returns a capabilities dictionary exposing DoubleRange and LongRange envelopes for hardware parameters. Empty or restricted in non-secure or unprivileged contexts.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows the super app container to verify that third-party mini apps do not request unsupported video modes that crash native camera drivers.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Facilitates device tier profiling, allowing mini apps on budget smartphones to avoid requesting high-stress 60fps 4K video feeds.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review scanners verify that mini apps inspect getCapabilities() before invoking applyConstraints() with aggressive exact parameters.

title: MediaTrackConstraints Dictionary & Deterministic Hardware Negotiation
description: Defines the core architectural framework of the MediaTrackConstraints dictionary used across getUserMedia() and applyConstraints(). By establishing a strict dichotomy between mandatory exact constraints (ConstrainDoubleRange, ConstrainBoolean) and preferential ideal constraints, it provides deterministic media negotiation across heterogeneous mobile hardware.

detail.specification: W3C Media Capture and Streams - Section 4.3.4 MediaTrackConstraints
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines constraint sets with 'min', 'max', 'exact', and 'ideal' properties. 'exact' must be matched or cause rejection; 'ideal' guides the user agent's distance-metric algorithm to select the closest match.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides the foundational schema for super app permission dialogs and hardware capability allocation across third-party mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Recommends the use of 'ideal' over 'exact' constraints to ensure media streams remain resilient when running on resource-constrained or fragmented Android devices.
detail.store_review_rule: Store linters flag hardcoded 'exact' constraints on resolution and frameRate that frequently fail on entry-level smartphones, mandating 'ideal' fallbacks.

title: CanvasRenderingContext2D.measureText() Method & Zero-Reflow Text Layout
description: Standardizes programmatic text measurement via CanvasRenderingContext2D.measureText(). Returning a comprehensive TextMetrics object, this method enables mini apps to perform off-screen text layout, dynamic badge sizing, and canvas word wrapping without forcing expensive DOM layout recalulations or triggering browser reflows.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 4.12.5.1 The 2D rendering context (measureText)
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes a text string and returns a TextMetrics object reflecting current font, direction, letterSpacing, and wordSpacing context properties. Executes synchronously and deterministically in CPU/GPU memory.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables high-performance mini app charting, gaming, and custom UI components (e.g. data grids, POS receipt printers) to format multi-line text dynamically at 60fps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates DOM reflow thrashing caused by appending invisible measuring <span> elements into the document tree.
detail.store_review_rule: Store performance benchmarks verify that canvas-heavy mini apps use measureText() rather than DOM measurement techniques for dynamic canvas labeling.

title: TextMetrics Interface & Sub-Pixel Typographic Box Geometry
description: Defines the core architectural framework of the TextMetrics interface returned by measureText(). Beyond simple width, modern TextMetrics provides detailed typographic bounding box metrics including actualBoundingBoxAscent, actualBoundingBoxDescent, actualBoundingBoxLeft, actualBoundingBoxRight, fontBoundingBoxAscent, and fontBoundingBoxDescent for sub-pixel text alignment.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 4.12.5.1 The TextMetrics interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Read-only geometric attributes detailing the physical glyph bounds relative to the text baseline, enabling exact vertical centering and boundary clipping calculations.
