detail.superapp_container_relevance: Essential for mini app fintech graphics, digital signature pads, and QR/barcode overlays requiring pixel-perfect bounding box alignment without clipping diacritics.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Provides exact pixel dimensions to optimize backing canvas allocations, preventing excessive VRAM consumption from oversized canvas framebuffers.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps rendering complex international scripts (e.g. Vietnamese diacritics, Thai tone marks, Arabic ligatures) must utilize fontBoundingBox and actualBoundingBox metrics to avoid visual clipping.

title: CanvasRenderingContext2D.fontKerning Property & Glyphic Spacing Governance
description: Standardizes the programmatic control of font kerning pairs in 2D canvas text rendering via CanvasRenderingContext2D.fontKerning. Supporting 'auto', 'normal', and 'none', it allows mini apps to enable or disable font-defined kerning adjustments, ensuring visual consistency across mobile platforms and WebViews.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 4.12.5.1 Drawing text to the canvas (fontKerning)
detail.technical_mechanics: Configures whether kerning pairs built into OpenType/TrueType fonts are applied during fillText() and strokeText(). 'normal' enforces kerning; 'none' disables it to optimize layout speed.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures mini app e-commerce banners, branded typography, and receipts render with high typographic fidelity across Android and iOS host WebViews.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Allows high-throughput canvas engines (e.g. live financial tickers, real-time telemetry plots) to set fontKerning = 'none' to reduce glyph shaping computation under CPU load.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review verifies that high-precision mini app documents use fontKerning = 'normal' for legible branded typography and 'none' only when justified for real-time performance.

title: CanvasRenderingContext2D.letterSpacing Property & Declarative Spacing Parity
description: Standardizes letter spacing adjustments in 2D canvas text rendering using CanvasRenderingContext2D.letterSpacing. By accepting standard CSS length strings (e.g. '2px', '0.1em'), it eliminates manual string splitting and per-glyph drawing loops, bringing native CSS typography parity directly to the canvas rendering context.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 4.12.5.1 Drawing text to the canvas (letterSpacing)
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts CSS length strings configuring inter-character spacing. Applied automatically by the underlying text rasterizer during measureText(), fillText(), and strokeText().
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement modern design systems with loose or tight character spacing without executing expensive JavaScript manual glyph layout loops.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Reduces garbage collection pressure and CPU overhead by replacing custom multi-draw JavaScript kerning routines with a single native rasterization pass.
detail.store_review_rule: Store guidelines recommend using native letterSpacing rather than custom character iteration loops to maintain 60fps rendering in mini app canvas widgets.

title: CanvasRenderingContext2D.textRendering Property & Quality vs Performance Tradeoffs
description: Establishes normative standards for configuring text rendering hints via CanvasRenderingContext2D.textRendering. Offering 'auto', 'optimizeSpeed', 'optimizeLegibility', and 'geometricPrecision', it empowers mini apps to balance text rendering quality against mobile GPU/CPU battery and framerate budgets.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 4.12.5.1 Drawing text to the canvas (textRendering)
detail.technical_mechanics: Provides browser hints: 'optimizeLegibility' enables ligatures and kerning for crisp static text; 'optimizeSpeed' disables advanced typographic shaping for high-frequency dynamic rendering.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows super app mini apps to adapt text rasterization based on runtime mode—opting for speed during canvas scrolling/panning and switching to legibility during stationary display.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents mobile GPU thermal throttling during heavy animation frames by avoiding expensive sub-pixel glyph hinting passes.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app game developers and real-time dashboard builders must set textRendering = 'optimizeSpeed' during high-cadence animation loops to maintain container 60fps SLAs.

title: Worker Interface Constructor & Script Execution Sandboxing
description: Standardizes off-main-thread background task execution via the Worker interface (new Worker(scriptURL, options)). By creating an isolated background thread with its own event loop and memory space, mini apps can offload heavy business logic, cryptographic signing, and data processing without blocking host UI responsiveness or triggering ANR watchdogs.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 10 Web workers (The Worker interface)
detail.technical_mechanics: Instantiates a DedicatedWorker executing a distinct JavaScript script at the given same-origin URL or blob URL. Supports options dictionary specifying type: 'classic' or type: 'module', and credentials modes.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Prevents complex mini app calculations (e.g. e-commerce cart tax calculations, heavy data parsing, PDF parsing) from causing main thread frame drops or stutter in the super app container.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Container monitors background thread CPU consumption and enforces strict execution priority and thread count limits under host memory pressure.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps executing heavy synchronous calculations (>50ms continuous CPU blocking) must delegate processing to a Worker to meet 60fps frame budget certification.

title: Worker.postMessage() Structured Cloning & Memory Transfer Sandboxing
description: Establishes asynchronous message passing and memory ownership transfer between the host browsing context and dedicated background workers via Worker.postMessage(message, transfer). Enforces structured cloning boundaries and zero-copy Transferable object semantics (ArrayBuffer, MessagePort, ImageBitmap).

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 10.2 Dedicated workers and the Worker interface (postMessage)
detail.technical_mechanics: Serializes data across thread boundaries using the structured clone algorithm. When transfer array is provided, detaches buffer allocations from the caller context to achieve zero-copy memory transfer.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables ultra-fast transfer of biometric frames, cryptographic hashes, and large catalog indices between mini app UI contexts and worker threads without serialization latency.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Zero-copy transfer prevents heap ballooning and double-buffering OOM events on low-memory mobile devices.
detail.store_review_rule: Data payloads exceeding 1MB passed across worker boundaries must utilize Transferable objects rather than structured cloning to maintain memory thresholds.

title: DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope Execution Context & Security Boundary
description: Standardizes the dedicated worker global execution context (DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope, represented by self). Workers lack direct access to the DOM, window object, and parent document cookies, providing an isolated sandbox for processing untrusted or computationally expensive operations.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 10.2 Dedicated workers and the DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines worker global properties (name, close()) and events (message, messageerror). Inherits WorkerGlobalScope capabilities including IndexedDB, WebCrypto, and fetch while excluding DOM APIs.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides an architectural security barrier preventing background execution routines from tampering with the host super app DOM or injecting malicious scripts.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: DedicatedWorkerGlobalScope instances are isolated per mini app origin, ensuring that worker crashes or uncaught exceptions do not destabilize the host application.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must cleanly trap worker errors via onerror and messageerror handlers, preventing unhandled background rejections from propagating.

title: WorkerGlobalScope.importScripts() Synchronous Script Ingestion Sandboxing
description: Standardizes synchronous sub-script evaluation within classic workers via WorkerGlobalScope.importScripts(...urls). Governs same-origin restrictions, CSP script-src directives, and caching policies to prevent unauthorized remote code execution in background worker threads.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 10.3 The WorkerGlobalScope interface (importScripts)
detail.technical_mechanics: Synchronously fetches, compiles, and executes one or more scripts in the worker context. Bound by the worker's CSP and same-origin rules; network failures throw NetworkError DOMExceptions.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures that mini app background workers cannot bypass container CSP policies by dynamically fetching unauthorized third-party executables at runtime.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Scripts imported via importScripts must reside in the local mini app package bundle or adhere to strict CDN origin allowlists.
detail.store_review_rule: Store security pipelines verify that importScripts calls only reference package-bundled assets or approved enterprise CDNs, strictly prohibiting unpinned dynamic script URLs.

title: Worker.terminate() Deterministic Lifecycle Teardown & Resource Reclamation
description: Standardizes immediate worker thread destruction via Worker.terminate(). Provides container and parent contexts with an imperative mechanism to abort runaway background tasks, free native thread handles, and reclaim dedicated heap memory upon mini app navigation or background freezing.

detail.specification: HTML Living Standard - Section 10.2 Dedicated workers and the Worker interface (terminate)
detail.technical_mechanics: Immediately terminates the worker thread and discards pending microtasks and event loop queues. Frees all associated V8/JavaScriptCore contexts and native thread handles.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables the super app container to cleanly terminate worker execution when a mini app is closed or navigated away, preventing background zombie processes from draining mobile battery.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Under OS low-memory or thermal throttling, container host can forcefully invoke terminate() on background mini app workers to protect core app stability.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app lifecycle handlers (e.g. onDestroy, onHide) must invoke worker.terminate() for all active worker instances to eliminate memory leaks.

title: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 & 3D Spatial Rendering Architecture
description: Establishes the normative framework for 3D coordinate space rendering and perspective transformations in modern web and WebView layouts via the W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2. Defines 4x4 transformation matrices, local coordinate systems, and hardware-accelerated composition layers for mobile devices.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 Recommendation / Candidate Recommendation
detail.technical_mechanics: Extends 2D transforms with 3D affine transforms (translate3d, scale3d, rotate3d, matrix3d). Establishes 3D rendering contexts where elements share a common spatial coordinate system.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to build interactive card flips, 3D product carousels, and spatial transitions accelerated by mobile GPU hardware without dropping frames.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Promotes 3D transformed elements to dedicated compositor layers; container monitors layer counts to prevent excessive mobile VRAM consumption.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must avoid creating deep hierarchies of 3D transformed containers that trigger excessive GPU backing surface allocations.

title: CSS transform-style Property & 3D Rendering Context Hierarchies
description: Standardizes child element spatial positioning within 3D rendering contexts via the CSS transform-style property ('flat' vs 'preserve-3d'). Governs whether nested DOM elements participate in the parent 3D scene or are flattened into a single 2D plane.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 - Section 3 The transform-style Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Setting transform-style: preserve-3d establishes a 3D rendering context where descendants maintain independent z-axis positions and intersect accurately in 3D space.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides architectural containment ensuring that complex mini app 3D card deck animations do not leak spatial coordinates into super app host navigation bars.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents unintended z-buffer fighting and GPU layer proliferation by strictly containing 3D contexts within designated mini app widget boundaries.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review ensures preserve-3d is scoped only to interactive visual components and not declared on root body/html containers.

title: CSS perspective Property & 3D Depth Perception Standardization
description: Standardizes the viewing distance between the z=0 plane and the user viewport via the CSS perspective property. Controls the intensity of the 3D foreshortening effect, ensuring consistent visual depth across varying mobile screen physical densities.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 - Section 2 The perspective Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts length values (e.g. 500px, 1000px) or 'none'. Applies a perspective projection matrix to child elements, scaling visual size proportionally to distance along the z-axis.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures that promotional 3D banners, interactive vouchers, and product packaging views render with realistic, distortion-free perspective across diverse device sizes.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Hardware rasterizer computes perspective transformations in vertex shaders, maintaining 60fps throughput without CPU recalculations.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing 3D perspectives must declare values >= 300px to prevent visual distortion and disorientation on small mobile displays.

title: CSS perspective-origin Property & Vanishing Point Alignment
description: Standardizes the vanishing point coordinate alignment for 3D perspective projections via the CSS perspective-origin property. Governs the exact x/y observer vantage point, ensuring seamless visual integration with host viewport centerlines.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 - Section 2.1 The perspective-origin Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts one or two length/percentage values representing the horizontal and vertical position of the perspective vanishing point (default: 50% 50%).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to align their 3D interactive graphics with dynamic mobile UI anchors (e.g. bottom navigation sheets or top status bars) without visual misalignment.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates layout shifts by allowing perspective vanishing points to adapt smoothly during device orientation changes.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must ensure perspective-origin values adapt correctly across both portrait and landscape viewport orientations.

title: CSS backface-visibility Property & GPU Backface Culling Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the display and rendering behavior of the reverse side of 3D transformed elements via the CSS backface-visibility property ('visible' vs 'hidden'). Provides native GPU backface culling to eliminate redundant rasterization passes during two-sided flip card transitions.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Transforms Module Level 2 - Section 4 The backface-visibility Property
detail.technical_mechanics: When set to 'hidden', the element is culled by the GPU rasterizer whenever its front face is rotated away from the viewer, preventing rendering of mirror-reversed content.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Crucial for mini app banking card flips, scratchcard games, and interactive loyalty vouchers where front and back content must be decoupled without visual bleeding.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Reduces GPU fill rate pressure by eliminating pixel shading passes for hidden backfaces during complex rotation animations.
detail.store_review_rule: Two-sided flipping components in mini apps must set backface-visibility: hidden on both card faces to prevent visual artifacting and GPU overdraw.

title: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 & Visual Clipping Architecture
description: Establishes the normative framework for partial or complete hiding of visual elements using clipping paths and masking images via the W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1. Defines standardized compositing models for vector geometry clipping and alpha/luminance raster masking across modern WebViews.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 W3C Recommendation
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines CSS properties for clipping (clip-path, clip-rule) and masking (mask-image, mask-mode, mask-repeat, mask-position, mask-clip, mask-origin, mask-size, mask-composite). Operates at the compositor level.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement complex circular avatar cutouts, rounded card carousels, and shaped promotional banners with native GPU efficiency.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates memory-heavy PNG alpha cutout overlays by performing mathematical vector clipping directly in the GPU rendering pipeline.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must utilize CSS masking and clipping rather than heavy full-screen bitmap alpha overlays to minimize memory consumption.

title: CSS clip-path Property & Basic Shape Vector Clipping Sandboxing
description: Standardizes geometric element clipping boundaries via the CSS clip-path property. Supports basic shapes (circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), path(), inset()) and external SVG clipping paths (<clipPath>) to restrict element painting and hit-testing to explicit geometric perimeters.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 - Section 3 Clipping Paths: the clip-path property
detail.technical_mechanics: Clips the element to the specified path or shape. Areas outside the clipping region are transparent and do not dispatch pointer events or intercept user touches.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides robust containment preventing mini app decorative banners from spilling outside designated card bounds and interfering with host touch targets.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Because clip-path restricts pointer event hit-testing to the clipped shape, it eliminates invisible transparent DOM elements from intercepting touch gestures.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app interactive elements that use custom non-rectangular bounds must apply clip-path to ensure hit-testing precisely matches visible geometry.

title: CSS mask-image Property & Alpha/Luminance Mask Layering
description: Standardizes raster and gradient masking of DOM elements via the CSS mask-image property. Allows mini apps to define complex transparency gradients and feathered edges using CSS linear-gradient, radial-gradient, or external SVG/PNG mask sources.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 - Section 4 Masking: the mask-image property
detail.technical_mechanics: Applies a mask layer image where the alpha channel (or luminance) modulates element opacity. Supports multiple mask layers combined via mask-composite.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement smooth horizontal scroll fade-out gradients and feathered card transitions matching super app native design tokens.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Using CSS gradient masks avoids downloading external transparent PNG assets, reducing mobile network usage and asset cache footprints.
detail.store_review_rule: Scrollable mini app lists requiring edge fading must utilize CSS mask-image linear gradients rather than floating absolute DOM overlay strips.

title: CSS mask-size Property & Mask Image Proportional Scaling
description: Standardizes the sizing and scaling behavior of mask layer images via the CSS mask-size property. Supporting keywords ('contain', 'cover') and explicit length/percentage dimensions, it ensures mask imagery scales proportionally across diverse mobile viewport aspect ratios.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 - Section 4.5 Sizing Mask Image: the mask-size property
detail.technical_mechanics: Specifies the dimensions of the mask painting area, scaling mask-image assets in alignment with background-size syntax and conventions.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Guarantees that decorative brand cutouts and themed voucher masks maintain exact visual proportions across varying smartphone display dimensions.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Vector mask scaling prevents texture re-allocation and avoids GPU bitmap resampling artifacts on high-DPI retina screens.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps using image-based masks must explicitly define mask-size to prevent unintended mask repetition or clipping on wide mobile displays.

title: CSS mask-composite Property & Multi-Layer Mask Compositing
description: Standardizes multi-layer mask compositing and Boolean operations via the CSS mask-composite property. Supporting Porter-Duff compositing operators ('add', 'subtract', 'intersect', 'exclude'), it allows developers to combine multiple mask layers into intricate compound clipping geometries.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Masking Module Level 1 - Section 4.8 Composite Mask Layers: the mask-composite property
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines how each mask layer is combined with the layers below it using Porter-Duff source-over, source-in, source-out, and XOR compositing algorithms.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to create advanced visual punch-outs (e.g. ticket stubs with circular cutout notches and translucent body regions) without requiring complex canvas rendering.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Executed directly in the GPU compositor pipeline, eliminating costly CPU canvas 2D pixel manipulation loops for compound shapes.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps creating compound ticket or voucher geometries must use CSS mask-composite rather than JavaScript canvas rendering to ensure optimal 60fps scrolling.

title: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 1 & Hardware-Accelerated Filter Processing Pipeline
description: Standardizes the visual processing pipeline for applying graphical operations (blur, color shifts, contrast, shadows) directly to rendered elements before compositing. Filter effects process elements as off-screen bitmap buffers, applying directed acyclic filter graphs and hardware-accelerated shaders before final display presentation.

detail.specification: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 1 - Section 1 Introduction & Processing Model
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines filter primitives and shorthand filter functions that operate on an off-screen bitmap surface. The user agent rasterizes the target element and its subtrees into an off-screen texture, evaluates filter operations sequentially via GPU fragment shaders, and composites the final filtered texture into the target stacking context.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides mini apps with native, 60fps declarative visual styling for status badges, deactivated UI cards, and dynamic visual state shifts without manual canvas pixel manipulation or external image assets.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents runaway GPU texture allocation during thermal pressure by allowing the super app container to clamp filter graph complexity, cap blur radii, or degrade non-essential filters to simple opacity shifts under low memory conditions.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must avoid deep chaining of multiple heavy filter functions (such as multiple blurs or large drop-shadows) on frequently scrolling container elements to avoid dropping frame rates below 60fps.

title: CSS filter Property & Declarative Visual Post-Processing Shaders
description: Standardizes the CSS filter property allowing developers to apply one or more visual post-processing effects—such as grayscale(), sepia(), saturate(), hue-rotate(), invert(), opacity(), brightness(), contrast(), blur(), and drop-shadow()—to an element and all of its descendants.

detail.specification: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 1 - Section 2 The filter Property
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts a list of filter functions or SVG filter references. When specified, the element establishes a stacking context and a containing block for absolute and fixed positioned descendants, rendering into an isolated off-screen compositor layer before blending.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables instant UI theming, inactive disabled states for mini app checkout buttons, and dynamic visual feedback without triggering DOM tree re-renders or additional network asset fetches.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Because elements with CSS filters create dedicated compositor layers, excessive concurrent filtered elements can exhaust GPU VRAM; super app runtime monitors container layer count and disables filters on hidden subtrees.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must not apply animated CSS filters to full-screen root elements during continuous gestures; animations should target transform and opacity to maintain hardware compositor acceleration.

title: CSS backdrop-filter Property & Host Glassmorphism / Modal Layer Isolation
description: Standardizes the CSS backdrop-filter property, which applies graphical effects (such as Gaussian blurring or color tinting) to the area immediately behind an element rather than to the element's own foreground contents.

detail.specification: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 2 - Section 3 The backdrop-filter Property
detail.technical_mechanics: The browser reads back the rendered pixels of all elements situated beneath the target element within the same stacking context, copies them to an auxiliary scratch texture, executes the specified filter functions via GPU fragment shaders, and composites the filtered background underneath the element's own semi-transparent background and foreground children.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Critical for super app top-layer dialogs, floating action sheets, bottom navigation bars, and host security capsules to establish premium glassmorphic visual separation without obscuring host context.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Backdrop read-backs require GPU-to-CPU roundtrips or multi-pass texture sampling; under severe battery or thermal pressure (W3C Compute Pressure 'critical'), the super app container falls back to solid background colors.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing backdrop-filter on modal dialogs must provide a solid fallback background color via @supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(10px)) to maintain WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios on legacy WebViews.

title: CSS blur() Filter Function & Privacy-Preserving Background Content Obfuscation
description: Standardizes the blur() CSS filter function, which calculates an off-screen Gaussian blur convolution across an element's bitmap using a specified pixel radius length, smoothly dispersing pixel color values across neighboring coordinates.

detail.specification: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 1 - Section 4 Filter Functions: blur()
detail.technical_mechanics: Executes a two-pass separable Gaussian blur (horizontal then vertical 1D convolutions) over the rasterized buffer. Pixels outside the boundary are sampled according to edge clamp policies, with computational cost scaling linearly with radius unless hardware downsampling is employed.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables instant privacy obfuscation of sensitive financial balances, eKYC ID photo previews, and confidential account numbers during app switching, backgrounding, or when sensitive authorization prompts are triggered.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Large blur radii (>20px) on large viewport areas induce heavy GPU fill rate load; the store runtime enforces a maximum radius recommendation of 16px for interactive elements.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps handling financial or personal identity data must implement blur() masking or equivalent privacy shields on background view transitions to prevent shoulder surfing and OS task switcher data leaks.

title: CSS drop-shadow() Filter Function & Compositor-Level Elevation Rendering
description: Standardizes the drop-shadow() CSS filter function, which projects a blurred, offset silhouette of an element's exact alpha mask (including transparent PNG contours, SVG paths, and text glyphs), contrasting with rectangular box-shadow.

detail.specification: W3C Filter Effects Module Level 1 - Section 4 Filter Functions: drop-shadow()
detail.technical_mechanics: Extracts the alpha channel of the rendered element, tints it with the specified color, shifts it along the x and y axes, applies a Gaussian blur, and composites the resulting shadow layer behind the original element before stacking.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides realistic elevation and physical depth for non-rectangular mini app components, such as circular floating action buttons, custom badge pins, and transparent PNG merchandise previews.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Renders efficiently within GPU raster pipelines without invalidating DOM layout trees, eliminating layout recalculation overhead compared to complex nested container box-shadows.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must utilize drop-shadow() for transparent and irregular vector icons instead of hacking multiple nested box-shadow elements, preserving clean DOM hierarchy and rendering performance.

title: WHATWG HTML Constraint Validation API & Declarative Form Security Pipeline
description: Standardizes the browser-native client-side form validation infrastructure defined by the WHATWG HTML Living Standard. Provides declarative validation attributes (required, pattern, minlength, maxlength, min, max, step, type) and programmatic evaluation algorithms that intercept form submission before network transmission.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 4.10.21 Constraint Validation
detail.technical_mechanics: Each submittable form control implements validation subroutines that automatically compute candidate status against declarative constraints whenever the control's value mutates, preventing invalid forms from firing submit events.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Guarantees that mini app checkout forms, user profile inputs, and authentication prompts enforce syntactic and semantic correctness before invoking host payment bridges or backend API endpoints.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Executes entirely in the local browser layout engine with zero network latency, minimal memory allocation, and zero reliance on heavy third-party JavaScript validation libraries.
detail.store_review_rule: All mini app input forms submitting financial, personal, or transactional data must utilize standard HTML constraint validation attributes to ensure predictable baseline data hygiene and native accessibility.

title: HTML Constraint Validation Architecture & Client-Side Form Integrity Hygiene
description: Standardizes the end-to-end architecture of client-side form validation, combining declarative markup constraints, pseudo-classes (:valid, :invalid, :user-invalid, :required), and programmatic JavaScript APIs to maintain transactional data hygiene.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard & MDN Web Docs Constraint Validation Architectural Guide
detail.technical_mechanics: Establishes a dual-layer validation model: the rendering engine binds CSS pseudo-classes dynamically for real-time visual feedback, while the script engine exposes the ValidityState interface and validation methods for transactional checks.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Prevents malformed data ingestion, SQL/XSS injection payload attempts at form boundaries, and eliminates broken transactions across host-to-mini-app bridge boundaries.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Lightweight, event-driven validation operates with near-zero memory footprint and avoids CPU spikes during rapid keystroke entries.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must not disable native form validation (via form novalidate) without implementing equivalent programmatic checkValidity() enforcement prior to host bridge checkout invocations.

title: ValidityState Interface & Granular Form Error Boolean Taxonomy
description: Standardizes the ValidityState read-only interface representing the validation state of an input element. Exposes a strongly-typed boolean taxonomy (valueMissing, typeMismatch, patternMismatch, tooLong, tooShort, rangeUnderflow, rangeOverflow, stepMismatch, badInput, customError, valid).

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 4.10.21.2 The ValidityState interface
detail.technical_mechanics: An immutable property bag returned by element.validity. Each boolean attribute is deterministically calculated by the engine based on current control value, configured constraints, and custom error strings.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows super app mini apps to precisely diagnose validation failures and provide localized, context-aware error handling for phone numbers, national IDs, and currency amounts without string parsing.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Allocates a single lightweight internal C++ state struct per form control, guaranteeing negligible memory overhead even on complex multi-step application forms.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must query specific validity flags (e.g., validity.valueMissing vs validity.patternMismatch) to present clear, assistive guidance rather than generic 'invalid form' alerts.

title: HTMLInputElement.checkValidity() & Programmatic Form Validation Contracts
description: Standardizes the checkValidity() and reportValidity() methods on HTML form controls and HTMLFormElement. checkValidity() returns a boolean indicating whether constraints are met and fires a cancelable 'invalid' event if false, while reportValidity() also renders native error bubbles.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 4.10.21.3 Constraint validation methods
detail.technical_mechanics: Invokes the constraint validation algorithm on the element or form. If invalid, dispatches a trusted, cancelable 'invalid' DOM event to the target element; reportValidity() additionally scrolls the first invalid control into view and renders the browser's native error bubble.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement programmatic validation gates at multi-step wizard transitions and immediately before triggering native payment sheet bridges.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Runs synchronously without heap allocations, allowing seamless execution inside high-frequency touch event handlers.
detail.store_review_rule: Prior to invoking super app payment or authentication bridge APIs (e.g. host.requestPayment), mini apps must execute form.checkValidity() and abort if false, preventing unvalidated transaction submissions.

title: HTMLInputElement.setCustomValidity() & Localized Dynamic Error Messaging
description: Standardizes the setCustomValidity() method, allowing developers to set a custom validation error message on a form control. Setting a non-empty string marks the control as invalid (validity.customError = true), while an empty string clears the error condition.

detail.specification: WHATWG HTML Living Standard - Section 4.10.21.3 The setCustomValidity() method
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes a string argument representing the localized validation message. If the string is non-empty, sets customError to true, valid to false, and records the validationMessage for display in native UI bubbles and accessibility trees.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to integrate complex business logic validation (e.g. bank account checksums, real-time voucher code validation) directly into the native browser validation lifecycle.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Internal string storage replaces expensive custom error popup DOM nodes, preserving memory and preventing DOM tree bloat.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must reset custom validity messages (setCustomValidity('')) as soon as the user corrects the input to avoid permanently blocking form submission.

title: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 & Continuous Multi-Column Flow
description: Standardizes the CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1, introducing multi-column containers that break continuous content into multiple parallel vertical columns. Content flows effortlessly across columns, maintaining optimal typographic line lengths across variable mobile and tablet viewport widths.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 - Section 1 Introduction
detail.technical_mechanics: A multi-column container establishes a new block formatting context. Content flows sequentially from one column box to the next, with column heights balanced automatically by the browser layout engine.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps displaying editorial, catalog, or long-form documentation content to format text into readable magazine-style columns on foldable and tablet devices without JavaScript pagination.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Native multi-column layout is computed during the normal block layout pass without requiring JavaScript DOM splitting or secondary reflow cycles.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps presenting long-form terms of service, product manuals, or articles must utilize native CSS multicol rather than custom JavaScript DOM slicing to ensure fluid scrolling performance.

title: CSS Multi-column Layout Architecture & Dynamic Fragmentation Formatting
description: Standardizes the architectural principles of multi-column layout, including fragmentation boundaries, column box generation, margin collapsing within columns, and responsive flow adaptation.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 & MDN Web Docs Multi-column Layout Guide
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines how anonymous column boxes are generated between the multi-column container and its children. Establishes fragmentation rules where block elements break across columns without breaking inline semantics.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a robust layout primitive for mini app newsfeeds, product spec sheets, and responsive dashboards across diverse screen sizes.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Avoids memory-intensive virtual DOM pagination components, offloading column balancing entirely to optimized native browser layout engines.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must verify that break-inside: avoid is applied to critical interactive elements (such as buttons or cards) within multicol containers to prevent unnatural splitting across columns.

title: CSS column-count, column-width & Shorthand Dynamic Column Calculation
description: Standardizes the column-count, column-width, and columns shorthand properties, governing how the number and width of columns are dynamically computed based on available container width.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 - Section 3 The Number and Width of Columns
detail.technical_mechanics: When column-width is specified, the user agent creates as many columns of at least that width as can fit within the container. When combined with column-count in the columns shorthand, column-count acts as a maximum ceiling.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables completely responsive mini app content layouts that seamlessly transition from 1 column on compact mobile phones to 2-3 columns on foldables and tablets without media queries.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Zero JavaScript resize listeners required, eliminating CPU event-handling spikes when rotating mobile devices or unfolding dual-screen devices.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app developers should prefer using the columns shorthand with an optimal column-width (e.g. columns: 20rem) to guarantee readability across all super app device form factors.

title: CSS column-gap & column-rule Properties: Separation and Visual Boundaries
description: Standardizes column-gap and column-rule properties (column-rule-color, column-rule-style, column-rule-width) for multi-column containers, controlling spatial separation and vertical divider lines between columns.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 - Section 4 Column Gaps and Rules
detail.technical_mechanics: column-gap specifies the spacing between adjacent column boxes. column-rule paints a border-like vertical divider in the center of the column gap without altering layout dimensions or taking up additional space.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to create crisp, themeable visual borders and structured column spacing aligned with super app host design systems and color tokens.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Painted directly during the border drawing phase; does not trigger reflow or create extra DOM elements like artificial <hr> divider tags.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must use column-gap and column-rule for column partitioning rather than injecting custom divider divs, ensuring clean DOM structure and full accessibility compatibility.

title: CSS column-span Property & Full-Width Interstitial Heading Layout
description: Standardizes the column-span property (column-span: all), allowing an element inside a multi-column container to span across all column tracks, temporarily interrupting column flow and establishing a full-width break.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Multi-column Layout Module Level 1 - Section 5 Spanning Columns
detail.technical_mechanics: When an element has column-span: all, it spans all columns of the multicol container. Content preceding the spanning element is balanced across columns before the element, and subsequent content resumes multi-column flow below it.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to embed full-width promotional banners, section headings, or interactive callouts within multi-column catalog feeds without splitting the container into multiple separate DOM elements.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Handled natively within the layout fragmentation engine without requiring complex Flexbox/Grid DOM wrappers or JavaScript positioning.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing column-span: all must ensure the spanning element does not introduce vertical layout shifts during asynchronous content loading.

title: W3C CSS @counter-style At-Rule: Custom Numbering System Architecture
description: Standardizes the CSS @counter-style at-rule, allowing mini app developers to define custom counter styles for ordered lists, procedural steppers, and multi-lingual catalog indexes without injecting bespoke JavaScript numbering routines.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Counter Styles Level 3 - Section 2 Defining Custom Counter Styles: the @counter-style rule
detail.technical_mechanics: The @counter-style at-rule creates a named counter style accessible via list-style-type and counter() / counters() functions. It specifies algorithm rules, symbols, prefixes, suffixes, ranges, and fallback strategies interpreted natively by browser styling engines.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps running in global or multi-lingual super apps (e.g. Arabic, Southeast Asian, East Asian locales) to format checkout steps, order tracking, and terms clauses using localized indigenous numeral systems natively.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Computed off-thread by the CSS layout engine; eliminates redundant JavaScript localization formatters and regex replacements on list DOM trees.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps serving localized regional catalogs must define regional counter styles via declarative @counter-style rules rather than mutating DOM node textContent in JavaScript.

title: CSS counter-style system Descriptor: Algorithmic Conversion Taxonomy
description: Standardizes the system descriptor within @counter-style, defining algorithmic conversion mechanisms including cyclic, numeric, alphabetic, symbolic, additive, and fixed numbering sequences.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Counter Styles Level 3 - Section 3 Counter Algorithms: the system descriptor
detail.technical_mechanics: Specifies how integer counter values map to representation glyphs. For instance, 'cyclic' repeats symbols infinitely, 'numeric' interprets symbols as positional digits in a base-N system, and 'alphabetic' mimics spreadsheet-style indexing (A-Z, AA-AZ).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides standardized stepping logic for mini app breadcrumbs, multi-stage KYC identity verification steppers, and tiered loyalty reward progressions.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Algorithm execution is zero-allocation C++ code within browser layout engines, preventing garbage collection stalls during massive list rendering.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must configure an appropriate system descriptor (such as numeric or additive) conforming to ISO/IEC language locale conventions for official regional stores.

title: CSS counter-style symbols Descriptor: Glyphic Marker Definition
description: Standardizes the symbols descriptor within @counter-style, specifying space-separated strings or image tokens used to construct marker representations for positional and cyclic systems.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Counter Styles Level 3 - Section 4 Specifying Symbols: the symbols and additive-symbols descriptors
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines an ordered sequence of Unicode character symbols or string literals used by the counter algorithm. For positional numeric systems, at least two symbols are mandatory to construct base systems.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to implement custom brand-aligned icon markers, emoji bullets, or Southeast Asian script numerals (e.g. Lao, Khmer, Thai) in list-based product guides.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Symbols are cached in the style engine dictionary; re-rendering list items reuses pre-parsed symbol handles without DOM reallocation.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing custom font glyphs in symbols must verify webfont availability or provide standard Unicode fallback symbols to prevent unreadable empty box glyphs (tofu).

title: CSS counter-style additive-symbols Descriptor: Roman & Classical Numerals
description: Standardizes the additive-symbols descriptor for additive numbering systems (such as Roman numerals, Armenian, or classical Chinese counting systems), mapping integer weights to symbol representations.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Counter Styles Level 3 - Section 4.2 The additive-symbols descriptor
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts a list of additive tuple pairs (<integer> <symbol>) ordered strictly by descending numeric weight. The algorithm greedily extracts the largest weight until the value reaches zero.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Essential for mini app financial agreements, leasing contracts, statutory disclosure documents, and legal terms requiring Roman numeral clause enumerations (I, II, III, IV...).
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Zero memory overhead compared to bundling third-party Roman numeral conversion npm libraries into mini app packages.
detail.store_review_rule: Legal and regulatory mini apps formatting statutory contract clauses must utilize native CSS additive-symbols instead of client-side JavaScript formatting libraries to minimize package bundle size.

title: CSS counter-style fallback Descriptor: Resilient Out-of-Range Recovery
description: Standardizes the fallback descriptor within @counter-style, specifying a secondary counter style applied when a counter value falls outside the defined range or cannot be represented by the system.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Counter Styles Level 3 - Section 5 Fallbacks: the fallback descriptor
detail.technical_mechanics: Specifies another valid counter style name (defaulting to 'decimal'). If the current style cannot render the integer (e.g. negative numbers in an alphabetic system), the browser cascades to the fallback style without erroring.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Guarantees graceful degradation in mini apps displaying infinite scroll lists, dynamic chat threads, or pagination sequences exceeding anticipated numeral ranges.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Prevents silent layout breaks or NaN text display when user list collections grow unexpectedly large under heavy usage.
detail.store_review_rule: Every custom @counter-style declared in mini apps must specify an explicit, robust fallback (such as decimal) to maintain accessibility across out-of-range counter increments.

title: W3C CSS Custom Highlight API: Highlight Interface & Range Encapsulation
description: Standardizes the Highlight interface in the CSS Custom Highlight API Level 1, allowing mini app scripts to programmatically style arbitrary DOM Range objects without modifying DOM tree structure or injecting span tags.

detail.specification: CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1 - Section 2 The Highlight Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: A Highlight object is an iterable collection of AbstractRange / Range instances. Adding or removing ranges immediately updates the visual presentation during subsequent painting passes without invalidating the DOM or triggering layout reflow.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables high-performance in-page search highlighting, syntax colorization, and collaborative text annotation in mini apps without disrupting DOM selection, event listeners, or accessibility trees.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Eliminates heavy DOM manipulation overhead (like wrapping search hits in <mark> or <span class='highlight'> elements), preserving 60fps responsiveness during real-time filtering.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps providing in-page document search or real-time catalog filtering must use the CSS Custom Highlight API where supported rather than mutating DOM structures with wrapper elements.

title: HighlightRegistry Interface: Centralized Highlight Map Coordination
description: Standardizes the HighlightRegistry interface, providing a map-like dictionary (CSS.highlights) that maps custom highlight identifiers to Highlight objects across the document.

detail.specification: CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1 - Section 3 The HighlightRegistry Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: HighlightRegistry implements standard Map methods (set, get, has, delete, clear). Assigning a Highlight to a name (e.g. CSS.highlights.set('search-results', highlight)) registers it for styling under ::highlight(search-results).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows super app host containers and guest mini apps to maintain separate, non-colliding highlight layers (e.g. host security warnings vs mini app content annotations) in a unified registry.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Highlights can be cleared atomically via CSS.highlights.delete() or clear(), immediately freeing Range object memory without DOM clean-up traversal.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must register scoped highlight names prefixed with mini app namespaces to prevent colliding with super app host ambient highlight registries.

title: CSS ::highlight() Pseudo-Element: Declarative Highlight Styling Sandbox
description: Standardizes the ::highlight() pseudo-element, enabling CSS rules to declaratively style custom highlights (color, background-color, text-decoration) independently of document hierarchy.

detail.specification: CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1 - Section 4 Styling Highlights: the ::highlight() pseudo-element
detail.technical_mechanics: Applies styling to ranges registered in the HighlightRegistry matching the argument name (e.g. ::highlight(search-result) { background-color: yellow; color: black; }). Only text-level properties are permitted, preventing accidental layout reflow.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides sandboxed visual formatting for mini app legal contracts, document viewers, and chat message search matching without permitting dangerous style mutations that disrupt page layout.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Styles are applied purely in the rendering paint phase, bypassing layout and style recalculation bottlenecks.
detail.store_review_rule: Custom highlight styling in mini apps must adhere to WCAG 2.2 AA contrast ratios between highlighted text color and highlight background colors.

title: CSS.highlights Property: Static Global Entry Point & Feature Gating
description: Standardizes the static CSS.highlights property on the global CSS namespace, serving as the canonical entry point and runtime feature check for highlight capabilities.

detail.specification: CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1 - Section 3.1 The CSS namespace
detail.technical_mechanics: The CSS.highlights property returns the HighlightRegistry instance associated with the current document. Checking ('highlights' in CSS) provides a reliable, synchronous feature detection test.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps running in diverse WebView engines (Chromium, Safari WebKit, Gecko) to gracefully detect Highlight API support and fall back cleanly when running on older container kernels.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Single global accessor instance per document; zero memory cost when inactive.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing custom highlights must verify ('highlights' in CSS) prior to invocation, providing graceful fallback highlighting mechanisms for legacy container WebViews.

title: Highlight.priority Property: Multi-Layer Overlap Conflict Resolution
description: Standardizes the priority property on the Highlight interface, enabling deterministic visual layering and conflict resolution when multiple custom highlights overlap the same text ranges.

detail.specification: CSS Custom Highlight API Module Level 1 - Section 2.1 Highlight Priority
detail.technical_mechanics: Highlight.priority accepts an integer (default 0). When two highlights intersect the same character range, the styles of the highlight with the higher priority take precedence. When priorities are equal, the last registered style wins.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to layer spell-check warnings (priority 1), search query matches (priority 2), and active user selections (priority 3) cleanly without style collision or visual ambiguity.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Handled natively within the GPU composite paint stage; avoids costly JavaScript boundary intersection calculations.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps implementing multiple simultaneous highlight layers must establish a documented priority hierarchy to prevent lower-priority decorations from obscuring high-priority security warnings.

title: W3C TouchEvent Interface: Multi-Touch State & Surface Interaction Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the TouchEvent interface representing touch gesture events on touch-sensitive surfaces, tracking simultaneous touch points, touch phases, and modifier keys across mobile devices.

detail.specification: W3C Touch Events Community Group Report - Section 5 The TouchEvent Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: TouchEvent encapsulates touch point arrays through touches, targetTouches, and changedTouches lists. It provides event cancellation semantics via preventDefault() to suppress emulated mouse events and native viewport panning.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Underpins mobile touch interaction for mini app interactive maps, signature pads, mobile checkout sliders, and touch-based mini-games within super app containers.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: User agents optimize TouchEvent dispatch via passive event listeners ({ passive: true }) to prevent blocking the compositor thread during touch scrolls.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must register touch listeners as passive ({ passive: true }) unless explicitly preventing default scroll behavior (such as on custom drawing canvases or signature capture pads).

title: W3C Touch Interface: Contact Point Geometry & Pressure Telemetry
description: Standardizes the Touch interface representing an individual contact point, providing precise spatial coordinates, touch radius ellipses, rotation angles, and force/pressure measurements.

detail.specification: W3C Touch Events Community Group Report - Section 3 The Touch Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Each Touch object exposes clientX/clientY, pageX/pageY, screenX/screenY, identifier (tracking continuous finger contact), radiusX/radiusY, rotationAngle, and force (normalized 0.0 to 1.0).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini app digital signature pads, e-KYC biometric touch capture, and interactive canvas tools to capture variable stroke pressure and touch precision on mobile touchscreens.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Touch objects are immutable snapshots generated per touch event, allowing safe extraction without retaining persistent references to heavy native input contexts.
detail.store_review_rule: Biometric or signature capture mini apps must record Touch.force and coordinate precision to guarantee legally binding digital signing requirements.

title: W3C TouchList Interface: Multi-Touch Collection Indexing & Memory Hygiene
description: Standardizes the TouchList interface representing indexed collections of Touch points, enabling structured multi-touch gesture processing (pinch-to-zoom, two-finger rotation, multi-finger taps).

detail.specification: W3C Touch Events Community Group Report - Section 4 The TouchList Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Exposes length and item(index) methods. Used across touches (all active touches on the screen), targetTouches (touches originating on the target element), and changedTouches (touches that triggered the current event).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to differentiate between global multi-touch gestures and local component interactions, preventing gesture collisions between nested mini app widgets and super app navigation drawers.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Allocated as lightweight array buffers in the browser engine; recycling occurs immediately following event loop dispatch.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps supporting multi-touch gestures must scope gesture tracking to targetTouches rather than global touches to prevent hijacking super app host edge-swipe gestures.

title: Element touchstart Event: Touch Contact Initiation & Fast-Click Architecture
description: Standardizes the touchstart event dispatched when one or more touch points are placed on the touch surface, initiating gesture recognition and eliminating the legacy 300ms mobile click delay.

detail.specification: W3C Touch Events Community Group Report - Section 5.1 The touchstart Event
detail.technical_mechanics: Bubbles through the DOM tree. Can be intercepted at capture or bubble phases. Dispatched immediately upon physical surface contact prior to any synthesized mousedown or click events.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides instantaneous feedback for mini app navigation bars, payment confirmation buttons, and catalog product cards, ensuring sub-50ms user-perceived responsiveness.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Handled directly on the browser input thread when declared passive, preventing main-thread layout recalculations from delaying visual touch highlights.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app interactive buttons must implement immediate active state feedback via touchstart or CSS :active to maintain crisp, native-app tactile parity.

title: Element touchmove Event: Continuous Gesture Tracking & Compositor Decoupling
description: Standardizes the touchmove event fired continuously as touch points move along the touch surface, governing drag-and-drop interactions, carousels, and custom pull-to-refresh widgets.

detail.specification: W3C Touch Events Community Group Report - Section 5.2 The touchmove Event
detail.technical_mechanics: Dispatches at high frequency aligned with hardware refresh rates (60Hz/120Hz). Contains updated touch coordinates across changedTouches. If non-passive preventDefault() is called, native browser scrolling is locked.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Crucial for mini app swipeable image carousels, custom drawer sheets, and range sliders, ensuring fluid gesture tracking without hitching.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Developers must decouple heavy DOM mutations from touchmove handlers using requestAnimationFrame or CSS Transforms to avoid catastrophic frame drops.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps implementing custom touchmove handlers must throttle computations via requestAnimationFrame and avoid synchronous layout reads (such as offsetHeight) inside the handler.

title: WHATWG TreeWalker Interface: Filtered Tree Traversal & Hierarchical DOM Navigation
description: Standardizes the TreeWalker interface representing the nodes of a document subtree and a position within them, providing filtered hierarchical navigation across DOM parent, child, and sibling axes.

detail.specification: WHATWG DOM Living Standard - Section 6 Traversal, The TreeWalker Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: TreeWalker exposes currentNode, parentNode(), firstChild(), lastChild(), previousSibling(), nextSibling(), previousNode(), and nextNode(). It traverses an active DOM view while filtering nodes via whatToShow bitmasks and custom NodeFilter callbacks.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides super app security containers and mini app SDKs with a zero-allocation, non-destructive mechanism to inspect DOM hierarchies, scrub malicious attributes, verify accessibility nodes, and sanitize rich text before rendering.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Operates as a live pointer on existing DOM tree nodes without cloning subtrees or allocating intermediate NodeList arrays, preserving memory under low-RAM conditions on mobile devices.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps performing client-side template rendering or dynamic HTML sanitization must utilize TreeWalker or Native Sanitizer APIs rather than recursive JavaScript DOM recursion to avoid call-stack overflow vulnerabilities.

title: Document.createTreeWalker(): NodeFilter Scoping & Sanitized Subtree Inspection
description: Standardizes the Document.createTreeWalker() factory method, constructing a new TreeWalker object rooted at a specified node with custom whatToShow bitmasks and NodeFilter filtering logic.

detail.specification: WHATWG DOM Living Standard - Section 6 Traversal, createTreeWalker
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts root, whatToShow bitflags (e.g. NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT | NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT), and optional filter callback. Returns an immutable traversal walker bound to the specified root container.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Used by super app host bridge security guards to audit guest mini app widgets, ensuring third-party scripts do not inject unauthorized iframe, object, or script tags into host UI slots.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: The resulting TreeWalker object holds only weak internal references and traversal cursor pointers, which are automatically collected when the walker goes out of scope.
detail.store_review_rule: Third-party mini app components embedding untrusted user-generated content must sanitize DOM fragments using createTreeWalker() with NodeFilter.SHOW_ELEMENT to strip executable script vectors before DOM insertion.

title: WHATWG NodeIterator Interface: Linear DOM Sequence Traversal & Flat Node Iteration
description: Standardizes the NodeIterator interface representing an iterator over a sequence of nodes in a document subtree in document order, presenting a flat view of filtered DOM structures.

detail.specification: WHATWG DOM Living Standard - Section 6 Traversal, The NodeIterator Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Exposes root, whatToShow, filter, referenceNode, pointerBeforeReferenceNode, nextNode(), previousNode(), and detach() (legacy no-op). Iterates sequentially in document tree order (pre-order depth-first).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Essential for mini app search indexing, localized text replacement, and in-page highlighting engines where flat sequential iteration over text nodes or headings is required without complex tree recursion.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Maintains an internal cursor position dynamically updated by the browser engine even as DOM modifications occur, eliminating the need to buffer DOM snapshots in JavaScript memory.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps indexing product catalog descriptions or search keywords must use NodeIterator to scan text nodes linearly, preventing memory spikes associated with document.querySelectorAll('*') arrays.

title: Document.createNodeIterator(): Subtree Iteration & Lightweight Node Paging
description: Standardizes the Document.createNodeIterator() factory method, initializing a sequential iterator rooted at a specified node to traverse nodes matching specific whatToShow and filter criteria.

detail.specification: WHATWG DOM Living Standard - Section 6 Traversal, createNodeIterator
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts root, whatToShow bitflags, and filter function or object. Constructs a lightweight cursor tracking nodes in document order, advancing or rewinding across siblings and children transparently.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement efficient incremental batch processing (e.g. processing 50 nodes per frame) during large catalog rendering or form inspection without locking the main thread.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Decouples node processing from synchronous DOM queries, allowing chunked execution via requestIdleCallback or scheduler.postTask to maintain high responsiveness.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps parsing large data tables or multi-item catalogs must employ createNodeIterator() for chunked processing when analyzing DOM nodes to satisfy super app INP and frame rate benchmarks.

title: NodeFilter Interface & Callback Architecture: Constant WhatToShow Flags & Acceptance Filtering
description: Standardizes the NodeFilter interface and constants used by TreeWalker and NodeIterator to filter nodes during traversal, defining granular node-type bitmasks and tri-state acceptance outcomes.

detail.specification: WHATWG DOM Living Standard - Section 6 Traversal, The NodeFilter Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines whatToShow constants (SHOW_ALL, SHOW_ELEMENT, SHOW_ATTRIBUTE, SHOW_TEXT, SHOW_COMMENT, SHOW_DOCUMENT) and filter return codes: FILTER_ACCEPT (include node), FILTER_REJECT (exclude node and its children in TreeWalker), and FILTER_SKIP (exclude node but continue traversing children).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides exact control over subtree pruning in super app security scanners, allowing dangerous branches (such as external shadow roots, unverified custom elements, or hidden tracking pixels) to be instantly skipped or rejected.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Callback executions are invoked synchronously inside the traversal loop; returning FILTER_REJECT immediately halts traversal of entire subtrees, dramatically reducing CPU cycles.
detail.store_review_rule: Security review scanners for mini app bundles must enforce NodeFilter.FILTER_REJECT on unapproved third-party custom element subtrees to prevent unauthorized DOM traversal and attribute snooping.

title: W3C CSS Logical Properties & Values: Flow-Relative Formatting & BiDi Internationalization
description: Standardizes the CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1, introducing logical equivalents to physical box model properties that map dynamically to block and inline dimensions based on writing-mode and direction.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1 - Section 1 Introduction
detail.technical_mechanics: Replaces physical directions (top, right, bottom, left) with flow-relative directions (block-start, block-end, inline-start, inline-end). Automatically adapts box boundaries when switching between LTR, RTL (Arabic/Hebrew), and vertical writing modes (CJK).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables super app mini app developers to author a single universal stylesheet that renders flawlessly across multi-regional deployments without requiring duplicate RTL CSS overrides or locale-specific layout hacks.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Computed directly in the CSS cascade engine; eliminates runtime JavaScript layout flipping scripts that trigger layout recalculations upon locale change.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps certified for multi-regional distribution across ASEAN and MENA regions must author layouts using CSS logical properties to guarantee native-grade bidirectional fidelity.

title: CSS margin-inline Property: Flow-Relative Inline Margin Spacing & RTL Layout Automation
description: Standardizes the margin-inline shorthand property (margin-inline-start and margin-inline-end), mapping to logical inline margins according to the element's writing-mode, direction, and text-orientation.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1 - Section 4 Flow-Relative Margins
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts <length>, <percentage>, or auto. Maps margin-inline-start to physical margin-left in LTR and margin-right in RTL; maps margin-inline-end conversely.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Critical for mini app navigation bars, breadcrumb trails, product catalog cards, and form field icons, ensuring correct icon-to-text spacing when switching between English/Vietnamese (LTR) and Arabic (RTL).
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Resolved by the browser compositor and layout engine during initial box computation with zero runtime memory overhead.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app UI frameworks must prohibit hardcoded physical margin-left/margin-right on directional components (e.g. back buttons, dropdown arrows) in favor of margin-inline.

title: CSS padding-inline Property: Responsive Touch Target & Content Boundary Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the padding-inline shorthand property (padding-inline-start and padding-inline-end), establishing flow-relative internal padding that adjusts automatically to text flow direction.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1 - Section 4 Flow-Relative Padding
detail.technical_mechanics: Defines logical inline start and end padding offsets. Governs clickable hit-target padding and text containment within button badges, input fields, and dialog wrappers.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Guarantees that super app mini app action buttons and input fields maintain WCAG 2.2 AA compliant 48x48px touch targets and symmetric or flow-relative internal padding regardless of active language.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Handled within standard CSS box model calculations without generating redundant style nodes or triggering JavaScript resize listeners.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app interactive buttons and clickable list items must utilize padding-inline to maintain consistent touch boundaries across internationalized form layouts.

title: CSS inset-inline Property: Flow-Relative Modal, Badge & Popover Positioning
description: Standardizes the inset-inline shorthand property (inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end), defining the logical inline offset of positioned elements relative to their containing block.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1 - Section 5 Flow-Relative Offsets
detail.technical_mechanics: Acts as the logical equivalent to left and right properties for absolute, fixed, or sticky elements. Maps to inset-inline-start and inset-inline-end according to the containing block's writing direction.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini app notification badges, floating action buttons (FAB), drawer sheets, and shopping cart counter bubbles to anchor to the correct edge (e.g. trailing edge) across both LTR and RTL locales.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Positioning offsets are computed by the rendering engine's layout geometry pipeline without JavaScript positioning calculations or viewport polling.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app floating components and notification counters anchored to container edges must declare positions via inset-inline to prevent visual overlap with super app host navigation bars in RTL locales.

title: CSS border-inline Property: Flow-Relative Dividers & Container Accent Rule Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the border-inline shorthand property (border-inline-start and border-inline-end), defining flow-relative borders for color, style, and width along the inline axis.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Logical Properties and Values Module Level 1 - Section 4 Flow-Relative Borders
detail.technical_mechanics: Combines border-inline-color, border-inline-style, and border-inline-width across inline-start and inline-end edges. Automatically mirrors vertical quote rules, card accents, and table cell borders.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to render decorative callout borders, timeline step indicators, and form field validation borders that naturally flip orientation between LTR and RTL scripts.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Paints during the normal border rasterization pass without requiring synthetic decorative border elements or secondary DOM nodes.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini app card designs and blockquote components featuring leading decorative vertical stripes must specify border-inline-start rather than border-left to pass international design review.

title: W3C CSS Motion Path Module Level 1: Declarative Trajectory & Path Animation Architecture
description: Standardizes the CSS Motion Path Module Level 1, allowing authors to animate any graphical element or DOM node along a specified path or geometric trajectory declaratively without JavaScript coordinate calculations.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Motion Path Module Level 1 - Section 1 Introduction
detail.technical_mechanics: Establishes a motion path coordinate system. Uses offset-path to specify the trajectory, offset-distance to specify progress, offset-rotate to define orientation, offset-anchor to establish origin, and offset-position to set the path's initial point.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to implement engaging delivery tracking animations (e.g. delivery motorbike moving along a map route), interactive tutorial pointers, and gamified reward paths entirely on the compositor thread without CPU-bound requestAnimationFrame loops.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Motion path animations execute directly on the GPU compositor thread when animated via CSS Transitions or Web Animations API, avoiding main-thread layout thrashing during low-battery or thermal throttling states.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps featuring route animations or animated trajectory indicators must implement CSS Motion Path or WAAPI rather than setInterval/requestAnimationFrame coordinate manipulation to minimize mobile CPU drain.

title: CSS offset-path Property: Vector Path Trajectory & Ray/Geometry Sandboxing
description: Standardizes the offset-path property, specifying the mathematical path an animated element follows, supporting path() SVG strings, ray() polar coordinates, basic shapes (circle, ellipse, polygon), and url() external SVG references.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Motion Path Module Level 1 - Section 2 Defining a Motion Path
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts path('<string>') with SVG path syntax (M, C, S, Q, T, A, Z commands), ray(<angle> [<size>] [contain]), or basic shape functions. Defines the 1-dimensional parametric curve along which offset-distance operates.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini app developers to bind interactive UI elements, floating badges, and order-progress markers to complex curved routes that precisely match underlying vector illustrations and transit maps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Path parsing and spline evaluation are pre-compiled into GPU vertex buffers or bezier lookup tables upon CSSOM instantiation, ensuring zero per-frame parsing overhead.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must ensure path() coordinate strings are normalized and bounded within the visible container viewport to prevent animated elements from flying out of the super app sandbox boundary.

title: CSS offset-distance Property: Normalized Linear Progress & Compositor Interpolation
description: Standardizes the offset-distance property, defining the position of an element along the path specified by offset-path as a length or percentage from 0% (path start) to 100% (path end).

detail.specification: W3C CSS Motion Path Module Level 1 - Section 4 Positioning along a Motion Path
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts <length-percentage>. 0% points to the start of the path; 100% points to the total path length. Interpolable and animatable continuously via CSS keyframes or Web Animations API.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a clean, single-property progress indicator for multi-step onboarding journeys, financial goal completion gauges, and real-time transit telemetry within mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Percentage-based distance interpolation is accelerated on the browser compositor, bypassing style recalculations and preventing main-thread UI hitching during complex scroll gestures.
detail.store_review_rule: Interactive progress animations linked to network polling or WebSocket state must animate offset-distance via CSS transitions rather than mutating inline style coordinates.

title: CSS offset-rotate Property: Dynamic Tangential Orientation & Auto-Heading Alignment
description: Standardizes the offset-rotate property, defining the direction and rotation angle of an element as it moves along an offset-path, supporting automatic tangential alignment and reverse orientation.

detail.specification: W3C CSS Motion Path Module Level 1 - Section 5 Rotation along a Motion Path
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts auto, reverse, or [<angle>] offset (e.g. auto 90deg). When auto is specified, the element automatically aligns its x-axis with the tangent vector of the path at the current offset-distance position.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Eliminates complex trigonometry in mini app navigation maps, vehicle delivery dispatch dashboards, and animated game sprites, automatically rotating icons to face their movement direction.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Tangential angle calculation is evaluated natively within the browser rendering pipeline, removing the need for trigonometric Math.atan2() computations in JavaScript render loops.
