title: AudioListener: Virtual Listener Spatial Orientation & Multi-Channel Perception
description: Standardizes AudioListener (BaseAudioContext.listener), defining the position, orientation, and forward/up vector geometry of the virtual listener in the 3D acoustic scene.

detail.specification: Web Audio API - Section 5.18: AudioListener interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Represents the user's ears in 3D audio space; exposes positionX/Y/Z, forwardX/Y/Z, and upX/Y/Z as AudioParam automation curves for sample-accurate head-tracking synchronization.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps integrating device motion or XR headsets to synchronize head orientation with spatial audio panning without audio glitches.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Listener position updates are clamped to container viewport coordinates and paused when the mini app is not active in the viewport.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must ensure listener forward and up vectors remain orthogonal to prevent audio distortion and undefined spatial panning behavior.

title: AudioParam: Sample-Accurate Parameter Automation & Glitch-Free Transitions
description: Standardizes AudioParam, providing sample-accurate scheduled changes (linear ramps, exponential ramps, and target values) to audio node attributes with strict rate control.

detail.specification: Web Audio API - Section 5.3: AudioParam interface & Automation curves
detail.technical_mechanics: Provides setValueAtTime, linearRampToValueAtTime, exponentialRampToValueAtTime, setTargetAtTime, and setValueCurveAtTime; operates at a-rate (audio sample rate) or k-rate (block rate).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables click-free volume fading, filter sweeps, and pitch transitions in mini app UI sounds, gaming audio, and music playback.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: AudioParam automation queues are automatically cleared upon node disconnect or context suspension, preventing lingering CPU scheduling tasks.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must use linearRampToValueAtTime or setTargetAtTime instead of instant value assignments for volume transitions to prevent acoustic clicks/pops.

title: DynamicsCompressorNode: Dynamic Range Control & Acoustic Safety Limiting
description: Standardizes DynamicsCompressorNode, providing automatic gain control, dynamic range compression, and acoustic limiting to prevent speaker distortion and hearing damage.

detail.specification: Web Audio API - Section 5.14: DynamicsCompressorNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Lowers volume of loud signals and raises soft sounds; exposes threshold (dB), knee (dB), ratio, attack (seconds), release (seconds), and reduction (metering reduction in dB).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Protects users from unexpected acoustic shock and clipping distortion across user-generated or dynamic audio content in mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Acts as an essential master-bus safety limiter before destination routing with minimal fixed DSP memory footprint.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini games and audio streaming mini apps must include a DynamicsCompressorNode on the master audio bus before connecting to AudioDestinationNode to maintain safe volume thresholds.

title: ConvolverNode: Impulse Response Convolution & Realistic Room Acoustics
description: Standardizes ConvolverNode, enabling high-fidelity acoustic simulation and reverb through spectral convolution of input audio with recorded impulse response buffers.

detail.specification: Web Audio API - Section 5.13: ConvolverNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Performs real-time convolution using an AudioBuffer containing an impulse response (IR); exposes buffer and normalize (boolean energy normalization).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables professional acoustic reverb, concert hall simulation, and voice filtering inside specialized audio and game mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Large impulse response buffers (>5MB) are subject to container cache eviction under memory warnings and should be loaded on demand.
detail.store_review_rule: Impulse response buffers used in ConvolverNode must not exceed 10 seconds in duration or 44.1kHz stereo to avoid excessive RAM allocation in mobile web containers.

title: BiquadFilterNode: Second-Order Audio Filtering & Acoustic Shaping
description: Standardizes BiquadFilterNode, providing low-order IIR filters (lowpass, highpass, bandpass, lowshelf, highshelf, peaking, notch, allpass) for sound shaping, noise reduction, and equalization in mini apps.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.12: BiquadFilterNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Implements second-order recursive filters with configurable frequency, Q, gain, and detune AudioParams; exposes getFrequencyResponse() for synchronous magnitude/phase response inspection.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables sound equalizers, environmental muffle effects (e.g. menu pause screen sound dampening), and audio enhancement in gaming, e-learning, and conferencing mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Filter coefficients are computed efficiently on SIMD vector registers; unused filter nodes must be disconnected to free audio graph processing threads.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing BiquadFilterNode must bound resonant peak Q values (Q <= 30.0) to prevent acoustic distortion and clipping spikes.

title: AnalyserNode: Real-Time Audio Frequency & Time-Domain Telemetry
description: Standardizes AnalyserNode, enabling non-destructive real-time frequency analysis and waveform data extraction for audio visualization, voice activity detection, and acoustic monitoring.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.11: AnalyserNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Performs Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) analysis; exposes fftSize (32 to 32768), frequencyBinCount, minDecibels, maxDecibels, smoothingTimeConstant, getByteFrequencyData, and getFloatTimeDomainData.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides real-time audio visualization (visualizers, wave meters, speech input indicators) in mini apps without modifying the underlying audio signal.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Container caps fftSize at 2048 on mid/low-tier mobile chipsets to prevent excessive GPU/CPU work in visualization render loops.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must decouple FFT data extraction from high-frequency touch loops, polling AnalyserNode inside requestAnimationFrame only when visible.

title: GainNode: Audio Amplitude Modulation & Master Bus Attenuation
description: Standardizes GainNode, providing precise amplification and attenuation control over audio signals with sample-accurate AudioParam gain scheduling.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.10: GainNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Applies multiplicative volume gain; exposes gain AudioParam supporting linear and exponential fades via setValueAtTime and linearRampToValueAtTime.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Acts as the fundamental volume control, mute switch, and audio bus mixer across background music, sound effects, and voice channels in mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Host container injects a master GainNode at the root of the mini app audio graph to enforce system-wide mute and volume ducking during phone calls.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must route all sound emission through a designated master GainNode to allow host volume ducking and instant mute on container backgrounding.

title: StereoPannerNode: Low-Cost Stereo Spatialization & Balance Control
description: Standardizes StereoPannerNode, providing equal-power stereo panning across left and right audio channels with minimal computational overhead compared to full 3D panners.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.19: StereoPannerNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Positions mono/stereo input across a stereo soundfield using an equal-power panning algorithm; exposes pan AudioParam (-1.0 full left to +1.0 full right).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides lightweight directional audio for 2D casual games, UI audio panning, and stereo balance adjustments without the high CPU cost of HRTF convolution.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Ideal lightweight alternative to PannerNode under mobile device thermal pressure or low-battery power saving modes.
detail.store_review_rule: 2D mini games and UI applications must prefer StereoPannerNode over PannerNode unless authentic 3D spatial height and distance attenuation are strictly required.

title: WaveShaperNode: Non-Linear Distortion & Harmonic Waveform Saturation
description: Standardizes WaveShaperNode, enabling mathematical non-linear distortion curves and waveshaping for audio saturation, guitar amp emulation, and synthetic sound design.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.15: WaveShaperNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Applies non-linear transfer function defined by a Float32Array curve; exposes curve and oversample ('none', '2x', '4x') to eliminate digital aliasing.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables music creation tools, audio synthesizer mini apps, and gaming sound effects (explosions, overdrive) to create rich harmonic distortion.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Oversampling 4x incurs significant DSP load; container can clamp oversample to '2x' or 'none' under thermal pressure.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps using WaveShaperNode must not dynamically allocate large curve arrays (>65536 samples) per audio frame to prevent garbage collection pauses.

title: OscillatorNode: Periodic Waveform Synthesis & Pitch Scheduling
description: Standardizes OscillatorNode, providing real-time audio synthesis of standard periodic waveforms (sine, square, sawtooth, triangle) and custom Fourier tables with microsecond scheduling.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.7: OscillatorNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Generates audio waveforms at specified frequency and detune AudioParams; exposes type ('sine', 'square', 'sawtooth', 'triangle', 'custom'), setPeriodicWave(), and start()/stop() lifecycle methods.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables zero-asset UI audio generation (beeps, clicks, alerts) and musical synthesizers in mini apps without loading heavy audio asset files over the network.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: OscillatorNode is single-use per start/stop cycle; nodes automatically detach and become eligible for garbage collection once stopped.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps generating UI feedback tones must utilize OscillatorNode synthesis to avoid bundling repetitive static WAV/MP3 sound files under 50KB.

title: ConstantSourceNode: Constant Value AudioParam Modulation & Control Signals
description: Standardizes ConstantSourceNode, continuously outputting a constant scalar value for parameter modulation, matrix gain scaling, and complex audio graph automation.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.9: ConstantSourceNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Outputs a constant monetary or scalar signal at offset AudioParam; allows connecting audio rate signals to multiple AudioParams for synchronized macro-control.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables unified control busses where a single master slider or sensor input dynamically controls multiple filter cutoffs, gain levels, and pan values across mini app soundscapes.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Runs as a negligible scalar compute operation; stopped automatically when associated sound pipelines terminate.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps coordinating complex multi-node audio parameter changes must use ConstantSourceNode rather than redundant requestAnimationFrame JavaScript loops.

title: ChannelSplitterNode: Multi-Channel Audio Demultiplexing & Stream Separation
description: Standardizes ChannelSplitterNode, separating multi-channel audio streams into individual mono audio channels for discrete per-channel DSP processing and routing.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.20: ChannelSplitterNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes a single multi-channel audio input and splits it into N individual mono outputs corresponding to channel index (left, right, center, LFE, surround).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Crucial for surround-sound mini apps, audio language track selection, and separate left/right audio signal processing (e.g. karaoke vocal separation).
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Zero-copy memory de-interleaving directly inside the audio rendering thread.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must not split beyond the channel count provided by the input stream to avoid allocating silent audio bus processing overhead.

title: ChannelMergerNode: Multi-Channel Audio Multiplexing & Matrix Assembly
description: Standardizes ChannelMergerNode, combining multiple mono audio streams into a single multi-channel stream for surround sound or multi-track destination output.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.21: ChannelMergerNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes up to N individual mono audio inputs and multiplexes them into a single multi-channel output stream with specified channelCount.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to assemble multi-channel audio outputs (stereo, 5.1 surround) from separately processed sound elements before feeding to destination or recording.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Merger nodes maintain minimal internal buffers, interleaving samples into the destination block synchronously.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must configure the channelCount of ChannelMergerNode to match the physical hardware capability of the host device.

title: DelayNode: Temporal Sound Delay & Echo Buffering Governance
description: Standardizes DelayNode, providing dynamically adjustable digital delay lines for echo effects, acoustic distance modeling, and audio-video lip-sync alignment.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.16: DelayNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Delays the incoming audio signal by a configurable delayTime AudioParam; allocates a circular buffer up to maxDelayTime (default 1.0s, configurable up to 180s).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides realistic acoustic reflections, slapback echoes, and AV synchronization corrections in live streaming and communication mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Delay ring buffers allocate memory proportional to maxDelayTime * sampleRate * channels; container restricts maxDelayTime to <= 5.0 seconds on mobile devices.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps instantiating DelayNode must explicitly declare maxDelayTime <= 5.0s; unconstrained maxDelayTime allocations are rejected to prevent mobile OOM crashes.

title: AudioBuffer: In-Memory Multi-Channel PCM Audio Asset Governance
description: Standardizes AudioBuffer, providing structured in-memory storage of linear PCM audio data with discrete channel allocation, sample rate matching, and zero-copy transfer.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.1: AudioBuffer interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Holds linear PCM audio samples in 32-bit floating point format; exposes sampleRate, length, duration, numberOfChannels, getChannelData(), and copyFromChannel()/copyToChannel().
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Acts as the standard decoded audio format for UI sound effects, game audio clips, and music samples loaded into mini app memory.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: AudioBuffers consume raw uncompressed RAM (~10MB per minute of stereo audio at 44.1kHz); host enforces a 50MB total AudioBuffer cache ceiling per mini app.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must decode audio clips into AudioBuffer on demand or stream longer tracks (>30 seconds) via HTMLAudioElement/MSE rather than preloading full songs into AudioBuffer.

title: AudioBufferSourceNode: Low-Latency Sound Playback & Pitch Looping
description: Standardizes AudioBufferSourceNode, enabling ultra-low-latency playback, looping, and variable-speed pitch modulation of pre-decoded AudioBuffer sound assets.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.6: AudioBufferSourceNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Plays back an AudioBuffer; exposes buffer, playbackRate AudioParam, detune AudioParam, loop, loopStart, loopEnd, and start()/stop() methods.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Essential for responsive game sound effects, button clicks, and rapid-fire audio triggers in high-performance interactive mini apps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: AudioBufferSourceNode instances are lightweight disposable objects designed to be created per sound trigger and garbage collected after playback.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must instantiate new AudioBufferSourceNode objects per playback invocation rather than attempting to restart stopped instances.

title: MediaStreamAudioSourceNode: Real-Time Microphone & Live Ingestion Bridge
description: Standardizes MediaStreamAudioSourceNode, bridging live audio streams from getUserMedia() or WebRTC into the Web Audio processing graph for real-time DSP and filtering.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.4: MediaStreamAudioSourceNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes a MediaStream containing at least one audio track and exposes an audio graph source output matching the stream's channel count; exposes mediaStream attribute.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables mini apps to perform live noise reduction, vocal effects, voice modulation, and volume metering on real-time microphone input during voice calls or live streaming.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Audio graph capture pauses immediately when microphone permission is revoked by the host or the user switches to another mini app.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing MediaStreamAudioSourceNode must obtain explicit microphone consent and release MediaStream audio tracks upon closing the audio session.

title: MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode: Audio Graph Egress & WebRTC Pipeline Export
description: Standardizes MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode, exporting the processed multi-node audio graph output as a standard MediaStream for recording or WebRTC live broadcast.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.5: MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Acts as an audio destination node that routes output into a synthesized MediaStream; exposes stream attribute containing an active MediaStreamAudioTrack.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to mix background music, synthesized sound effects, and processed microphone audio into a single clean audio stream for MediaRecorder or WebRTC peer connections.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Provides bounded streaming buffers, automatically throttling frame egress if the downstream WebRTC or MediaRecorder sink experiences backpressure.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps exporting audio streams via MediaStreamAudioDestinationNode must ensure proper track disposal to prevent lingering background audio recording sessions.

title: OfflineAudioContext: Headless Faster-Than-Realtime Audio Rendering
description: Standardizes OfflineAudioContext, enabling background, deterministic, and faster-than-realtime rendering of complex Web Audio graphs into an AudioBuffer without hardware output.

detail.specification: Web Audio API W3C Recommendation - Section 5.2: OfflineAudioContext interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Constructed with numberOfChannels, length, and sampleRate; renders the audio graph via startRendering() returning a Promise resolving to rendered AudioBuffer; supports suspend() and resume() at exact sample frames.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables audio editing, sound wave exporting, podcast track bouncing, and pre-baking complex soundscapes in mini apps without playing sound through device speakers.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Runs off-thread and can be throttled or executed in a Web Worker; host enforces a rendering timeout of 30 seconds to prevent denial-of-service CPU lockups.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps performing audio export or batch synthesis must use OfflineAudioContext rather than playing and recording real-time audio through destination nodes.

title: Contact Picker API: Privacy-Preserving On-Demand Address Book Access
description: Standardizes the Contact Picker API, providing an on-demand, user-mediated mechanism for mini apps to request contact information from the native device address book without granting blanket, continuous contacts read permissions.

detail.specification: W3C / WICG Contact Picker API Living Standard - Section 1: Introduction and Security Model
detail.technical_mechanics: Operates exclusively in top-level secure contexts (HTTPS); requires transient user activation (e.g. button click) to present the native platform contact picker sheet; the user explicitly selects which contact entries and data fields to disclose to the calling web context.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Critical for P2P money transfers, mobile phone bill top-ups, split-the-bill dining, and viral social sharing inside mini apps, eliminating the severe security risk of exposing the full device contacts database to third-party merchant code.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: The native contact picker UI is presented in an out-of-process system sheet; the webview runtime consumes minimal memory and releases picker handles immediately upon selection or cancellation.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps requesting contact details for payment routing or invitation flows must use the Contact Picker API rather than legacy proprietary container bridges that request unrestricted READ_CONTACTS permissions.

title: Navigator.contacts: Capability Detection & Picker Entry Point
description: Standardizes the navigator.contacts property, exposing the ContactsManager singleton interface for capability detection and contact query invocation in supported web runtime environments.

detail.specification: W3C / WICG Contact Picker API - Section 2: Extensions to the Navigator Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Read-only property returning a ContactsManager instance if the host browser and OS support native contact picking; returns undefined in insecure contexts, iframes without capability delegation, or unsupported desktop environments.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows super-app container SDKs to feature-detect native address book integration, providing graceful fallback to manual input forms or super-app in-network friend selectors when host OS contacts are unavailable.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Static property with zero runtime overhead; doesn't trigger permissions prompts or background queries during initial capability probing.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must guard contacts integration behind feature detection ('contacts' in navigator) and provide manual input fallbacks to ensure compatibility across webview engines and desktop client versions.

title: ContactsManager: Native Address Book Interface & Picker Controller
description: Standardizes the ContactsManager interface, defining methods to introspect supported contact properties and launch the platform-native contact selection dialog.

detail.specification: W3C / WICG Contact Picker API - Section 3: The ContactsManager Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Encapsulates select() and getProperties() asynchronous methods; guarantees that contact data is sanitized and normalized into ContactInfo dictionaries conforming to standardized schema types.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a clean, uniform interface for mini-app developers across Android, iOS (via webkit container polyfill), and desktop shells, standardizing contact retrieval contracts across the entire ecosystem.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Promises returned by ContactsManager are rejected with TypeError or SecurityError if invoked without transient activation, or resolved with empty lists if the user dismisses the system dialog.
detail.store_review_rule: Container shells must wrap ContactsManager calls in structured error-handling handlers to gracefully process user cancellations without application crashes.

title: ContactsManager.select(): Multi-Field Selection & Transient Activation Enforcement
description: Standardizes the ContactsManager.select() method, enabling mini apps to request specific contact properties with optional multi-selection while enforcing strict transient user activation constraints.

detail.specification: W3C / WICG Contact Picker API - Section 3.2: The select() method
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts an array of requested properties (e.g. ['name', 'tel']) and an options dictionary ({multiple: true/false}); returns a Promise resolving to a sequence of ContactInfo objects; strictly fails with SecurityError if called without transient user activation.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables batch recipient selection for group red packets, holiday gifting, or corporate expense splitting while strictly preventing rogue scripts from opening background or spam dialogs.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Only active during the duration of the modal UI; contact objects are garbage collected once processed by the mini-app application state.
detail.store_review_rule: Store review rejects any mini app attempting to invoke ContactsManager.select() from automated timers (setTimeout), onload events, or background tasks without immediate user tap.

title: ContactsManager.getProperties(): Property Introspection & Data Minimization
description: Standardizes ContactsManager.getProperties(), enabling mini apps to query which contact fields ('name', 'email', 'tel', 'address', 'icon') are supported by the underlying operating system before triggering selection.

detail.specification: W3C / WICG Contact Picker API - Section 3.1: The getProperties() method
detail.technical_mechanics: Asynchronous method returning a Promise resolving to an array of supported property names from the set ['address', 'email', 'icon', 'name', 'tel']; allows runtime UI adaptation based on OS capabilities.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enforces GDPR and privacy principle of data minimization; allows mini apps to verify if 'tel' or 'email' is available, avoiding requesting extraneous properties that could compromise user trust or trigger review rejections.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Cached by the browser engine after initial query; microtask resolution with negligible memory footprint.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must only request the minimal set of properties necessary for their specific business feature (e.g. only 'tel' for cellular top-ups), validated against getProperties() output during static compliance audits.

title: Window Management API: Multi-Screen Topologies & Merchant POS Displays
description: Standardizes the Window Management API, enabling mini apps to discover connected physical screens, query screen visual metrics, and position application windows across multiple displays in merchant POS, digital signage, and dual-screen kiosk environments.

detail.specification: W3C Window Management API Working Draft - Section 1: Introduction
detail.technical_mechanics: Extends the Screen interface and Window interface with getScreenDetails(); operates within secure contexts; guarded by the 'window-management' permission; provides accurate multi-display geometry without device fingerprinting leaks.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Critical for retail and restaurant super-app POS mini apps where a merchant-facing terminal must project a customer-facing payment sheet, promotional carousel, or loyalty QR code onto a secondary external monitor.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Screen topology state is managed in the browser display server layer; window placement resources are cleaned up immediately when secondary popup or projection windows are closed.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps requesting window-management permissions must declare explicit business justification (such as dual-screen merchant checkout or multi-monitor analytics dashboards) in their store submission metadata.

title: Window.getScreenDetails(): Asynchronous Screen Enumeration & Permission Negotiation
description: Standardizes Window.getScreenDetails(), providing an asynchronous method to request screen topology access and retrieve detailed multi-display spatial configurations.

detail.specification: W3C Window Management API Working Draft - Section 4: Extensions to the Window Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Returns a Promise resolving to a ScreenDetails object containing all connected displays; triggers a system permission prompt if not previously granted; rejects with NotAllowedError if denied by the user or restricted by Permissions-Policy: window-management=().
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides super-app container frameworks with an explicit, permission-gated workflow for dual-screen merchant setups, preventing silent background multi-monitor snooping.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: The permission check is mediated by the browser permissions engine; promise resolution is non-blocking and handles screen configuration changes dynamically.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must invoke Window.getScreenDetails() in response to direct user setup actions (such as clicking 'Configure External Display') rather than during cold startup.

title: ScreenDetails Interface: Multi-Display Coordinate Space & Screen Selection
description: Standardizes the ScreenDetails interface, representing the complete multi-screen environment including the array of all available physical screens and a pointer to the current screen hosting the mini app window.

detail.specification: W3C Window Management API Working Draft - Section 5: The ScreenDetails Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Exposes screens (sequence of ScreenDetailed objects), currentScreen (ScreenDetailed for the window's current viewport), and the screenschange / currentscreenchange event listeners for dynamic topology tracking.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows mini apps to calculate absolute multi-screen coordinates (left, top, width, height) to launch fullscreen customer checkout sheets onto external displays with pixel-perfect accuracy.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Maintains an active reference to system display configurations; dispatches change events without polling or background wake lock overhead.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must subscribe to currentscreenchange events to gracefully handle window dragging across displays with differing DPI or color gamuts.

title: ScreenDetailed Interface: Physical Display Metrics & Primary Identification
description: Standardizes the ScreenDetailed interface, extending the standard Screen object with granular display metadata including internal/external status, primary designation, and human-readable device labels.

detail.specification: W3C Window Management API Working Draft - Section 6: The ScreenDetailed Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Inherits from Screen; adds isPrimary (boolean indicating operating system primary display), isInternal (boolean distinguishing built-in laptop/tablet screens from external HDMI/USB-C monitors), devicePixelRatio, and label (display model string).
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables intelligent screen routing in POS environments: the mini app automatically identifies the external customer display (!isInternal) without requiring merchants to manually drag windows.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Properties are cached read-only attributes reflecting OS display server properties; zero continuous computation cost.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must not use ScreenDetailed.label or screen dimensions for cross-site fingerprinting or user tracking; violations result in immediate store revocation.

title: ScreenDetails.screens: Dynamic Display Lifecycle & Hot-Plug Arbitration
description: Standardizes the ScreenDetails.screens collection and dynamic lifecycle management, allowing mini apps to react seamlessly to external monitors being plugged in or disconnected during operation.

detail.specification: W3C Window Management API Working Draft - Section 5.1: The screens attribute and screenschange event
detail.technical_mechanics: A frozen array of ScreenDetailed objects representing active connected displays; fires screenschange event on the ScreenDetails parent whenever a display is attached, detached, or repositioned in system settings.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Ensures POS and kiosk mini apps recover gracefully when a customer-facing display cable is unplugged, automatically collapsing customer UI back into the primary merchant viewport without freezing.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Display hot-plug notifications are event-driven via native OS display manager hooks (e.g. udev, CGDisplayRegisterRegister, Win32 WM_DISPLAYCHANGE), avoiding continuous polling loops.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing secondary displays must implement screenschange handlers to safely tear down or repatriate secondary windows when external displays are disconnected.

title: Content Indexing API: Native OS Offline Content Discovery & Catalog Indexing
description: Standardizes the Content Indexing API, allowing mini apps to register cached, offline-capable content items (articles, documents, media, tickets) with the super-app shell and native OS offline discovery surfaces.

detail.specification: WICG Content Indexing API Living Standard - Section 1: Introduction
detail.technical_mechanics: Exposed on ServiceWorkerRegistration.index; allows mini apps to register structured metadata describing content already cached locally in CacheStorage or IndexedDB, enabling offline discovery even when the mini app is not active.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Allows super apps to build unified 'Downloaded Content' or 'Offline Hub' screens where users can browse and launch offline articles, boarding passes, and downloaded mini-app resources with zero network latency.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Content index records are lightweight metadata pointers (~1KB each); the host automatically removes entries if the underlying cache quota is purged or the mini app is uninstalled.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps registering content in the Content Index must verify that all declared assets (HTML, scripts, media) are completely cached offline before adding the entry.

title: ContentIndex Interface: Asynchronous Offline Content Metadata Management
description: Standardizes the ContentIndex interface, defining methods for adding, deleting, and querying indexed content entries within the Service Worker scope.

detail.specification: WICG Content Indexing API Living Standard - Section 3: ContentIndex Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Provides add(), delete(), and getAll() methods; operates asynchronously and returns Promises; scoped to the origin and Service Worker registration.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Provides a clean, standardized programmatic lifecycle for mini-app content syndication into the super app's central discovery feed and search engine.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Metadata is stored in a structured key-value database managed by the browser engine; operations are non-blocking and batched.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must keep the ContentIndex synchronized with their local CacheStorage; attempting to launch deleted or expired items results in store compliance demerits.

title: ContentIndex.add(): Structured Offline Asset Registration & Category Taxonomy
description: Standardizes ContentIndex.add(), enabling mini apps to register content items with rich metadata including unique identifier, title, description, category, icons, and deep launch URLs.

detail.specification: WICG Content Indexing API Living Standard - Section 3.1: The add() method
detail.technical_mechanics: Takes a ContentDescription dictionary containing id (DOMString), title, description, category ('homepage', 'article', 'video', 'audio'), url (relative or absolute URL within scope), and icons array; validates that url and icons are reachable.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables e-reading, streaming, and ticketing mini apps to surface downloaded novels, video episodes, or event tickets directly in the super app's native offline drawer.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Adding an existing id overwrites the previous entry, preventing unbounded metadata accumulation.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps must categorize content accurately according to the ContentDescription category enum; misrepresenting articles as system notifications is prohibited.

title: ContentIndex.delete(): Deterministic Index Revocation & Cache Cleanup Coordination
description: Standardizes ContentIndex.delete(), allowing mini apps to remove expired, viewed, or deleted items from the offline index and notify host discovery surfaces.

detail.specification: WICG Content Indexing API Living Standard - Section 3.2: The delete() method
detail.technical_mechanics: Accepts an id (DOMString); returns a Promise resolving to undefined once the item is unindexed; gracefully ignores non-existent ids without throwing exceptions.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Essential when a user deletes a downloaded video or when an airline boarding pass expires after flight completion, ensuring stale offline cards disappear from the super-app dashboard.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Immediately purges corresponding entry from the OS offline provider database and frees associated metadata storage.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps implementing offline media download features must pair cache eviction logic with ContentIndex.delete() to avoid phantom links in the super app UI.

title: ServiceWorkerRegistration.index: Container Binding & Worker Lifecycle Integration
description: Standardizes the ServiceWorkerRegistration.index property, binding the ContentIndex instance directly to the active Service Worker lifecycle and execution scope.

detail.specification: WICG Content Indexing API Living Standard - Section 2: Extensions to the ServiceWorkerRegistration Interface
detail.technical_mechanics: Read-only property on ServiceWorkerRegistration returning the ContentIndex instance; available in both Window contexts (navigator.serviceWorker.ready) and ServiceWorkerGlobalScope.
detail.superapp_container_relevance: Enables background sync workers and periodic sync handlers to autonomously update the content index when fresh articles or updated tickets are fetched in the background while the user sleeps.
detail.eviction_and_pressure_handling: Inherits Service Worker registration lifecycle; if the service worker registration is unregistered, the entire content index for that scope is automatically purged.
detail.store_review_rule: Mini apps utilizing background sync to refresh offline content must access index via registration.index inside the service worker execution thread.

title: W3C Navigation Timing Level 2: Sub-Millisecond Page Lifecycle Telemetry
description: Standardizes W3C Navigation Timing Level 2 (PerformanceNavigationTiming), providing high-precision, sub-millisecond timestamps for the entire mini app loading pipeline from unload, redirect, DNS, TCP/TLS handshake, request/response, to DOM parsing and load completion.
requirements: Containers MUST expose PerformanceNavigationTiming entries via the Performance Timeline API (window.performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')) for fine-grained mini app startup analysis.
Mini app SDKs MUST record critical startup markers including responseStart, domInteractive, and domContentLoadedEventEnd to detect cold-start bottlenecks.
High-resolution timestamps MUST conform to DOMHighResTimeStamp, with anti-fingerprinting clock coarsening applied (e.g. 5 microseconds minimum tick) in untrusted contexts.
Containers MUST sanitize or redact redirectStart and redirectEnd timestamps across cross-origin redirects to eliminate navigation timing side-channel leaks.
Mini app store review pipelines MUST benchmark median loadEventEnd against device tier baseline standards (e.g., <1200ms on mid-range Android).

title: W3C Server Timing API: End-to-End Gateway & Backend Latency Traceability
description: Standardizes the W3C Server Timing specification (PerformanceServerTiming), allowing backend gateways, edge proxies, and mini app services to pass granular performance metrics to the client container via HTTP response headers.
requirements: Super app API gateways and mini app backends SHOULD emit the Server-Timing header (e.g. Server-Timing: db;dur=53, edge;dur=12) on API and static resource responses.
Containers MUST parse PerformanceServerTiming entries from PerformanceResourceTiming and PerformanceNavigationTiming objects via .serverTiming array properties.
Sensitive internal infrastructure metrics (e.g. server hostnames, internal microservice IPs) MUST NOT be exposed in Server-Timing headers delivered to public mini app guest runtimes.
Mini app observability platforms MUST correlate client-side network request durations with server-side processing metrics to isolate edge network delays from backend compute latency.
Cross-origin resources MUST specify Timing-Allow-Origin headers before the container grants guest mini apps access to detailed Server Timing metrics.

title: W3C Long Animation Frames API (LoAF): Main-Thread UI Responsiveness Diagnostics
description: Standardizes the Long Animation Frames API (LoAF) under PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming, superseding legacy Long Tasks by isolating the exact JavaScript scripts, event listeners, and rendering layout phases that exceed 50ms frame thresholds.
requirements: Containers SHOULD implement PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming to capture animation frame updates exceeding 50ms, facilitating actionable INP (Interaction to Next Paint) optimizations.
Mini app monitoring SDKs MUST inspect PerformanceScriptTiming entries nested within LoAF records to identify the specific source URL, execution time, and invoker type of sluggish event handlers.
Containers MUST enforce privacy safeguards by redacting source script URLs and character positions for cross-origin or non-CORS scripts embedded within mini apps.
Store quality gates MUST flag mini apps generating excessive LoAF entries during checkout, booking, and payment flows to prevent UI freezing and user drop-off.
LoAF telemetry SHOULD be aggregated locally using PerformanceObserver with buffered: true and periodically flushed during idle browser periods via requestIdleCallback.

title: PerformanceNavigationTiming: Navigation Type & Cache Validation Telemetry
description: Specifies the PerformanceNavigationTiming interface properties, enabling mini apps and container runtimes to distinguish between initial navigations, page reloads, back-forward cache restorations, and prerender activations.
requirements: Containers MUST accurately populate PerformanceNavigationTiming.type ('navigate', 'reload', 'back_forward', 'prerender') to contextualize startup telemetry.
Performance monitoring SDKs MUST correlate PerformanceNavigationTiming.transferSize against encodedBodySize to verify local disk and Service Worker cache hit rates.
Mini apps MUST utilize domInteractive timestamps to decouple JavaScript bundle execution overhead from initial DOM structural availability.
Runtimes MUST enforce strict origin isolation so that cross-tenant navigations inside embedded iframes cannot query host window PerformanceNavigationTiming records.
Telemetric reports MUST annotate whether a navigation was fulfilled via BFCache or memory cache to ensure accurate cold-start KPI reporting.

title: PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming: Script Invocation & Frame Attribution
description: Specifies the PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming and PerformanceScriptTiming interfaces, capturing render duration, style and layout time, and script execution attribution for responsive UI audit compliance.
requirements: Mini app containers supporting Chromium-based WebViews (v123+) MUST expose PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming via PerformanceObserver.
Developers SHOULD inspect scripts array entries to distinguish long-running framework re-renders from heavy third-party analytics scripts.
Audit harnesses MUST calculate total blocking time and render delays by summing LoAF duration minus standard 16.6ms / 8.3ms refresh cycle allowances.
Store pre-submission automated testing pipelines MUST simulate intensive touch gestures and flag any frame where renderStart to styleAndLayoutEnd exceeds 30ms.
Container telemetry bridges MUST throttle and debounce LoAF emission to prevent telemetry reporting loops from exhausting device memory.

title: WICG Shape Detection API: Hardware-Accelerated Barcode & Vision Extraction
description: Standardizes the WICG Shape Detection API specification, defining native, hardware-accelerated computer vision primitives (BarcodeDetector, FaceDetector) decoupled from CPU-heavy WebAssembly vision libraries.
requirements: Containers supporting high-performance merchant scanning and ticket validation SHOULD expose BarcodeDetector backed by OS-level vision APIs (Google ML Kit, Apple Vision).
Mini apps MUST check barcode format support via BarcodeDetector.getSupportedFormats() before invoking detection workflows.
Containers MUST enforce camera permission gates and transient user activation checks before granting access to live video stream image processing.
Visual processing pipelines MUST sanitize and validate extracted barcode raw values before passing them into payment or deep-linking routing layers.
Face and barcode detection capabilities MUST be governed by container Permissions-Policy headers to prevent unauthorized background surveillance.

title: Barcode Detection API: Low-Latency QR & Barcode Recognition Architecture
description: Specifies the BarcodeDetector interface for detecting and decoding 1D and 2D barcodes (QR code, Aztec, Data Matrix, EAN-13, Code 128) directly from ImageBitmap, HTMLCanvasElement, or HTMLVideoElement frames.
requirements: Mini apps MUST instantiate BarcodeDetector with explicit formats options (e.g. ['qr_code', 'ean_13']) to optimize scanning hardware acceleration and reduce CPU consumption.
The detect() method MUST accept standard ImageBitmapSource inputs and return DetectedBarcode objects containing rawValue, format, boundingBox, and cornerPoints.
Containers MUST restrict continuous scanning frame rates (e.g., maximum 15-30 fps) to avoid battery drain and thermal throttling on mobile devices.
Decoded string payloads MUST be treated as untrusted input, requiring strict sanitization against XSS, SQL injection, and URI scheme tampering.
Containers MUST provide fallback JavaScript/Wasm scanning bridges on platforms where native OS BarcodeDetector implementation is absent.

title: BarcodeDetector.getSupportedFormats(): Dynamic Scanner Capability Negotiation
description: Specifies the static BarcodeDetector.getSupportedFormats() method, allowing mini apps to asynchronously query the host operating system's hardware-supported barcode symbiologies.
requirements: Mini app barcode scanning components MUST query BarcodeDetector.getSupportedFormats() during initialization to dynamically configure UI scanner capabilities.
Host containers MUST return an immutable sequence of supported format strings matching standard WICG barcode format definitions.
If a required commercial format (e.g., PDF417 for boarding passes or Code 39 for inventory) is unsupported natively, the mini app MUST degrade gracefully to server-side or WebAssembly decoding.
Store submission verification MUST audit format negotiation fallbacks to ensure mini apps do not throw unhandled runtime exceptions on budget devices.
Capability detection queries MUST NOT expose persistent device identifiers or OS-specific fingerprinting vectors to guest runtimes.

title: BarcodeDetector.detect(): Asynchronous Frame Analysis & Coordinate Geometry
description: Specifies the BarcodeDetector.detect() execution model, returning detected barcode geometries, bounding boxes, and corner point polygons for augmented reality (AR) bounding overlays.
requirements: Mini apps MUST pass valid canvas, image, or video elements to detect() and handle promise rejection upon invalid image data or buffer detachment.
DetectedBarcode.cornerPoints MUST be used to render precise AR viewfinder highlights and bounding polygons over recognized physical targets.
Mini app camera scanning flows MUST pause or throttle detect() invocations immediately upon successful barcode match to prevent duplicate scan events.
Containers MUST verify that video frames fed into detect() originate from active MediaStreamTrack instances with valid user consent.
High-resolution video streams MUST be downscaled or clipped to the scanner viewfinder region to maximize detection throughput and minimize memory footprint.

title: PerformanceScriptTiming: JavaScript Execution Attribution in LoAF Runtimes
description: Specifies the PerformanceScriptTiming interface, isolating execution duration, pause duration, compile time, and invoker origins for scripts executed within long animation frames.
requirements: Containers supporting LoAF MUST populate PerformanceScriptTiming objects detailing invoker types ('user-callback', 'event-listener', 'promise-resolve', 'classic-script').
Mini app performance monitoring tools MUST compute execution duration versus compile duration to identify JIT compilation lag on cold app launches.
Cross-origin script entries without CORS Timing-Allow-Origin MUST have their sourceURL, sourceFunctionName, and sourceCharPosition scrubbed to prevent code leaks.
Mini app SDKs SHOULD utilize PerformanceScriptTiming data to detect runaway recursive promise chains and unoptimized heavy DOM event handlers.
Store telemetry aggregators MUST group sluggish script execution metrics by third-party vendor SDKs to enforce ecosystem-wide dependency performance budgets.

title: W3C Web MIDI API: Musical Instrument & Peripheral Hardware Governance
description: Standardizes the W3C Web MIDI API (MIDIAccess, MIDIPort, MIDIInput, MIDIOutput), enabling mini apps in educational, creative, and gaming categories to enumerate and interact with hardware MIDI synthesizers and controllers.
requirements: Access to navigator.requestMIDIAccess() MUST be gated behind explicit user prompt permissions and container Permissions-Policy ('midi') directives.
Requests including sysex: true (system exclusive messaging) MUST require high-assurance user confirmation due to firmware flash and hardware reconfiguration risks.
Containers MUST isolate MIDI port access between mini app tenants, preventing background or unpinned tabs from intercepting raw MIDI message streams.
Mini apps interacting with MIDI hardware MUST gracefully handle dynamic device disconnect and reconnect events via statechange listener bindings.
Store security review policies MUST audit mini apps requesting SysEx permissions, rejecting non-creative apps attempting unauthorized peripheral access.

title: MIDIAccess Interface: Device Enumeration & Connection State Machine
description: Specifies the MIDIAccess interface, managing the collection of accessible MIDIInputMap and MIDIOutputMap instances and orchestrating dynamic peripheral device attachment lifecycles.
requirements: MIDIAccess.inputs and MIDIAccess.outputs maps MUST provide immutable iterators over currently connected physical and virtual MIDI interfaces.
Containers MUST dispatch statechange events on the MIDIAccess instance whenever hardware controllers are plugged in or removed.
Mini apps MUST verify sysexEnabled boolean state before attempting to transmit vendor-specific parameter change packets.
Containers MUST enforce origin boundaries ensuring that MIDIAccess handles cannot be leaked across iframe or multi-window boundaries.
Observability hooks SHOULD monitor MIDIAccess request frequency to detect unauthorized device enumeration or background fingerprinting attempts.

title: MIDIPort Interface: Peripheral Port Identity & Connection Mechanics
description: Specifies the MIDIPort base interface common to MIDIInput and MIDIOutput, defining device identification (id, manufacturer, name, version), connection states, and asynchronous open/close lifecycles.
requirements: MIDIPort.open() and MIDIPort.close() asynchronous methods MUST be used to manage physical hardware bus power and driver handles deterministically.
Containers MUST sanitize MIDIPort.name and manufacturer strings before exposing them to guest code to prevent device-based fingerprinting or spoofing.
MIDIPort connection states ('open', 'closed', 'pending') MUST accurately mirror the underlying operating system ALSA, CoreMIDI, or Windows MIDI subsystem status.
Mini apps MUST close all open MIDIPort connections when navigating away or transitioning into background suspended lifecycle states.
Host runtimes MUST immediately revoke MIDIPort access if the user disables hardware permissions in the super app container settings.

title: MIDIInput Interface: Low-Latency Message Stream Ingestion & Timing
description: Specifies the MIDIInput interface and midimessage event, enabling real-time ingestion of note-on, note-off, control change, and pitch bend bytes with high-precision timestamping.
requirements: MIDIInput.onmidimessage listeners MUST receive MIDIMessageEvent objects containing Uint8Array data payloads and DOMHighResTimeStamp timestamps.
Containers MUST enforce strict message length validation (e.g. 1-3 bytes for channel voice messages) to prevent buffer overflow attacks in bridge layers.
Mini apps SHOULD process high-frequency control change messages on dedicated worker threads or via Web Audio AudioWorklet routing to avoid UI stutter.
Containers MUST suppress MIDIInput message delivery when the mini app window loses focus or enters a background tab state.
Store compliance audits MUST verify that educational and music mini apps handle note-off tracking properly to avoid stuck synthesizer voices.

title: MIDIOutput Interface: Hardware Sequencing & Timestamped Message Dispatch
description: Specifies the MIDIOutput interface and send() method, enabling mini apps to transmit queued, schedule-accurate MIDI commands to external sound modules, lighting rigs, and synthesizers.
requirements: MIDIOutput.send(data, timestamp) MUST accept standard MIDI 1.0 byte sequences and schedule transmission according to DOMHighResTimeStamp timelines.
Containers MUST enforce throughput limits (e.g. standard 31.25 kbaud MIDI bandwidth) to prevent denial-of-service bus flooding on attached hardware.
SysEx message transmissions MUST be validated against known manufacturer ID registries if container security policy restricts arbitrary device firmware manipulation.
Mini apps MUST implement clear() method support where available to abort pending queued message sequences upon user pause or cancellation.
Container host bridges MUST catch and isolate driver-level hardware transmission errors to prevent native super app crashes.

title: W3C Web Locks API: Multi-Context Resource Arbitration & Deadlock Mitigation
description: Defines the W3C Web Locks API standard specification, providing asynchronous mutual exclusion primitives across execution contexts (documents, DedicatedWorkers, SharedWorkers, ServiceWorkers) within an origin. Enables mini-apps to coordinate access to partitioned client storage, IndexedDB databases, and OPFS handles without race conditions.
detail: The W3C Web Locks API specification establishes the LockManager interface exposed on navigator.locks in secure contexts. Execution contexts request locks by name, which are held until an asynchronous callback promise settles. Locks are scoped per origin and can be requested in 'exclusive' (default, single holder) or 'shared' (multiple concurrent holders) modes. The specification defines rigorous queue semantics: requests are granted in FIFO order unless modified by options such as mode, steal, or ifAvailable. Deadlock mitigation is architected through cooperative design, deterministic lock ordering recommendations, and integration with AbortSignal to enforce request timeouts. In a super-app architecture where a mini-app may run across multiple tabs, iframes, or worker threads concurrently, Web Locks provide the canonical mechanism to arbitrate database migrations, offline sync sessions, and cached authentication token refreshes without cross-thread corruption.

title: Web Locks API Architecture: Scope, Lifecycle & State Coordination
description: Details the Web Locks API concepts and operational lifecycle across modern browser runtimes. Explains how lock ownership is tied to promise settlement and how unhandled rejections or execution context termination automatically release locks to prevent orphaned resource locking.
detail: MDN documentation specifies that navigator.locks is available across window, DedicatedWorker, SharedWorker, and ServiceWorker scopes within secure origins (HTTPS). A lock is granted when the browser invokes the passed callback and is automatically released when the returned promise resolves or rejects. If an execution context crashes or is terminated (e.g., tab closed, worker terminated, or super-app container background freeze), the user agent guarantees deterministic lock release, preventing permanent resource starvation. Mini-app developers must structure async workflows such that all critical sections clean up intermediate state upon rejection. The API eliminates the need for brittle localStorage polling or heartbeat-based advisory locks, reducing CPU wakeups and memory overhead across the super-app runtime.

title: LockManager Interface: Global Namespace Arbitration & Introspection
description: Specifies the LockManager interface providing request() and query() methods for coordinated locking operations. Governs lock acquisition policies, signal interception, and programmatic introspection of pending and held locks across the origin.
detail: The LockManager interface is the central coordination entity exposed via navigator.locks. It provides two core methods: request(name, [options], callback) and query(). Lock names are arbitrary DOMStrings scoped strictly to the calling origin, preventing cross-tenant mini-app interference. LockManager manages separate queues per resource name and arbitrates between exclusive and shared locks according to standard reader-writer lock semantics. The container sandbox leverages LockManager to ensure that background background-sync workers do not collide with foreground mini-app UI updates when mutating local state, allowing high-throughput concurrent reads while strictly serializing write transactions.

title: LockManager.request(): Mode Selection, Preemption & Abort Signal Integration
description: Examines the parameters and behavioral options of LockManager.request(), including 'mode' ('exclusive' vs 'shared'), 'ifAvailable' non-blocking try-lock mechanics, 'steal' emergency preemption, and 'signal' cancellation via AbortSignal.
detail: LockManager.request(name, options, callback) accepts options dictionaries configuring lock behavior. Key options include: (1) mode: 'exclusive' (default) or 'shared', allowing reader-writer optimization; (2) ifAvailable: boolean (default false); if true and the lock cannot be granted immediately, the request is not queued and the callback is invoked with null, providing non-blocking trylock capability essential for opportunistic background maintenance; (3) steal: boolean (default false); if true, any held locks for the name are preemptively broken and granted immediately to this request, reserved for emergency failover recovery; (4) signal: an AbortSignal instance allowing timeout or caller-mediated cancellation before the lock is granted. If aborted while queued, the returned promise rejects with an AbortError without invoking the callback. Super-app store runtime guidelines require mini-apps to bind AbortSignal.timeout() to queued lock requests to guarantee SLA bounds and prevent frozen UI threads.

title: LockManager.query(): Snapshot Diagnostics & Deadlock Forensic Telemetry
description: Specifies the LockManager.query() method returning a snapshot of all currently held and pending lock requests within the origin. Enables programmatic deadlock detection, performance diagnostics, and health monitoring.
detail: LockManager.query() returns a Promise that resolves to a LockManagerSnapshot dictionary containing two sequences: 'held' and 'pending'. Each entry contains: 'name' (DOMString), 'mode' ('exclusive' or 'shared'), and 'clientId' (a unique DOMString matching the Client interface of the owning window or worker). This enables real-time origin-wide concurrency introspection. Mini-app monitoring systems can periodically inspect lock queues to detect hung locks (e.g., locks held longer than 30 seconds), identify stalled clients, and automatically report telemetry back to the super-app store telemetry gateway. The clientId correlation allows the host container to pinpoint whether a stalled lock belongs to a background worker or an active foreground frame, facilitating surgical worker recycling without restarting the entire mini-app.

title: WICG Document Picture-in-Picture: Arbitrary DOM Floating Window Architecture
description: Specifies the WICG Document Picture-in-Picture specification, extending Picture-in-Picture capabilities beyond HTMLVideoElement to arbitrary HTML documents. Allows mini-apps to pop out interactive UI components into an always-on-top floating window that stays visible while the user navigates across the super-app or operating system.
detail: The Document Picture-in-Picture API allows an origin to create an always-on-top auxiliary window containing a full Document object. Unlike the legacy HTMLVideoElement.requestPictureInPicture() which only projects video streams, Document PiP supports arbitrary interactive DOM elements (custom video controls, live chat, mini-games, trading tickers, ride-hailing tracking, and video conferencing grids). The API is exposed on window.documentPictureInPicture in secure contexts. The specification enforces strict origin inheritance: the PiP window shares the same origin, execution environment, and cookie/storage jar as the opener window. Crucially, user gesture activation (transient user activation) is strictly mandatory to initiate requestWindow(), preventing intrusive popups. The super-app host container enforces strict lifecycle coupling: if the opener mini-app context navigates or terminates, the PiP window is automatically destroyed.

title: DocumentPictureInPicture.requestWindow(): Configuration & Window Provisioning
description: Details the requestWindow() method of the DocumentPictureInPicture interface, governing sizing dimensions, return-to-opener controls, and asynchronous window creation.
detail: DocumentPictureInPicture.requestWindow(options) opens an always-on-top floating window and returns a Promise resolving to a Window object. The options dictionary supports: (1) width: integer specifying the requested initial inner width in CSS pixels; (2) height: integer specifying initial inner height; (3) disallowReturnToOpener: boolean indicating whether the native PiP window should hide the back-to-tab button (useful for transient floating widgets); (4) preferInitialWindowPlacement: boolean hinting platform positioning. Calling requestWindow() requires transient user activation and automatically closes any previously open Document PiP window within the browser instance (single-instance guarantee). The opener script can directly populate the returned window.document, append nodes, and transfer DOM subtrees using Element.append(), establishing seamless dual-window UI orchestration.

title: DocumentPictureInPicture.window Property: Active Instance Tracking & Reference
description: Specifies the window attribute on DocumentPictureInPicture, providing immediate programmatic access to the currently open PiP Window instance or null if no window is active.
detail: The window read-only property of documentPictureInPicture returns a reference to the active DocumentPictureInPicture Window object if one exists, or null otherwise. This property allows decoupled components within the mini-app to check whether an always-on-top floating window is currently active without maintaining brittle global state variables. When the PiP window is closed—either via user click on the system close widget, calling window.close() programmatically, or upon opener teardown—this property automatically reverts to null. Mini-apps use this property to synchronize UI toggle states, adjust layout density in the main viewport, and redirect audio/video rendering pipelines dynamically.

title: DocumentPictureInPictureEvent: Lifecycle Attachment & Event Dispatch
description: Details the DocumentPictureInPictureEvent dispatched to documentPictureInPicture upon opening an always-on-top floating window, enabling automatic styling propagation and event listener registration.
detail: When a PiP window is successfully opened via requestWindow(), the 'enter' event is fired on window.documentPictureInPicture, passing an instance of DocumentPictureInPictureEvent. This event exposes the 'window' property pointing to the newly opened auxiliary Window object. Event listeners bound to 'enter' can immediately initialize the auxiliary window's DOM, attach style sheets, and register event listeners for user interactions (e.g., mute, play/pause, close). Furthermore, the auxiliary window fires a standard 'pagehide' event when closed by the user, providing the canonical cleanup hook to transfer DOM subtrees back to the main document. This symmetric lifecycle architecture guarantees zero state loss when transitioning between docked and floating modes.

title: Chrome Platform Guide: Document Picture-in-Picture Implementation & Style Copying
description: Details technical implementation best practices for Document Picture-in-Picture, including style inheritance, custom media controls, canvas rendering, and security boundaries.
detail: The official Chrome platform developer guide emphasizes critical implementation patterns for Document PiP. Because the auxiliary window initializes with a blank Document, style sheets from the main document do not automatically apply. Developers must explicitly copy style sheets by iterating over document.styleSheets and cloning them into the auxiliary document (or copying <link rel='stylesheet'> and <style> elements). The guide also highlights: (1) handling canvas and WebGL rendering by rendering directly to an OffscreenCanvas or transferring elements; (2) responsive resizing handling via window.onresize within the PiP window; (3) security controls ensuring the PiP window carries the opener origin's lock icon and title bar to prevent spoofing. Super-app store certification requires mini-apps utilizing Document PiP to properly handle style copying, ensure accessibility contrast in floating mode, and gracefully restore all state upon PiP window dismissal.

title: W3C Badging API: OS Launcher & Taskbar Unread Count Governance
description: Defines the W3C Badging API standard specification, enabling web applications and mini-apps to set an application-wide badge on their app icon in the operating system launcher, shelf, taskbar, or dock without dispatching disruptive push notifications.
detail: The Badging API provides a subtle, non-intrusive notification mechanism for installed mini-apps and web applications. Exposed via Navigator and WorkerNavigator in secure contexts, it allows mini-apps to display a numeric badge or unread status dot directly on the application icon. This is essential for messaging, order status, ride updates, and financial alert mini-apps. Unlike system notifications which appear in notification centers and interrupt users, badges update passively. The host super-app container mediates badge updates from mini-apps, aggregating them into the super-app's master app badge or displaying them within the super-app's internal home screen launcher grid. The API prevents notification spam while keeping users informed of pending actions.

title: Navigator.setAppBadge(): Numeric Value Clamping & Formatting Semantics
description: Specifies the setAppBadge() method on Navigator and WorkerNavigator, detailing integer parameter semantics, flag markers, platform truncation, and promise resolution lifecycle.
detail: Navigator.setAppBadge(contents) returns a Promise resolving to void. The 'contents' parameter is an optional positive integer (unsigned long long). If contents is omitted or passed with no arguments, the user agent displays a generic unread indicator (such as a dot or flag). If an integer is supplied, the platform displays the number. If contents is 0, the specification treats it as a call to clear the badge (clearing the indicator). Modern operating systems enforce display limits (e.g., capping display at 99+ or 999+). The method is available both in the window context and inside ServiceWorkerGlobalScope via WorkerNavigator, enabling background push messages to update unread badge counts even when the mini-app UI is not actively open. Super-app store policies require mini-apps to clear or decrement badges immediately when unread items are consumed.

title: Navigator.clearAppBadge(): Badge Reset Semantics & Background Hygiene
description: Details the clearAppBadge() method on Navigator and WorkerNavigator, establishing immediate removal of icon badges upon user engagement or state resolution.
detail: Navigator.clearAppBadge() returns a Promise that resolves when the icon badge has been successfully cleared. Calling clearAppBadge() is semantically identical to invoking setAppBadge(0). It ensures that once a user navigates to an inbox, reviews orders, or clears notifications, stale unread indicators are removed from the OS launcher immediately. In background ServiceWorker push handling, if an incoming message invalidates prior alerts (e.g., order delivered or chat read on another device), the ServiceWorker calls self.navigator.clearAppBadge() to ensure multi-device badge synchronization. Store review guidelines penalize mini-apps that leave orphaned badges after user interaction.

title: Web App Manifest 'share_target' Member: Declarative Ingestion Architecture
description: Specifies the 'share_target' member in the Web App Manifest, allowing mini-apps to register as system-wide share targets capable of receiving shared text, links, and binary files from other apps via native OS share sheets.
detail: The 'share_target' manifest member enables a mini-app to appear in the system share dialog alongside native applications. The member dictionary defines: (1) action: the URL within the mini-app scope that processes the shared data; (2) method: 'GET' (for simple search queries/links) or 'POST' (for binary files and multi-field payloads); (3) enctype: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' (default) or 'multipart/form-data' (required for file sharing); (4) params: a dictionary mapping standard keys ('title', 'text', 'url', 'files') to custom query parameter or form field names. In a super-app ecosystem, the host application intercepts system share intents, validates the target mini-app's manifest declaration, sanitizes incoming MIME types, and routes the payload to the mini-app's registered action URL.

title: Web Share Target File Handling: Service Worker Ingestion & Payload Sandboxing
description: Details the implementation of file ingestion via Web Share Target Level 2, explaining how Service Workers intercept POST requests with FormData, extract binary Blobs, and cache them for UI consumption.
detail: The official Chrome capabilities guide for Web Share Target explains the end-to-end architecture for processing shared multimedia files (images, videos, PDFs). When a user shares a file from the OS or another app to a mini-app registered with method 'POST' and enctype 'multipart/form-data', the browser dispatches a fetch event to the mini-app's Service Worker. The Service Worker intercepts the request, calls event.request.formData() to extract the binary File objects, stores them into CacheStorage or IndexedDB, and redirects the client window to a dedicated preview/composer route. The guide emphasizes rigorous security controls: validating file extension vs MIME type, scanning for malicious payloads before execution, and rejecting unlisted file types. In the super-app store architecture, share targets are sandboxed such that incoming files cannot bypass origin security boundaries.

title: Network Information API: Dynamic Bandwidth & Latency Telemetry for Adaptive Mini-App Runtimes
description: Details the Network Information API interfaces and properties exposed via navigator.connection. Enables super-app runtimes and mini-apps to measure effective connection types, downlink bandwidth, and round-trip latency to dynamically adjust multimedia fidelity and background data prefetching.
detail: The Network Information API specification and MDN documentation define the NetworkInformation interface, accessible via navigator.connection within secure contexts. It exposes real-time telemetry regarding the system's active network interface, including effectiveType ('slow-2g', '2g', '3g', '4g'), downlink (estimated effective bandwidth in megabits per second), rtt (estimated round-trip time in milliseconds), and the change event listener for dynamic network transition monitoring. In a super-app mini-app container, this telemetry enables adaptive loading strategies: video streaming engines switch bitrates, asset loaders defer heavy script bundles or high-resolution textures when rtt spikes or effectiveType drops below '4g', and background synchronization workers throttle non-critical batch uploads. This guarantees responsive UI interactions and avoids packet queue saturation over degraded cellular networks.

title: NetworkInformation.effectiveType: Cellular Quality Bucketing & Asset Degradation Architecture
description: Specifies the effectiveType attribute of the NetworkInformation interface, which maps complex network telemetry metrics (downlink, RTT) into standardized cellular connection buckets for deterministic client-side degradation policies.
detail: According to MDN documentation and WICG specifications, NetworkInformation.effectiveType returns an enumerated string value representing the quality of the network connection categorized as 'slow-2g', '2g', '3g', or '4g'. Unlike physical layer indicators that only reflect hardware radio state (e.g., connected to Wi-Fi with zero actual internet throughput), effectiveType is computed dynamically based on recently observed HTTP request/response round-trip times and transport-layer throughput. For super-app mini-app architectures, this metric serves as the primary gating signal for asset pipeline degradation: on 'slow-2g' or '2g', mini-apps must disable autoplaying animations, bypass non-essential telemetry pings, serve vector skeletons instead of raster images, and enforce aggressive local offline caching via ServiceWorkers.

title: NetworkInformation.saveData: End-User Data-Saving Preference Ingestion & Payload Budgeting
description: Details the saveData boolean attribute of the NetworkInformation interface, reflecting user-configured data-reduction preferences at the OS or browser level to enforce strict bandwidth quotas and payload pruning across mini-apps.
detail: The NetworkInformation.saveData attribute returns a boolean indicating whether the user has enabled a reduced data usage option in the client user agent or operating system settings. The specification mandates that web applications inspect this signal to minimize data transfer. In the context of super-app mini-app store governance, complying with saveData is a key review and quality gate requirement: when saveData is true, mini-apps are required to omit high-resolution background hero images, disable speculative preloading or link prefetching, reduce audio bitrate, and respect client data quotas. The super-app host container also injects the 'Save-Data: on' HTTP header into all subresource requests dispatched through its native networking proxy.

title: Navigator.connection: Centralized Gateway for Mobile Connectivity State Machines
description: Defines the Navigator.connection property binding the NetworkInformation singleton to the global execution context, providing a unified reactive event pipeline for connectivity shifts.
detail: MDN documentation specifies that navigator.connection exposes the NetworkInformation object across window contexts. By attaching an event listener to navigator.connection for 'change' events, mini-apps can reactively respond to radio handoffs (e.g., switching from high-speed fiber Wi-Fi to a roaming cellular connection). The super-app container provides security sandboxing around navigator.connection: while coarse telemetry (effectiveType) is accessible to unprivileged mini-apps, granular downlink and RTT numbers can be rounded or quantized to prevent acoustic side-channel timing attacks or user fingerprinting across cross-origin embedded frames.

title: W3C Device Memory 1: Hardware RAM Quantization & Client-Hints Resource Allocation
description: Specifies the W3C Device Memory specification, establishing standardized client-side JavaScript APIs and HTTP Client Hints to expose quantized device RAM for low-end mobile device optimization.
detail: The W3C Device Memory specification defines the DeviceMemory interface and the 'Device-Memory' HTTP Client Hint header. To prevent fingerprinting, the API restricts reported values to approximate powers of two: 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, and 8 (representing gigabytes of system RAM, clamped between 0.25 GiB and 8 GiB). In super-app mini-app architectures, device memory quantization is fundamental for tiering runtime workloads: on devices reporting 1 GiB or less, the super-app container allocates smaller WebAssembly linear memory heaps, downsizes WebGL framebuffers, enforces strict DOM node count thresholds (e.g., virtualized scrolling lists capped at 50 nodes), and aggressively terminates background idle webview instances to prevent native OS low-memory (OOM) process termination.

title: W3C Device Posture API: Physical Form Factor & Hinge Sensor Orchestration
description: Defines the W3C Device Posture API specification for detecting the physical mechanical state of foldable, dual-screen, and flexible mobile hardware devices.
detail: The W3C Device Posture API standardizes how web runtimes access the physical posture of mobile devices equipped with hinges or flexible screens. The specification introduces the DevicePosture interface, exposing the 'type' attribute which reflects categorical postures such as 'continuous' (flat slab display or external monitor) and 'folded' (device bent along a physical hinge). It also defines integration with CSS media features via '@media (device-posture: folded)'.
