Authors invoke 'child.layoutNextFragment(constraints, breakToken)' to generate 'LayoutFragment' objects representing discrete renderable slices.
The generator returns a 'FragmentResultOptions' dictionary defining 'autoBlockSize', 'inlineSize', 'blockSize', 'childFragments', and custom 'data' attributes.
Supports pagination, column breaks, and virtualization through 'ChildBreakToken' chaining, enabling infinite lists and multi-column feeds without UI stutter.
Prevents circular layout loops by strictly enforcing unidirectional parent-to-child constraint passing.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Adopt 'child.layoutNextFragment()' virtualization models inside super-app infinite scroll feeds to achieve fixed-memory DOM rendering.
Sanitize child fragment positioning coordinates to ensure child elements cannot render outside their allocated container bounding box.

title: Intrinsic Sizes Computation: minContentSize and maxContentSize Calculation via Generator Protocol
category: Houdini Layout Engine, Rendering Pipeline & Container Architecture
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Layout API Level 1, Section 3.3 (Intrinsic Sizes) & Section 5.1 (Determining Intrinsic Sizes)
key_takeaways: Layout classes must implement '*intrinsicSizes(children, edges, styleMap)' to calculate container dimensions under min-content and max-content sizing rules.
Yields 'child.intrinsicSizes()' requests across all layout children to asynchronously aggregate child intrinsic metrics without blocking layout threads.
Enables precise CSS grid and flexbox integration where parent containers size themselves dynamically based on custom layout child contributions.
Reduces redundant layout passes (reflow churn) by caching intrinsic size computations inside engine internal slots.
Handles border, padding, and scrollbar offsets explicitly through the 'LayoutEdges' interface ('inlineStart', 'inlineEnd', 'blockStart', 'blockEnd').
super_app_standard_recommendations: Standardize intrinsic sizing algorithms for complex mini-app components (widgets, cards, dynamic badges) embedded in the super-app host canvas.
Monitor CPU cycle consumption of 'intrinsicSizes' executions in developer diagnostics to catch pathological layout calculations before store release.

title: CSS Layout Worklet Security Boundaries: Side-Channel Defense, Thread Isolation & Memory Quotas
category: Houdini Layout Engine, Rendering Pipeline & Container Architecture
standard_reference: W3C CSS Layout API Level 1 Section 9 & W3C Worklets Level 1 Section 5 (Security Considerations)
key_takeaways: Layout worklets execute in isolated worker-like threads with strict capability restrictions: no synchronous cross-origin data access, no high-resolution clocks, and no local storage access.
Prevents microarchitectural side-channel attacks (e.g. Spectre) by disallowing timing primitives within the layout loop.
User agents enforce execution budgets; runaway layout generator loops exceeding time or recursion thresholds are terminated and fallback to standard block layout.
Disallows dynamic module importation via 'import()' inside the layout execution callback to ensure deterministic and auditable execution profiles.
Protects super-app host container stability: even if a partner mini-app crashes its layout worklet, the host application frame remains fully functional and responsive.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Implement a watchdog timer (50ms threshold) for all mini-app custom layout worklet executions; fallback to CSS flow layout upon timeout.
Prohibit layout worklet script registration from third-party remote CDNs; mandate bundle packaging within the signed mini-app archive (.wgt/.zpk).

title: W3C CSS Animation Worklet API: Off-Main-Thread Compositor Animations & WorkletAnimation Interface
category: Houdini Animation Engine, Compositor Performance & Kinetic UX
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Animation Worklet API, Section 2 (Animation Worklet) & Section 5 (Worklet Animation)
key_takeaways: Defines the Animation Worklet system allowing developers to write procedural animations that execute directly on the browser compositor thread at native display refresh rates (60/120Hz).
Main-thread JavaScript jank and heavy network/DOM operations do not interrupt or drop frames of active WorkletAnimation instances.
Exposes 'new WorkletAnimation(animatorName, effects, timeline, options)' on the main thread to bind animator logic to specific DOM element keyframe effects.
Supports multiple input timelines, including DocumentTimeline and ScrollTimeline, enabling complex scroll-linked and touch-linked animations.
Eliminates the performance overhead of 'requestAnimationFrame' loops that run on the congested main UI thread.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Adopt CSS Animation Worklet for all super-app navigation transitions, drawer gesture tracking, and pull-to-refresh kinetic interactions.
Include WorkletAnimation compliance checks in the mini-app store performance audit pipeline to verify 60fps gesture responsiveness.

title: registerAnimator() Protocol: StatelessAnimator vs StatefulAnimator and animate() Execution Loop
category: Houdini Animation Engine, Compositor Performance & Kinetic UX
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Animation Worklet API, Section 3 (Animator Definition) & Section 4 (Animator Instance)
key_takeaways: Animators are registered using 'registerAnimator(name, animatorCtor)' within 'AnimationWorkletGlobalScope'.
Distinguishes between 'StatelessAnimator' (idempotent, pure function of current time and input options) and 'StatefulAnimator' (maintains an internal state object persisted across frame ticks).
The 'animate(currentTime, effect)' method receives the resolved input timeline timestamp and computes the target 'localTime' for associated KeyframeEffect instances.
Stateful animators implement a 'state()' method that serializes state snapshots, allowing seamless migration between compositor threads and worklet scopes.
Enforces memory-efficient execution by pooling animator instances and recycling scopes across animation lifecycles.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Recommend 'StatelessAnimator' patterns for basic mini-app kinetic micro-interactions to maximize thread migration efficiency.
Require explicit JSON serialization schemas for 'StatefulAnimator' instances to facilitate safe state restoration during mini-app background suspend/resume events.

title: ScrollTimeline & Gesture Synchronization: Zero-Latency Touch-Driven Micro-Interactions
category: Houdini Animation Engine, Compositor Performance & Kinetic UX
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Animation Worklet API, Section 5.1 (Creating a Worklet Animation)
key_takeaways: WorkletAnimation instances accept custom timelines, binding animation progression directly to scroll offsets via ScrollTimeline or ViewTimeline.
Bypasses asynchronous touch event dispatching to JavaScript; physics simulations (springs, friction, inertia) are calculated directly on the compositor thread.
Enables smooth parallax headers, collapsing toolbars, and sticky tab strips that remain perfectly synchronized with user finger scrolling without visual tearing.
Supports non-linear timing curves and multi-phase animations that respond dynamically to gesture velocity.
Eliminates synchronous layout recalculations during scrolling by mutating only compositor-friendly properties (transform, opacity).
super_app_standard_recommendations: Establish standard compositor-driven scroll animation templates for mini-app store landing pages, promotional banners, and product catalogs.
Enforce that mini-app scroll-driven headers use AnimationWorklet or CSS Scroll-driven Animations rather than scroll event listeners.

title: Time Drift Compensation, Frame Budget Allocation & Compositor Overload Defenses
category: Houdini Animation Engine, Compositor Performance & Kinetic UX
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Animation Worklet API, Section 5.4 (Running Animators) & Section 6 (Timing Model)
key_takeaways: The user agent enforces strict frame budget quotas (typically < 4ms per frame) for animator code executing within the compositor frame loop.
If an animator script executes slow or blocking operations, the engine automatically throttles execution frequency or temporarily suspends the WorkletAnimation.
Time drift algorithms synchronize animator 'currentTime' with display VSYNC pulses, compensating for missed frames without jarring positional jumps.
Disallows synchronous IPC calls and long-running loops inside the 'animate()' callback to maintain compositor thread real-time guarantees.
Ensures smooth 120Hz ProMotion/High-Refresh-Rate mobile display support on modern iOS and Android devices.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Integrate animation frame budget monitoring into the super-app runtime, auto-terminating animators that exceed 4ms execution times.
Provide native telemetry reporting back to the mini-app store console when an app exhibits excessive animation jank or dropped compositor frames.

title: Animation Worklet Isolation: Process Boundaries, CSP Inheritance & Side-Channel Mitigation
category: Houdini Animation Engine, Compositor Performance & Kinetic UX
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: CSS Animation Worklet API, Section 8 (Security Considerations)
key_takeaways: AnimationWorkletGlobalScope inherits the Content Security Policy (CSP) of the owner document, restricting script source URLs and module loading.
Executes in an environment without access to document cookies, Web Storage, IndexedDB, or network fetch APIs, preventing data exfiltration via animations.
Restricts high-resolution timing APIs to prevent high-frequency side-channel attacks against host memory layouts.
Isolates multiple WorkletAnimation instances across separate global scopes to prevent cross-component interference in complex multi-tenant super-app canvases.
Protects the host super-app shell from animation hijacking or UI redressing attacks.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Mandate that all animation worklet scripts comply with the strict 'script-src 'self'' CSP directive in mini-app store configurations.
Ensure that mini-app animation worklets cannot observe host application viewport events or touch inputs outside their designated iframe/view boundary.

title: W3C WebXR Hand Input Module Level 1: 25-Joint Skeletal Tracking Model and XRHand/XRJointSpace APIs
category: Spatial Computing, Extended Reality (XR) & Biometric Peripherals
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: WebXR Hand Input Module - Level 1, Section 3 (Physical Hand Input Sources) & Section 3.2 (Skeleton Joints)
key_takeaways: Defines the 'XRHand' interface representing articulated human hand tracking, exposing an ordered skeleton of 25 distinct anatomical joints.
Joints include wrist, thumb (metacarpal, phalanx-proximal, phalanx-distal, tip), and four fingers (metacarpal, phalanx-proximal, phalanx-intermediate, phalanx-distal, tip).
Each joint is accessed as an 'XRJointSpace', enabling applications to query 3D position, orientation, and joint radius relative to reference spaces via 'XRFrame.getJointPose()'.
Enables controller-free, natural hand interactions (pinch-to-select, grab, poke, direct virtual UI touch) in spatial computing mini-apps.
Joint radius data allows realistic physical collision detection between user fingertips and virtual UI elements (buttons, sliders, 3D product models).
super_app_standard_recommendations: Support 'hand-tracking' feature requests in the super-app WebXR permission pipeline for spatial commerce and virtual showroom mini-apps.
Provide standard virtual UI interaction libraries (pinch, direct tap) within the super-app SDK to standardize hand gestures across mini-apps.

title: Biometric Privacy & Fingerprinting Defenses: Skeletal Geometry Redaction and Explicit User Consent
category: Spatial Computing, Extended Reality (XR) & Biometric Peripherals
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: WebXR Hand Input Module - Level 1, Section 5 (Privacy & Security Considerations)
key_takeaways: Hand skeletal dimensions (bone lengths, joint spacing, hand geometry) constitute unique biometric identifiers capable of cross-session user fingerprinting and identification.
W3C mandates explicit user consent before granting mini-apps access to 'hand-tracking' session features.
Recommends that user agents normalize bone lengths to synthetic demographic averages or introduce subtle noise to prevent precise biometric profile generation.
Access to joint tracking data MUST be gated: when the mini-app loses focus or runs in the background, joint poses return null or zeroed buffers.
Prevents passive tracking of user physical characteristics (hand tremors, medical indicators, fatigue) by untrusted third-party developers.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Classify 'hand-tracking' as a Sensitive Biometric Capability in the mini-app store permissions matrix, requiring upfront disclosure in store listings.
Implement biometric normalization in the super-app host container, sanitizing absolute skeletal dimensions before forwarding joint data to mini-apps.

title: W3C WebXR Layers API Level 1: XRCompositionLayer, XRProjectionLayer & Direct GPU Hardware Compositing
category: Spatial Computing, Extended Reality (XR) & Biometric Peripherals
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: WebXR Layers API Level 1, Section 3 (Layer Types) & Section 6 (GPU Layer and View Creation)
key_takeaways: WebXR Layers API introduces 'XRCompositionLayer' and 'XRProjectionLayer', enabling WebGL textures to be fed directly into platform VR/AR hardware compositors.
Bypasses intermediate texture copy and re-sampling steps, drastically reducing memory bandwidth, latency, and thermal throttling on standalone XR headsets and mobile AR devices.
Supports specialized layer geometries: XRQuadLayer (flat 2D UI panels, text dialogs), XRCylinderLayer (curved panoramic menus), and XREquirectLayer (360-degree video backgrounds).
Preserves sub-pixel text rendering quality and UI crispness by allowing the system compositor to sample UI textures at native display resolution with reprojection.
Provides 'XRSubImage' and 'XRWebGLSubImage' interfaces for managing stereo texture viewports (left-right, top-bottom, texture-array) efficiently.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Leverage XRQuadLayer for rendering super-app mini-app 2D interfaces within 3D spatial environments (Vision Pro, Meta Quest, Android XR).
Mandate XRProjectionLayer usage for mini-app 3D graphics rendering to maintain battery life and avoid frame stutter in mobile AR shopping modes.

title: XRMediaBinding & Hardware Video Acceleration: DRM Protected Content & 360 Cinema Projection
category: Spatial Computing, Extended Reality (XR) & Biometric Peripherals
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: WebXR Layers API Level 1, Section 7 (Video Layer Creation) & Section 7.5 (XRMediaBinding)
key_takeaways: Introduces 'XRMediaBinding', allowing HTMLMediaElement (HTMLVideoElement) video streams to be mapped directly into hardware compositor layers (XRMediaQuadLayer, XRMediaCylinderLayer).
Video decoding feeds directly into the display hardware without passing raw video frames through JavaScript or WebGL texture upload paths.
Supports Hardware DRM and Protected Media Paths (Encrypted Media Extensions / EME) inside immersive spatial environments, enabling premium streaming mini-apps.
Significantly reduces power consumption during spatial media playback, extending device battery life for virtual cinema and live concert experiences.
Ensures color accuracy and HDR metadata preservation by relying on the OS compositor video pipeline.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Provide 'XRMediaBinding' abstractions in the super-app streaming SDK for entertainment, ticketing, and live event mini-apps.
Enforce DRM compliance verification during mini-app store review for apps claiming spatial video streaming capabilities.

title: WebXR Layer Depth Sorting, Asynchronous Space Warp & Multi-App Occlusion Governance
category: Spatial Computing, Extended Reality (XR) & Biometric Peripherals
standard_reference: W3C Working Draft: WebXR Layers API Level 1, Section 9 (Depth Sorting Between Layers) & Section 10 (Space Warp)
key_takeaways: Enables precise depth buffer sharing and hardware depth sorting across multiple WebXR composition layers and system UI overlays.
Supports Motion Vector / Space Warp data submission, allowing headset compositors to extrapolate missing frames during GPU stalls and eliminate motion sickness.
Spatial Sandboxing: The super-app host container can interleave its own system layers (safety boundaries, notification badges, payment prompts) securely with mini-app content.
Guarantees that untrusted mini-apps cannot occlude system security dialogs, emergency boundaries, or biometric payment authorization windows.
Strictly restricts stereoscopic rendering parameters to prevent malicious manipulation of visual depth that could induce user disorientation.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Configure system security prompts to render in a dedicated, top-level hardware overlay layer that cannot be masked or occluded by mini-app layers.
Establish depth buffer validation standards to prevent visual glitches and ensure smooth reprojection when switching between spatial mini-apps.

title: Solid Protocol Specification: Personal Data Pods, Resource Server Architecture & Linked Data Platform (LDP) Interaction
category: Decentralized Personal Data Architecture & Privacy Governance
standard_reference: Solid Community Group / W3C Technical Report: The Solid Protocol, Section 2 & 5
key_takeaways: Decouples data storage from application logic by encapsulating user data into autonomous, interoperable Personal Online Datastores (Pods).
Built upon W3C Linked Data Platform (LDP) 1.0, leveraging RDF graph representations (Turtle, JSON-LD) and standard HTTP verbs (GET, PUT, POST, PATCH via SPARQL Update).
Enforces universal Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) for all resources, containers, and identity profiles, enabling cross-pod federated querying.
Eliminates vendor data silos by empowering users to store social profiles, transactional records, and health data in user-controlled storage nodes.
Defines strict server requirements for handling conditional HTTP requests (ETag, If-Match) to guarantee concurrency control in multi-client environments.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Architect the super-app user storage layer as an internal or federated Solid Pod, allowing mini-apps to request scoped data access rather than duplicating user records in siloed proprietary databases.
Standardize mini-app persistent user profiles using LDP-compliant resource containers with SPARQL/JSON-LD read-write interfaces.

title: Solid-OIDC Authentication: WebID URI Identity Anchoring, ID Token Extensions & DPoP Cryptographic Proof of Possession
standard_reference: Solid Community Group Specification: Solid-OIDC 0.1.0, Section 3-6
key_takeaways: Extends OpenID Connect 1.0 by substituting arbitrary opaque identifiers with a global WebID HTTP(S) URI inside the 'webid' claim.
Requires Demonstration of Proof-of-Possession (DPoP) at the HTTP layer, binding ID Tokens and Access Tokens to ephemeral client asymmetric keys (RFC 9449).
Eliminates bearer token theft and replay attacks across heterogeneous resource servers and third-party storage pods.
Defines WebID profile document discovery, where the WebID URI resolves to an RDF graph publishing the user's public signing keys and authorized OpenID Providers (OPs).
Mandates client registration via Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) or dereferenceable Client ID Document URIs, establishing verifiable client metadata.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Implement Solid-OIDC identity federation inside the super-app container, issuing DPoP-bound tokens to mini-apps for authenticating against host backend services.
Assign each registered mini-app a verifiable Client ID Document URI published on the store portal to eliminate shared secrets and static API keys.

title: Solid Web Access Control (WAC) & Access Control Policy (ACP): Decentralized Resource-Level Authorization Matrices
category: Decentralized Access Control, Policy Governance & Permission Sandboxing
standard_reference: Solid Community Group: Web Access Control (WAC) & Access Control Policy (ACP)
key_takeaways: WAC specifies access control lists (ACLs) as RDF resources (.acl) governing individual documents and container directory hierarchies.
Defines core permission modes: acl:Read, acl:Write, acl:Append (append-only write without read/update/delete), and acl:Control (administrative policy management).
Enforces acl:origin restrictions, preventing cross-origin web applications from accessing pod resources even if executed within an authenticated browser session.
Access Control Policy (ACP) provides a modular, fine-grained alternative separating Matchers (agents, client IDs, issuer scopes) from Access Policies.
Supports default inheritance rules ('acl:default') allowing recursive directory-tree permission propagation across complex nested data pods.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Adopt the acl:Append mode for untrusted mini-app telemetry and audit logging pods, preventing malicious mini-apps from reading, modifying, or truncating existing security logs.
Enforce strict client-origin and WebID validation on the host container's storage bridge according to WAC origin sandboxing rules.

title: Solid Application Interoperability & Shape Trees: Schema Validation, Type Registries & Cross-App Collaboration
category: Semantic Data Governance, Schema Validation & Interoperability
standard_reference: Solid Project / W3C Ecosystem Specifications: Solid Application Interoperability
key_takeaways: Standardizes Data Grants and Access Grants, allowing users to grant mini-apps access to specific data types (e.g., Contacts, Notes, Fitness) rather than raw directories.
Leverages Shape Trees and W3C SHACL/ShEx to enforce strict structural schemas on RDF graph resources before persistence.
Introduces Type Registries (Public and Private Type Indexes) enabling discovery of which Pod container holds instances of a specific RDF Class.
Eliminates schema chaos by ensuring all collaborating applications share deterministic, validated schema definitions.
Enables multiple independent mini-apps to seamlessly read and write the same underlying data entity without database migration or synchronization pipelines.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Establish a centralized Type Registry and SHACL schema library in the mini-app store console for shared enterprise domains (e.g., invoices, loyalty cards, medical appointments).
Require third-party mini-apps requesting user profile access to bind their requests to registered Shape Trees, rejecting unvalidated unstructured writes.

title: Solid Notifications Protocol: WebSockets, Server-Sent Events (SSE) & Linked Data Notifications (LDN)
category: Real-Time Event Architecture & Push Notification Governance
standard_reference: Solid Community Group: Solid Notifications Protocol 0.2.0
key_takeaways: Specifies standard subscription channels (WebSocketChannel2023, EventSourceChannel2023, WebHookChannel2023) for real-time resource state change delivery.
Discovery is achieved via HTTP Link headers ('rel="http://www.w3.org/ns/solid/terms#storageDescription"' and notification subscription endpoints).
Ensures notification payloads respect access control rules, sending lightweight state mutation alerts without leaking unauthorized resource data.
Eliminates aggressive HTTP polling across distributed personal data pods, reducing cellular network traffic and battery consumption.
Integrates with W3C Linked Data Notifications (LDN) for inbox-based decentralized inter-app messaging and workflow triggering.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Provide a native host event subscription API mirroring Solid Notifications WebSocketChannel, multiplexing resource mutation events across mini-app instances over a single persistent host connection.
Enforce security authorization checks on all outgoing notification broadcasts to ensure mini-apps only receive alerts for data resources they possess explicit acl:Read grants for.

title: W3C Vehicle Information Service Specification (VISS v2) Core: Vehicle Signal Specification (VSS) Tree & Data Model
category: Connected Vehicle Architecture, Automotive In-Cabin Sandboxing & IoT Governance
standard_reference: W3C Candidate Recommendation: Vehicle Information Service Specification (VISS v2) Core, Section 4-5
key_takeaways: Defines a standardized JSON-based protocol enabling client applications (in-cabin IVI mini-apps, fleet management) to query and control vehicle telemetry signals.

Binds directly to COVESA / W3C Vehicle Signal Specification (VSS) taxonomy, organizing signals into an unambiguous hierarchical tree (e.g., Vehicle.Speed, Vehicle.Powertrain.TractionBattery.StateOfCharge).
Abstracts heterogeneous underlying CAN, LIN, and Ethernet vehicle bus protocols into normalized web data types and semantic paths.
Supports CRUD operations: 'get' for current state readings, 'set' for vehicle actuator control, 'subscribe' for continuous change streams, and 'unsubscribe'.
Specifies strict metadata retrieval operations ('get' with metadata filter) returning signal data types, min/max boundaries, units, and read/write capabilities.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Adopt VISS v2 core data model as the standard bridge interface when deploying super-app mini-apps onto automotive smart cockpits and in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) systems.
Enforce strict VSS tree path validation in the mini-app permission manifest (e.g., 'vehicle:signals:Vehicle.Speed:read'), blocking unauthorized access to vehicle bus telemetry.

title: VISS v2 Transport Bindings: WebSocket Full-Duplex, MQTT Broker Integration & HTTP/REST Microservices
category: Automotive Transport Protocols, High-Frequency Telemetry & Stream Ingestion
standard_reference: W3C Candidate Recommendation: Vehicle Information Service Specification (VISS v2) Transport, Section 3-6
key_takeaways: Specifies protocol bindings across WebSocket (RFC 6455), HTTP/REST, and MQTT, catering to diverse network latencies and vehicle hardware constraints.
WebSocket transport provides persistent bidirectional framing with correlation request IDs ('requestId'), minimizing serialization overhead for high-frequency telematics.
MQTT binding aligns with edge gateway architectures, enabling vehicles to stream telematics to cloud brokers and receive remote mini-app commands asynchronously.
Standardizes subscription filters (time-based interval sampling, minimum change delta thresholds) to prevent bandwidth saturation over cellular connections.
Enforces message framing schemas that require explicit timestamping ('ts' in ISO 8601 UTC) and client request routing metadata.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Provide native WebSocket-based VISS v2 client adapters inside the automotive super-app runtime, preventing individual mini-apps from opening raw socket connections.
Apply client-side subscription rate-limiting and delta filtering in the host container to protect in-vehicle compute and cellular data plans from runaway telemetry polling.

title: VISS v2 Security Architecture: Access Token Verification, Scoped Proof-of-Possession & Automotive Safety Gating
category: Automotive Cybersecurity, Token Verification & Safety Guardrails
standard_reference: W3C Candidate Recommendation: VISS v2 Core, Section 6 (Security and Access Control)
key_takeaways: Mandates that all non-public vehicle signals require cryptographically signed Access Tokens (JSON Web Tokens / RFC 7519) in the 'authorization' payload field.
Differentiates read-only telematics (speed, odometer, ambient temperature) from safety-critical actuation (door locks, window control, HVAC, acceleration limiter).
Integrates with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization servers, mapping token scopes directly to VSS signal paths and permitted operations (e.g., 'Vehicle.Cabin.Door.Row1.Left.IsOpen:set').
Enforces strict ASIL (Automotive Safety Integrity Level) isolation: the VISS server must reject write operations that could jeopardize functional vehicle safety while the car is in motion.
Provides standardized error codes ('401 Unauthorized', '403 Forbidden', '404 Invalid Path', '400 Bad Request') for predictable client exception handling.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Implement a mandatory security gateway in the automotive super-app host that intercepts all mini-app vehicle API requests, verifying token scopes against safety policies before forwarding to the vehicle CAN/LIN bus.
Prohibit third-party mini-apps from acquiring actuation ('set') scopes unless certified under an enterprise automotive security compliance review program.

title: VISS v2 Historical Telemetry, Curve Logging & Offline Vehicle Data Buffering
category: Automotive Telematics, Edge Storage & Offline Synchronization
standard_reference: W3C Candidate Recommendation: VISS v2 Core, Section 5.4 (History and Curve Logging)
key_takeaways: Provides standardized interfaces for querying historical vehicle sensor time-series data using temporal bounds ('from', 'to') and resolution parameters.
Introduces curve-logging algorithms allowing in-vehicle brokers to buffer and downsample high-frequency telemetry during cellular coverage dead zones.
Guarantees message ordering and monotonic timestamp integrity when flushing buffered historical telematics upon reconnection.
Defines data compression policies and chunked payload streaming to prevent memory exhaustion on resource-constrained IVI head units.
Enables smart fleet and insurance mini-apps (usage-based insurance, driver behavior scoring) to operate reliably without continuous online connectivity.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Require automotive and telematics mini-apps to utilize host-managed historical telemetry buffers rather than spinning custom background polling loops.
Establish strict storage quotas (e.g., max 50 MB per mini-app) for local offline vehicle telemetry caches in the super-app runtime.

title: Automotive Data Privacy: Location Fuzzing, Personal Identifier Redaction & Driver Consent Management
standard_reference: W3C VISS v2 Security and Privacy Considerations & ISO 21434 Alignment
key_takeaways: Identifies vehicle location (Vehicle.CurrentLocation.Latitude/Longitude) and driver behavior telemetry as highly sensitive personal data subject to GDPR and UNECE WP.29 regulations.
Specifies privacy protection mechanisms including dynamic coordinate truncation/fuzzing when full precision is not strictly required by the mini-app use case.
Requires automated redaction of Vehicle Identification Numbers (VIN) and owner profile identifiers when exporting telemetry to untrusted third-party analytics services.
Mandates transparent driver consent notifications displayed on the central in-cabin touchscreen whenever a mini-app requests live vehicle sensor streaming.
Provides an instant emergency privacy mute switch ('incognito mode') disabling all external vehicle data streaming with zero latency.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Incorporate a persistent visual privacy indicator on the super-app top navigation bar whenever an active mini-app is reading live vehicle telemetry.
Provide user-configurable privacy controls in the super-app settings allowing drivers to toggle coarse vs precise location reporting for each installed mini-app.

title: FIDO Metadata Service (MDS 3.0): Cryptographic Authenticator Attestation Verification & Root Trust Anchors
category: Cryptographic Hardware Attestation, Passkey Security & Root Trust Federation
standard_reference: FIDO Alliance Proposed Standard 2021: FIDO Metadata Service (MDS) v3.0, Section 3-4
key_takeaways: Defines the global distribution mechanism for FIDO Authenticator metadata statements via cryptographically signed JWT BLOBs (MDS3 BLOB).
Signed by the FIDO Alliance MDS root certificate using RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 or ECDSA, guaranteeing authenticity and freshness through strict 'nextUpdate' timestamps.
Contains comprehensive payload entries for all certified authenticators, indexed by AAGUID (FIDO2) or AAID (UAF) or Attestation Certificate Key Identifier.
Allows relying parties (super-app identity gateways) to verify hardware authenticity, biometric modality, key protection types, and certification levels (FIDO Level 1 to 3+).
Includes real-time status reports ('statusReports') tracking compromised authenticator batches, revoked attestation keys, and security advisories.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Integrate an automated MDS 3.0 BLOB synchronization worker into the super-app identity server to validate passkey authenticators during biometric registration.
Establish a strict policy rejecting authenticators flagged with 'USER_VERIFICATION_BYPASS' or 'ATTESTATION_KEY_COMPROMISE' in MDS3 status reports for high-value financial mini-apps.

title: FIDO Metadata Statement v3.0: Hardware Security Certification, Cryptographic Algorithms & Biometric Quality Metrics
category: Hardware Security Evaluation, Biometric Governance & Cryptographic Policy
standard_reference: FIDO Alliance Proposed Standard: FIDO Metadata Statement v3.0, Section 3
key_takeaways: Defines the JSON schema for describing authenticator characteristics: supported public key algorithms (COSE algorithm numbers: ES256, EdDSA, RS256), user verification details, and attestation certificate chains.
Exposes keyProtection flags ('KEY_PROTECTION_TEE', 'KEY_PROTECTION_SECURE_ELEMENT', 'KEY_PROTECTION_REMOTE_HANDLE') distinguishing software keystores from tamper-resistant hardware chips.
Documents userVerificationDetails including biometric sensor type (fingerprint, iris, facial recognition), False Acceptance Rate (FAR), and False Rejection Rate (FRR).
Lists attachmentHint flags ('ATTACHMENT_HINT_INTERNAL' for platform passkeys vs 'ATTACHMENT_HINT_EXTERNAL' for roaming security keys like YubiKeys).
Provides root attestation certificate chains enabling relying parties to cryptographically validate the leaf attestation cert received in WebAuthn registration responses.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Mandate that enterprise banking and investment mini-apps enforce 'KEY_PROTECTION_SECURE_ELEMENT' or 'KEY_PROTECTION_TEE' via FIDO metadata statements before authorizing fund transfers.
Expose authenticator certification levels in the mini-app developer console to enable developers to configure risk-based authentication workflows.

title: IETF RFC 9535: JSONPath Query Expressions Syntax, Root Identifier ($) & Selector Evaluation Model
category: Data Transformation, Query Languages & Schema Sandboxing
standard_reference: IETF RFC 9535 (Proposed Standard, February 2024): JSONPath: Query Expressions for JSON, Section 1-3
key_takeaways: Standardizes the formal syntax and semantics of JSONPath query expressions, ending decades of vendor-specific dialect fragmentation and parser vulnerabilities.
Defines root identifier '$' referencing the entire input JSON value, child segments ('.name' or "['name']"), and recursive descent selectors ('..').
Formalizes wildcard selectors ('*') matching all elements of an array or object, and index selectors enabling precise integer subscripting.
Establishes a deterministic evaluation model that transforms an input JSON value and a query expression into a well-defined nodelist result.
Specifies strict UTF-8 string encoding rules, Unicode escape handling, and literal parsing semantics to prevent cross-platform query injection attacks.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Standardize on RFC 9535 compliant JSONPath engines across super-app backend gateways and client SDKs for declarative data extraction from mini-app payloads.
Prohibit proprietary JSONPath dialect extensions in the mini-app manifest to guarantee deterministic cross-platform query evaluation across iOS, Android, and Web.

title: RFC 9535 Filter Selectors (?<logical-expr>), Array Slices & Standard Function Extensions (length, count, match, search)
category: Expression Evaluation, Query Security & Safe Compute Sandboxing
standard_reference: IETF RFC 9535: JSONPath: Query Expressions for JSON, Section 2.3 & 2.4
key_takeaways: Specifies filter selectors '?<logical-expr>' evaluating boolean conditions against array elements or object properties using current node identifier '@'.
Supports comparison operators ('==', '!=', '<', '<=', '>', '>=') with well-defined type coercion and absence semantics, preventing subtle type confusion bugs.
Standardizes array slice selectors '[start:end:step]' following Python-style indexing semantics with negative offset wrapping.
Defines built-in function extensions: 'length()' for string/array/object sizes, 'count()' for nodelist cardinality, 'match()' for full regex matching, and 'search()' for substring regex scanning.
Strictly restricts regular expression syntax to standard RFC 9485 I-Regexp, eliminating catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS) vulnerabilities by disallowing lookaheads and backreferences.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Use RFC 9535 filter expressions for declarative permission scopes in mini-app API gateways (e.g., filtering sensitive fields before passing database responses to untrusted mini-apps).
Enforce I-Regexp compliance on all regex patterns in mini-app JSONPath filter queries to protect super-app host threads from ReDoS denial-of-service exploits.

title: JSONPath Security Considerations: ReDoS Mitigation, Recursive Descent Depth Limits & Input Size Caps
category: Query Engine Security, Resource Sandboxing & Denial-of-Service Defense
standard_reference: IETF RFC 9535: JSONPath Security Considerations, Section 4
key_takeaways: Identifies primary attack vectors against JSONPath processors: algorithmic complexity attacks via deeply nested structures, unbounded recursive descent ('..'), and memory exhaustion from broad wildcard nodelists.
Mandates implementation-defined caps on JSON nesting depth (recommended max 64 levels) and query expression syntax tree depth.
Recommends capping the maximum number of nodes in evaluated nodelists to prevent memory allocation denial-of-service during batch query processing.
Warns against evaluating untrusted JSONPath expressions directly on server-side nodes without AST validation, preventing prototype pollution or unintended property leaks.
Specifies that JSONPath evaluation must remain strictly side-effect free, with zero capability for modifying input JSON trees or executing arbitrary host functions.
super_app_standard_recommendations: Incorporate strict JSONPath query limits (max expression length 512 bytes, max AST depth 16, nodelist cap 1,000 items) in the super-app bridge query proxy.
Implement a static JSONPath linter in the mini-app store validation pipeline to detect inefficient recursive descent patterns ('$..*') before app publication.
